summary: very brief observation by a motorist of a red dot moving on a slight curve in the very clear morning sky: probable observation of the sun's reflection on a high-altitude aircraft.
description: On December 30, 2015, at 7:50 a.m., a driver in a roundabout observed a large, bright red dot for 30 seconds, descending very slowly from the clear sky along a very gentle curve. The witness pulled over but didn't have time to take out their phone to photograph the phenomenon before it disappeared. No other reports were collected. The witness was driving northwest, shortly before sunrise in the southeast. A red dot observed in the opposite direction to the sun, still slightly below the horizon, could be the reflection of the sun on a high-altitude flying object, such as an airplane. A check on Flightradar indicated an airplane nearly 100 km from the witness in this northwest direction; the airplane was descending slowly. The very good atmospheric visibility, due to the light northerly wind that was blowing that day, made this observation possible. See the weather report for Nemes on Météociel. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of sunlight reflecting off a high-altitude aircraft. Given that the witness was moving, the direction of observation is not precise enough to definitively attribute the phenomenon to this specific aircraft. This remains a hypothesis, consistent with the observation report.

summary: Observation of an object shaped like an upside-down soup plate, fluorescent orange in color, moving silently across the night sky: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On December 27, 2015, between 5:05 and 5:15 PM, a motorist was astonished to see a fluorescent orange object in the sky, shaped like an upside-down soup plate. The object, which appeared stationary, was surrounded by an orange halo. It moved southwest, and no sound was heard during its movement. It disappeared over the horizon. Several motorists stopped at the roadside also reportedly observed the phenomenon. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of an orange ball in the sky for a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, likely released from Saint-Vallier after a private party during the holiday season. The observed movement was slight, heading southwest. The wind recorded at the Auribeau-sur-Siagne weather station, 12 km away, was calm (see the Infoclimat report for the day of observation). At this time of day, in mountainous areas, at sunset, there are very localized winds, depending on the valleys, very light and difficult to predict. This weather report does not provide conclusive information to confirm the Thai lantern hypothesis. The lack of a result in the photo is not surprising: mobile phone cameras are very poor in low light. Nevertheless, despite the lack of evidence to confirm this hypothesis, given the description of the phenomenon and its high frequency Regarding lantern releases during the end-of-year period, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two white circular shapes in the clear sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 27, 2015, at 6:35 PM, a witness saw two circular shapes appear in the sky, flying slightly offset from one another. Their trajectory was south-north (or northeast). The witness noticed a detail on the second shape: a bright red point that went out after two seconds. The entire observation lasted less than 10 seconds. No other reports were collected. The observation of several "white circular shapes flying side by side" strongly suggests Thai lanterns. The movement was observed from south to north, which is consistent with the wind direction recorded in Lille and Cambrai (within 10 km) (see attached weather report). The angular displacement appears rapid (50th in 10 sec) but consistent with the recorded wind speeds (20 km/h), given a possible error or uncertainty of a factor of 2 on the actual wind speed on site, on the altitude of the lantern (50 or 100m) or on the duration of observation (10 or 20 seconds). GEIPAN classifies this case "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of the presence of orange luminous points in the night sky then rapid disappearance: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, December 26, 2015, at 8:30 p.m., a witness, while gathering firewood behind his house, was intrigued by the silent presence of a fixed orange light. Suddenly, this light moved at high speed southward and disappeared behind a hill. Going back out to collect more firewood, the witness observed up to four lights, each disappearing in turn. The observation, reported by the witness with the assistance of his wife and adult daughter, was accompanied by photographs, one of which showed no movement during the 1/4-second exposure. This photograph exhibits all the characteristics of a Thai lantern sighting: an orange light, no flashes, no noise, hovering, then disappearing (during a rapid movement) corresponding to the end of the candle. We can also consider the date, a Saturday evening, the day after Christmas, a time conducive to a gathering of family or friends celebrating Christmas. A further element of analysis: the weather situation given by the Météociel report for Mende (located 25 km to the east) at 8 PM indicates overcast skies, no precipitation, visibility 20 km, and a southeast wind less than 10 km/h. The possibility of a lantern is supported by: - the overcast skies: no visible stars, cloud floor estimated by the witness at 1,500 meters: it was not a commercial airliner, a satellite, or the International Space Station (ISS). - A light southeasterly wind, blowing in the direction of the points of light, explains the apparent immobility of a floating object pushed by the wind. In the first observation, the sudden and rapid flight, leading to its disappearance, corresponds to the end of the candle's combustion, causing the object to fall and go out. The southward movement interpreted by the witness is a misinterpretation; it corresponds to the sudden fall associated with the decrease in brightness due to the candle going out. As for the second observation of a point splitting into three points and then remaining separate, this corresponds to a new release of lanterns, three of them separating with the wind, combined with a parallax effect relative to the observer. The results of this investigation strongly suggest the observation of Thai lanterns, released on a Saturday evening during the Christmas holidays. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a luminous object with changing colors in the sky: probable observation of a festive LED balloon.
description: On December 24, 2015, at 6:10 PM, three people observed a luminous object with changing colors (green, blue, orange) silently passing by from a 10th-floor apartment for 45 seconds. The object disappeared behind the building, passing over the witnesses. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of a multicolored object flying at low altitude on a festive evening suggests a "lighter-than-air" object carried by the wind. The Orly airport weather station's Météociel report indicates a southwest wind, consistent with the object's movement (see the Météociel report). The multiple, changing colors suggest an LED light-up balloon similar to those described here. This type of festive balloon is becoming increasingly common. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable observation of an LED light-up balloon.

summary: Observation of the silent movement in the night sky of a bright red dot surrounded by a red halo on a straight trajectory: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On December 24, 2015, at 11:48 PM, a witness observed a bright red dot, surrounded by a red halo, moving silently in the sky along a straight path beneath the cloud cover. The witness took two photos. As the object flew overhead, the witness estimated its approximate size to be that of a car. The phenomenon disappeared behind the trees after traversing the sky for two minutes. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of an orange ball crossing the sky in a few minutes on a festive night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, likely licked nearby for Christmas. The movement is observed from the Southwest to the Northeast, which is consistent with the Southwest wind recorded in Asnieres-sur-Oise (Weather reports: light Southwest wind consistent with the movement: Weather in Asnieres-sur-Oise) and the sustained Southwest wind recorded in Creil, consistent with the movement: Météociel: wind in Creil). A sustained Southeast wind was recorded in Roissy, not consistent with the movement: Météociel Roissy. The photographs support this hypothesis: characteristic "fire" color. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of a Thai lantern. The witness, informed of this Thai lantern hypothesis, does not accept it. However, the observation report is entirely consistent with the observation of a Thai lantern: a horizontal and rectilinear movement of a luminous point with a red or orange halo, in the same direction as the local wind, on a festive evening. As always in this type of case, the distance and speed of the phenomenon are overestimated by the witness due to the inherent low luminosity of the lanterns, compared to the lights of the aircraft.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange glow in the night sky on a festive evening: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On December 24, 2015, at approximately 7:40 PM, a witness in their garden observed a very bright orange glow, silently crossing the clear sky from east to west. The glow shrank and disappeared. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness's description led the investigation to the observation of a lantern, which had all the characteristics of such a phenomenon: an orange glow, moving silently, propelled by the wind, and then disappearing as it went out. We will confirm this hypothesis: First, the witness's report contains a contradiction. They initially stated that the phenomenon "crossed the sky from due east to due west." Then, in the detailed description of the phenomenon, they indicated a "west-to-east" trajectory. To resolve the ambiguity, we will consider the phenomenon's position relative to the moon, which they described as "to the right and below the moon." The ephemeris of the lunar calendar (lunar calendar) indicates a phase one day before the full moon, with moonrise at 3:39 PM (UTC) on December 24, 2015. The moon is positioned in the east (having risen 3 hours prior), to the left of the observer looking south. The position of the phenomenon to the right of the moon (to the west when looking south) leads to a west-east trajectory, which corroborates its detailed description. The weather at the Belfort-Dorans station, less than 10 km to the south, as recorded on Météociel, indicates "clear skies, visibility to 20 km" with a "west wind gusting to 10-20 km/h". A floating object is therefore being pushed from west to east, which corresponds to the phenomenon's trajectory. The witness describes an orange glow, about a quarter to a third the size of the full moon, which then diminished to a point of light before disappearing. It's worth noting that this was Christmas Eve, a night conducive to this type of festive event. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a red light in the sky. Passage through the clouds then observation of the descent of a black object which then blends into the mountain: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On December 24, 2015, at 5:50 PM, two people out for a walk observed the silent movement of an intense red light in the slightly cloudy sky for eight minutes. This light followed an upward trajectory and took on a more orange hue before disappearing into the clouds. Intrigued, the witnesses moved on and then saw a black shape detach itself from the clouds and silently follow, first in a straight line and then downward. Unfortunately, they lost sight of the shape, whose dark color then blended with that of the mountain. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness conducted extensive research to try to find other accounts and an explanation for what she saw. Based solely on the color, shape, and brightness, the witness's description is already typical of a Thae lantern sighting. Other elements that support this hypothesis are the "festive" date (December 24) and, even more so, the final phase of the trajectory and observation. Indeed, an object is described as becoming dark and beginning to descend as if to land. This is precisely what happens at the end of a lantern's burn, although the lantern remains visible as a gray or black shape (not always round; here the witness refers to it as a honeycomb) when the night is not too dark (the witness indicates that the moon provided a chiaroscuro effect). The witness reports an absence of wind. However, ground wind is often not felt by witnesses, while there is often wind at altitudes of 100 or 200 meters. A light wind of 6 km/h can already cause a movement of 1 km in 10 minutes, resulting in a large angular excursion in the sky for a lantern flying at an altitude of 100 meters. Unfortunately, it is not possible to correlate the trajectory with the wind, as no local weather records are available. The absence of noise from an unknown object adds to the strangeness of the observation but remains entirely explainable for an object carried by the wind. The witness believes it to be a large object (twice the size of a glider). This estimate is explained by the fact that when an object is unrecognizable and its distance is unknown, it is very difficult for any witness to judge its size. Many details provided by the witness support the hypothesis of observing a Thai lantern released during a private celebration. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the observation as B: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of an orange luminous phenomenon in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 19, 2015, at 8:17 PM, a witness, alerted by his son, observed a large, slightly ovoid sphere shimmering a very bright orange from a distance. This sphere moved across the sky toward the witness. The witness then distinguished a widened "V" shape with small, regularly spaced lights and took three photographs. The object passed directly overhead without any sound being heard. The trajectory was straight, then took on a slight upward slope as it moved away; the UFO lost brightness and eventually disappeared. The witness's son saw three distinct phenomena. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of orange spheres crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party in the lead-up to the holiday season. The movement was observed from the Southwest, which is consistent with the Southwest wind recorded in Salon-de-Provence: the Infoclimat report indicates a wind from the 110th direction at 6 to 11 km/h. The only usable photo taken by the witness is out of focus (focus blur, very common in night photos under these conditions) and shows only a blurry orange circle. However, it proves the reality of the phenomenon, and the color of the object is entirely consistent with that of the Thae lanterns. The distance estimate made by the witness based on his aeronautical experience cannot be accurate since he has never seen this type of object. Because Thae lanterns are inherently dim (large candle flame), they are always perceived as much farther away than they actually are, and therefore appear much larger and faster than they really are. See Estimating the Size and Distance of an Unknown Phenomenon. The very regular movement of objects in the sky is quite normal for an object carried by a light wind. As the lanterns are often licked one after the other, after the same delay corresponding to the time it takes to light the torch, the result is an organized line of flying lights. Due to their inherently low brightness, Thae lanterns, intuitively compared to airplane lights, are most often interpreted by witnesses as being much farther away than they actually are, and therefore much faster. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of a bright point in the sky in foggy weather; impression of "pitching" of the UFO: probable astronomical misinterpretation of the planet Venus or the star Arcturus.
description: On December 14, 2015, at 7:15 a.m., a witness and his wife observed, through the fog, a bright point in the sky that appeared to "sway" and grow slightly larger. Only one witness account was recorded. Plotting the observation direction described by the witness on a map indicates an azimuth of approximately 135° (Southeast) (see attached map). The star chart shows the planet Venus in this direction at an elevation of 22° (compared to the 60° indicated by the witness), very bright (magnitude -3.6). The star Arcturus, less bright (magnitude 0.15), is at an azimuth of 117° and an elevation of 51°. The phenomenon described by the witness has all the characteristics of a very bright celestial object observed through light fog: the other stars are occulted, and the phenomenon appears slightly distorted. The impression that this light was "swaying" is characteristic of the autokinetic illusion (see: The perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky). GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of the planet Venus or the star Arcturus.

summary: Observation of a bright point moving across the sky which goes out and then comes back on two or three times in a row: mistaken for a satellite, involving the stage of the SL-23 R/B rocket numbered 2015-074-C.
description: On December 12, 2015, at 6:10 PM, two residents of Vendays-Montalivet (33) went outside to observe an Iridium satellite flare. At 6:14 PM, they saw a bright point of light moving around, going out and then coming back on two or three times in succession. The UAP sighting lasted thirty seconds. Only one witness statement was recorded. The description of the UAP as a bright point of light resembling a moving star, going out and coming back on several times, is characteristic of the observation of an artificial satellite rotating very rapidly on its axis. The reconstruction of the satellite passes using Calsky software shows that one of them could correspond, both in terms of time and trajectory: SL-23 R/B, numbered according to the international designations 41107 and 2015-074-C. It should also be noted that its trajectory from southwest to east culminated at approximately forty degrees of angular elevation, which is consistent with the witness's estimate of the UFO's altitude (see the investigation report). Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency, this case appears to be a fairly rare case of mistaken identity involving a Zenit rocket stage shortly after launch. The UFO's trajectory and description correspond perfectly with that of the SL-23 R/B object, which was clearly visible at the time of the observation. Furthermore, a visual observation of this object confirmed its variable and spectacular nature. This case is Class A, mistaken for a satellite, involving the SL-23 R/B rocket stage numbered 2015-074-C.

summary: Observation of the movement of several bright white or red points forming a triangle in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 7, 2015, at 10:45 PM, a witness observed three luminous points high in the sky, forming a triangle. The points (white or red) appeared to be connected. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of luminous points crossing the sky in a few minutes strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from the South-Southwest to the North-Northeast, which is consistent with the southerly wind recorded at Orly (7 km): Météociel). Due to their inherently low luminosity, Thai lanterns are often interpreted as being farther away than they actually are, and therefore moving faster. Lantern licking usually takes place on weekends; these lanterns may have been licked to send a message to Santa Claus! GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation by a motorist of a yellow luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of the headlights of flight RYR 1761.
description: On December 5, 2015, at 5:55 PM, a driver and his son observed a stationary yellow-orange phenomenon, as bright as Venus, in the sky for one minute. No unusual noise was heard. The witness turned the head away, and when he looked again, the phenomenon had disappeared. The observation of a large point of light in the sky for one minute could have several causes: - The reflection of the sun on a satellite, Iridium or another: a check on the Calsky website indicates no candidate satellite. - The reflection of the sun on the fuselage or wings of an airplane: at that time, when the sun is less than 7 arcseconds below the horizon, the airplane would have to be at an altitude of over 15,000 meters to still be in sunlight. - An airplane seen head-on, with its headlights on: a check on the Flightradar website indicates that an airplane taking off from Carcassonne passed directly in the line of sight of the witnesses at that precise moment. This aircraft likely took off with its headlights on, and the pilot switched them off once it reached a sufficient altitude, or the witnesses moved out of the glare of the aircraft's headlights. Facing the witnesses, who were also moving in their vehicles, this point of light appeared stationary for a minute. After the headlights were switched off, or the witnesses moved out of the glare, the navigation lights, being much less powerful, against a still somewhat bright sky, may have escaped the notice of the witnesses who were looking for a strong light. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the headlights of flight RYR 1761.

summary: Filmed observation of the silent movement of 4 orange lights in the night sky: Probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, November 29, 2015 (not November 30 as indicated in the police report), a motorist was surprised to see four orange lights appear successively in the night sky. All four moved slowly along a straight path and without any noise. The witness filmed the scene with his cell phone. Only one witness statement was collected. All the elements and what can be reconstructed from them are consistent with a lantern-licking observation (see the investigation report): - the movement was consistent with the wind direction; - the appearance, color, and brightness of the UFOs were consistent; - the passage of several UFOs in succession was typical; - it was a weekend day conducive to a festive event. The only doubt concerns the first point because the witness provided no details about the direction of movement of the UFOs or his perception of the wind (was he sheltered or not?). However, video analysis indicates a probable direction of movement (from South to North) consistent with the wind direction measured at nearby stations 15 to 20 km away. This, along with other factors, allows us to maintain the hypothesis as probable. The case is weak due to the lack of information provided by the witness. Fortunately, despite its poor quality, the video provides information on the probable direction of movement. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movements of about ten points in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On Friday, November 27, 2015, around 3:00 PM, a motorist driving on a local road between Noeux-les-Mines (62) and Mazingarbe (62) observed about ten bright white dots and one dark dot moving in the cloudy sky. The motorist stopped to film. The dots moved at high speed and disappeared into the clouds. No sound was heard. The observation lasted one minute. No other witness accounts have been collected. The directional movements of about ten bright white dots in the sky remain unexplained at this stage. The witness's video shows a short trajectory of a white dot (0.24 seconds) and that of a dark dot (0.33 seconds). The photograph also shows a white dot, all against a background of gray clouds. However, beyond this, the information from the observation is rather imprecise. In particular, the witness did not provide the exact location of the observation, nor did they identify the multiple events they witnessed in the video, making it impossible to identify them. Given these limited details, the possibility of birds being involved cannot be ruled out. The insufficient information available prevents further investigation of this observation. GEIPAN classifies the case as category C.

summary: Observation in the sky of rapid evolutions of mobile white beams: probable observation of luminous skyrose animations or luminous spots.
description: On November 27, 2015, between 7:32 and 7:37 a.m., a motorist driving on the A87 motorway was intrigued by what she saw in the sky. She reported seeing moving beams of light. These beams moved rapidly and reminded her of a circular object equipped with beams, spinning in a circle at high speed. Only one witness account was recorded. This report of observing rotating circular lights clearly evokes the light displays of a nightclub or other festive venue, reflecting off the cloud cover and/or the light rain (both were present that morning). The upward beams were not visible in this report. But depending on the atmospheric conditions, one can see the patterns created (on the sky screen) or the beams alone without the patterns, or both, a bit like in a movie theater, imagining cigarette smoke (visible beams) sometimes in conjunction with the presence of the screen (patterns present or not). Depending on atmospheric conditions, the effective range of a laser is highly variable and can reach tens of kilometers, which can make the phenomenon fleeting or even exceptional at great distances from the emission point. GEIPAN has not identified the source of the beam. The hypothesis of a technical test originating from the Puy du Fou facilities has been ruled out after investigation. Since some nightclubs close late Thursday night into Friday morning, the phenomenon could have originated from a nightclub even at 7:30 AM. The neighboring nightclubs could not be contacted, or refused to provide specific information. Other similar cases can be found on the GEIPAN website (use the keywords SKYROSE or LASER). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: skyrose or spotlights.

summary: Observation of the movement of several phenomena in the sky: observation of airplanes and probable observation of a thermal balloon.
description: On November 27, 2015, between 10:30 and 11:00 AM, a witness at home observed and filmed the movement of several objects in the sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness saw several UAPs (see the two attached videos). Apart from one spherical object, these UAPs were airplanes, some flying high and leaving a white trail, and others flying much lower (and therefore without a trail) after taking off from Blagnac Airport. Indeed, air traffic analysis (Flightradar) shows a situation of two airplanes flying in opposite directions, north-south for the low-flying one and south-north for the other, a situation exactly matching one of the videos and the witness's description, including the elongated, wingless appearance typically seen in airplanes at low altitudes under the glare of the sun (10:30 AM in November). The spherical UFO is probably a playful balloon, its angular size is on the order of 0.5 tenths of a degree (size estimated from the size (a few cm) of the residual leaves of the neighboring tree in the field of the video and 30 m away from the shot) and its elevation is between 15 and 20th (again from the neighboring tree). This could be a child's balloon at very low altitude or a solar thermal balloon (a few meters in diameter (see solar balloon flights)) at a distance of a few kilometers and an altitude of up to 1 or 3 km. The thermal balloon is more likely because the ground wind (West to East at the Blagnac station) makes it difficult to explain the strong North-South component of the observation, while the wind reading at higher altitude is clearly from North to South. This wind reversal with altitude could also explain the trajectory reversal seen at the end of the video relating to the spherical UFO, which the witness describes as an "arc of a circle." The balloon would indeed be in the altitude range (~1 km) corresponding to the wind reversal (see the document reconstructing the trajectories of UFO aircraft, the geometry of the observation, and the video of the spherical UFO). as well as the wind direction at ground level and at higher altitudes). Consequently, considering only the spherical UFO (the others being airplanes), GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a thermal balloon.

summary: Night observation of the low-altitude passage of a triangular shape delimited by lights: observation of a helicopter in flight.
description: On November 13, 2015, at approximately 10:15 PM, two people in a car were intrigued by the low-altitude passage of a triangular object whose shape was defined by three round, non-flashing white lights. Two red lights were seen in the center of the object. It moved silently and smoothly away into the cloudy sky. The witness was a military man and did not recognize any aircraft or helicopter. Only one witness statement was collected. GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) requested information from the military air traffic control center (CNOA) regarding recorded air traffic in the area at that time. The CNOA radar recording clearly indicated an identified aircraft, on a medical evacuation mission, flying at low altitude, which perfectly matches the witness's account in terms of trajectory, location, and time of overflight. This is illustrated by the overlay of radar tracks on the attached map (see Reconstruction). The low-altitude, uneven trajectory (as seen by the radar track and the observation) is characteristic of a helicopter. The radar recording cannot confirm the hovering at such a low altitude as observed (15m), but it is consistent with it. It's important to remember that estimating the distance to points of light at night is highly subjective. The observation of a triangle with continuous lights—one white at each vertex and two red in the center—is consistent with that of a helicopter. It may seem surprising that the witness did not see the red and green permanent navigation lights, nor the flashing white lights, but the helicopter, which was about to land, likely activated white spotlights that obscured other lights. It should be noted that an aircraft can use various lights in addition to the regulatory ones (navigation, collision avoidance, flashing). The video Hellenic Navy AB-2012 ASW (night Flight) shows a case with three red lights, two of which are steady and a third that can be perceived as steady and is emanating from the rotating red anti-collision light. Here too, the red and green navigation lights do not appear. Regarding the absence of any perceived noise from the object, even though, according to radar, it is only 200 meters above the ground, the witness indicates that the window is slightly open, but the vehicle's engine remains running, which is not an ideal condition. Most importantly, it is common in UFO sightings for the focus on a very "striking" visual observation to mask the accompanying sound. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this sighting as A, as perfectly identified: Helicopter.

summary: Short observation of the silent and rectilinear movement of a luminous colored object in the sky: lack of information.
description: On November 10, 2015, at 7:00 PM, a witness outside their home noticed a colored glow in the clear sky. For two to three seconds, the witness observed a luminous object with two bright colors (fluorescent green and pastel orange) moving in a straight, silent line. The object, at the height of the top of a fir tree at the back of the garden, then passed over the house and disappeared from the witness's view. No trail was observed. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation is unusual. The possibility of a drone cannot be ruled out but would be surprising given the time of day (darkness) and the isolated location of the few houses. Furthermore, the level of information about the observation is insufficient considering its strangeness and does not allow for a proper investigation (the fleeting nature of the observation (3 seconds), the lack of additional information (photo, other witness statements)). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case in category C: lack of information.

summary: Observations of the silent movement of several yellow-orange lights in the night sky: very likely observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On November 8, 2015, between 11:00 PM and 12:10 AM, two people observed several yellow-orange lights moving silently across the sky, following one another and disappearing at altitude. The sighting of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked off nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from south to north, consistent with the light southeasterly wind recorded in Rodez, 15 km away: Météociel. The area being very hilly, low-altitude air currents follow the valleys more than the prevailing wind. The gendarmerie investigation specifies that: - The detection and control center in Saint-Mars-La-Pile (37), responsible for monitoring aircraft radar tracks, reported no anomalies in the area concerned on the day of the witness statement. - The same search, conducted with the Air Force's operational center for the surveillance of space objects (COSMOS), found no trace of any phenomenon in the observed data. One of the witnesses clearly described the successive and regular takeoff of a series of these hot air balloons. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": highly probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Long night observation of a luminous colored phenomenon, flashing and stationary in the overcast sky: probable observation of the star Sirius.
description: On November 7, 2015, at 12:20 a.m., a witness outside their home was intrigued by the presence of a stationary, colored light in the overcast sky. The light was very bright and appeared to be flashing. The witness noticed that their nearby electric meter emitted a louder buzzing sound when the light was visible. The observation lasted 20 minutes but was intermittent. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the witness's description and the significant duration of the observation (20 minutes), the possibility of an astronomical misinterpretation was considered (see the weather report and astronomical chart in the investigation document). Sirius was located at the azimuth given by the witness (SE) and at an elevation between 5 and 10 degrees (see reconstruction). The fact that the witness may have perceived a higher elevation (20 to 30 degrees) does not constitute a true discrepancy (a deviation within the usual tolerance when the witness does not refer to a specific experiment or measurement technique). The intermittent observation could result from significant cloud cover, which may not have been continuous that evening. Similarly, the green and red light could result from atmospheric scintillation of Sirius at low elevation. The increase in noise from the nearby electric meter, coinciding with the presence of the observation, may be linked to the tension or surprise created by the observation in the witness ("I didn't see anything like that," "strange thing"). Experience indicates that the perception of noise can indeed be altered (amplified or diminished) depending on the intensity of the visual observation. GEIPAN considers this to be very likely an observation of Sirius under an overcast sky. Consequently, this testimony is classified as B: probable observation of the star Sirius.

summary: Observation of the passage of a fragmented red luminous phenomenon over the Pyrenees: observation of the atmospheric reentry of a Centaur stage.
description: On November 3, 2015, at 7:06 AM, a motorist near Blajan (31) observed a phenomenon in the sky composed of several reddish luminous fragments. The phenomenon broke into two, then four or five pieces, and quickly faded over the Pyrenees. No unusual sound was heard. This fireball (a very fast-moving luminous ball), observed for 15 to 20 seconds, during which it broke into four or five pieces, clearly has the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry of large space debris. Numerous witnesses also saw it in Spain. Another motorist on the A64 motorway near Montrejeau (31) also filled out a questionnaire to report the sighting. However, this space debris does not appear in the list of cataloged objects published by the American service SpaceTrack. A remarkable investigation was conducted by Ted Molczan who identified this large piece of debris as the 3rd stage of the Centaur launcher used to launch an American military satellite in 2002: See his investigation: Re-entry Sightings and Debris Recovery of 2008-010B Spain-2015 November 03 UTC. Three mysterious metallic spheres that fell from the sky crashed in Spain: see Three mysterious metallic spheres from the sky crashed in Spain. This case is remarkable because it combines eyewitness observations and debris found on the ground. GEIPAN classifies these observations as perfectly identified: atmospheric reentry of a Centaur stage.

summary: Observation with a camcorder of a diamond-shaped, multicoloured object in the morning sky: Capella sighting.
description: On Sunday, November 1, 2015, around 7:00 a.m., a witness was observing the stars and spotted a point of light at random. He then saw it appear to double. Using his camcorder, he watched and zoomed in, finding the multicolored diamond shape he saw unusual. No other accounts were collected. The point of light, which the witness described as "due west at the same altitude as the Moon," is Capella. The witness didn't report anything particularly strange while observing it with the naked eye ("I just stared at a point of light at random"... "At first glance, I thought it was a satellite"), except perhaps for a star's scintillation that appeared to double. All the strangeness perceived by the witness, and the reason for his testimony, stemmed from what he saw in the video. Here, once again, we have a classic example of artifacts generated by a device filming and zooming in on a star. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as A: Capella.

summary: Long observation of two bright points in the sky: observation of the conjunction of Venus and Jupiter.
description: On October 28, 2015, at 4:30 a.m., a witness was intrigued by the presence of two very bright white points in the southeastern sky. During the approximately thirty-minute observation, no unusual noise was heard. The two points moved very little along a straight upward trajectory. The witness took three photographs. Clouds then obscured the two points of light. No other reports were collected. The witness's description corresponds to the configuration of Venus and Jupiter that night, one above the other by a few degrees, around an elevation of 10° (Venus below, brighter as shown in the witness's photograph and the Stellarium reconstruction). The only discrepancy concerned the observation azimuth, but contact with the witness confirmed (using local geographical landmarks) that he was indeed looking east. Similarly, the elevation was estimated at around 30th, while the photo shows it to be around 10th. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of a conjunction of celestial bodies (Venus and Jupiter).

summary: Long observations in the night sky of the slow movement, one after the other, of numerous reddish lights which eventually disappear: probable observations of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, October 24, 2015, at 8:30 PM, several people observed numerous reddish lights moving slowly across the sky, one after the other. These lights appeared at low altitude near Molleges (13) and eventually disappeared vertically between Saint-Sixte (13) and Le Contras (13). The witness took photos and videos. Other people contacted by telephone also observed the lights. Two witness statements were collected. The observation of reddish lights crossing the sky on a weekend evening strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The observed movement was an angular elevation along a North-Northwest axis: this could indicate movement towards the witnesses and/or a vertical ascent. The local weather report from Salon, Marignane, and Avignon indicates a very weak and unstable wind: it is not possible to determine the wind direction at the precise time and location of the observation. The two analyzed photos reveal surprisingly sharp points of light, white in one photo and colored in the other. These points are in exactly the same position in the image: these two characteristics (extreme sharpness, fixed position) are those of what are called "dead pixels" or "hot pixels"; these are common defects in digital cameras, noticeable only in night photos. Therefore, these two photos provide no further information, except that the observed phenomena were dim. Due to the witnesses' accounts being entirely consistent with the observation of Thae lanterns, and despite the impossibility of validating the hypothesis with local wind data, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" – probable observation of Thae lanterns. Meteociel readings for the day of the observation: - weather in Avignon: Météociel. - weather in Salon-de-Provence: Météociel. - Weather in Marignane: Météociel.

summary: Observation of a black teche in a motionless black fog in the clear sky: unexplained phenomenon of medium strangeness (D1).
description: On October 23, 2015, in the late afternoon, a witness drove to Fumel airfield (in the commune of Montayral, Lot-et-Garonne) to get some fresh air with his dog. He drove past the hangars and parked in a small space near the surveyor's markers. He opened the door, let his dog out, and when he turned around, he saw a black shape in a black haze in the sky. The UFO appeared to him with a sort of arc-shaped loop in the lower left and high, far away. It remained perfectly still and made no noise. The sky was blue, and there was no haze. The witness did not have binoculars or a camera to observe the UFO. At one point, he looked away from the phenomenon for a few seconds, then tried to see the UFO again, but in vain; it had disappeared. Surprised by this sighting, the witness thought it would be mentioned in the press the next day by other witnesses, which was unlikely to happen. No other testimonies were collected. Three factors (immobility for 20 minutes, sudden disappearance, and the appearance of a distant, round shape with a protrusion) contradicted, individually or in combination, the various hypotheses considered: a celestial body (appearance and disappearance), an airplane (immobility), a helicopter (appearance, noise, and lack of radar detection), and the witness's eye condition (immobility). The investigation focused on a balloon, which could not be a balloon (too small), nor a solar balloon (cause of disappearance?, unlikely in this location), and then on a hot air balloon hypothesis. This hypothesis was plausible in this location and on a sunny late afternoon. The size (10 to 20 m) provides the minimum distance (a few kilometers) for a perception of the phenomenon as distant and blurry. However, this hypothesis encounters two difficulties: - the description of a protrusion that is difficult to explain by the gondola (the protrusion not pointing downwards). But this element is not the one most clearly detected by the witness (only after 10 minutes with a significant effort of concentration and focus) - and above all, the rapid disappearance. The witness looked away and then did not find the phenomenon again. It is difficult to assess the duration of the non-observation and its compatibility with the balloon's descent over this period. This would be compatible provided that several unknowns (size of the balloon) or margins of error (witness's angular data on the size and elevation of the UFO) are taken into account in a favorable way, in addition to the temporal conjunction (with the averted gaze). Overall, the hot air balloon hypothesis is the strongest, but its probability is well below 50% and therefore cannot be retained. The various hot air balloon pilots in the department, contacted for this investigation, did not respond to requests, which in itself does not constitute an argument against the hypothesis. This is a single testimony, and without a photograph. It is entirely possible (rural setting) that the phenomenon was not seen by others. The witness is precise and credible; the consistency (level of information and credibility) of the testimony is just sufficient (given the level of strangeness) to validate the unexplained nature of the observation (see the investigation report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as D1: Unexplained phenomenon of medium strangeness. Note: this case was submitted to the GEIPAN panel of experts.

summary: Observation of the movement of long threads in the sky and of balls of light emerging from small luminous animals: observation of ballooning (means of aerial locomotion of certain animals).
description: On October 23, 2015, at approximately 1:50 PM, a couple observed a peculiar phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them: three round spheres from which burst sheaves of threads several tens of meters long. From these spheres emerged thousands of tiny creatures that swirled and appeared to be illuminated by diodes. The witness took photographs. Only one witness account was collected. The white threads photographed by the witness had all the characteristics of spider silk, also known as "Virgin's threads" or "angel hair." These threads are the vehicles of tiny young spiders that are carried away by the wind. This phenomenon is called ballooning. October is a particularly favorable month for this observation. Fine, dry weather and a light breeze are also necessary, which is the case today: see the weather report. These extremely fine threads are only visible when they are moist and/or backlit. It is normal for them to become invisible when approached, either because the observer changes their angle relative to the sun or because they dry quickly. The photographs provided accurately depict this phenomenon. The multiple balls observed by the witness may be clusters of spiders (see photo). In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of young migratory spiders and their silk thread, commonly called "Virgin's thread".

summary: Observations lasting a few seconds of three bright white lights fixed in the night sky and one red light: probable observation of a military aircraft on exercise.
description: On October 21, 2015, at approximately 9:15 PM, a driver and passenger observed three bright white lights for a few seconds. These lights, described as diffuse, stationary halos, were visible a few dozen meters above the treetops. The witness stopped observing, finished driving, and then, from his home, saw the phenomena again. These lights were more scattered and further apart. No sound was audible. The witnesses alerted the police the following day: the driver made a drawing. No other witness statements were collected. The police investigation indicated that no airships had flown over the area at the time of the observation due to the strong winds that evening. The witness observed three stationary round lights and one isolated red light (see witness's drawing) for a few seconds. This appearance clearly suggests an aircraft seen from the front at night (3 headlights + a red position light on the left). The sound of this aircraft may not be heard by witnesses in their cars with the windows closed. From this angle, the aircraft's wings are invisible because they are not illuminated. The presence of an aircraft at low altitude in this location, far from any airfield, is unusual. However, the military RTBA map (Low Altitude Ground Network - see attached map) reveals that this area, designated R166, is precisely a specific zone reserved for very low-altitude military air exercises, particularly on Wednesday evenings. The weather report indicates overcast skies and light variable winds in Bergerac at 9 PM (see Météociel). The high humidity may explain the halo observed around the aircraft's lights. GEIPAN did not process this case quickly enough (within a one-month timeframe) to verify with military air traffic control that an aircraft was indeed present in the area at that time. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of a military aircraft on exercise. The white dots observed in the second part of the observation are probably other aircraft participating in the maneuver.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 3 to 4 red-orange UFOs in the night sky: observation of Thai lanterns released following a funeral.
description: On October 20, 2015, at 8:10 PM, a witness at home observed three or four luminous phenomena in the sky. These circular, reddish-orange objects moved silently along a straight north-south trajectory. The observation lasted approximately 15 minutes before the phenomena disappeared from the witness's view. The witness took several photographs. No other witness accounts were collected. The observation of reddish-orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked off nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from North to South, which is consistent with the North wind recorded in Nancy (see the Météociel report indicating a North wind for the day of observation; recorded in Nancy-Ochey, 22km away). It is rare to observe this type of festive phenomenon during the week, but it is worth noting that it occurred during school holidays. The photos suffer from noticeable motion blur, quite normal for handheld night photos; they clearly show the yellow-orange color described by the witness, which is characteristic of Thae lanterns. The change of direction towards the East at the end of the observation could correspond to a local wind following the Ruppes stream valley. GEIPAN initially classified and published this case as "B" (probable lantern), then, having received additional information from the gendarmerie confirming the release of Thai lanterns following a funeral, GEIPAN reclassified this case as A: confirmed observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of several white flashes in a well-identified part of the night sky: mistaking for a satellite reflection phenomenon, involving a satellite at very high altitude.
description: On October 14, 2015, at 11:31 PM, a witness observed several successive flashes in the sky, in a very specific area. He checked the Heavens Above website but found no Iridium satellite flashes or corresponding satellite passes. While of moderate strangeness, this case appears to be a likely case of mistaken identity involving an out-of-control satellite, rotating relatively rapidly at a very high altitude. A reconstruction shows that five or six satellites could be located in the area of the sky described by the witness, which could explain the observation. Monitoring the passes of these satellites will help determine which one is responsible for the observed flashes. This case is classified as Class B, a case of mistaken identity involving satellite reflections and a very high-altitude satellite.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous white sphere; deafening noise: observation of a perfectly identified military aircraft.
description: On October 14, 2015, at approximately 1:25 a.m., a witness was awakened by a deafening noise outside and observed, through the bathroom window, a white luminous sphere moving through two large circles as it gradually moved away. No other witness statements were collected. GEIPAN requested that military air traffic control verify the air traffic present in the area at that time. The radar track (attached) shows an aircraft circling north of Nemes. "The track whose trajectory is concentric north of Nemes between 11:14 p.m. and 11:22 p.m. is that of a military aircraft flying at flight level 105 (approximately 3,000 meters) and needing to perform this maneuver for operational reasons before continuing its flight." The witness, blinded by the aircraft's searchlights, described only a ball of light: he was unable to distinguish the shape of the fuselage and wings, which are generally dark-colored on military aircraft. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": sighting of a perfectly identified military aircraft.

summary: Observation of a dark, oval UFO levitating in a field: lack of information.
description: On October 9, 2015, at 9:00 PM, a motorcyclist on a small road observed a dark-colored, oval-shaped unidentified flying object (UFO) in a field 50 meters away. The witness stopped to observe: he heard no noise and saw people entering the UFO, which was hovering above the ground. Frightened, the witness continued on his way, stopping again a little further on to see the UFO depart quickly in a straight line. No other witness statements were collected. This testimony proved surprisingly short considering the strangeness of the phenomenon, which was observed for a considerable time (10 minutes). Due to this strangeness, GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Unidentified Flying Objects) asked the witness to go to the police station, which he verbally agreed to do. However, despite several follow-up emails and phone calls from both the police and GEIPAN, he never went. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as category "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the clear sky and of another object in the photographs: observation and photographs of Venus, with a probable photographic artifact.
description: On October 8, 2015, at 5:00 AM, a witness was intrigued by the presence of a bright light in the clear sky. He decided to take photographs and noted the presence of another object. Only one witness account was collected. The witness reported a very bright point to the east (a telephone conversation with the witness clarified that he observed the phenomenon "under the Moon, to the left"). The numerous photos show motion blur, to varying degrees, despite the use of a tripod: the witness triggered the shutter by pressing the shutter button (without a remote or self-timer), which was enough to cause significant motion blur due to the use of a long focal length lens (300 mm). Several other bright points can be seen in the uncropped photos, undoubtedly identified as the stars 31 Leo, Pi Leo, and HIP 48876 and 48734, confirming that it was indeed Venus that was photographed. In the cropped and enhanced photos (7298 to 7301), which are unfortunately not provided in their entirety, a strange saucer shape is visible. If we look at the thumbnails of these photos with a suitable tool (e.g., XnView photo software) that shows the original framing, we can see that these photos correspond to a decentered image of Venus. The strange shape may be a photographic artifact, called a "flare" or unwanted reflection, or it may be a real lenticular cloud (diagnosis is currently underway with photography and meteorology experts). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation and photographs of Venus, with a probable photographic artifact.

summary: Successive observations and filmed of fixed luminous phenomena in the sky: certain mistakes with the following astronomical objects: Arcturus, Vega, Capella, Aldebaran, Sirius, Jupiter and Regulus.
description: On October 7, 2015, around 8:20 PM, a resident of Evron (53) spotted a light with blue reflections in the sky through his window. He saw the UFO again 5 minutes later, as he was going to bed. He then called his son, and the two of them observed the UFO for 2 to 3 minutes. He then called his brother, who lives in a hamlet in the neighboring town of Sainte-Gemmes-le-Robert (53), to report the sighting, and took out his camcorder to film the UFO. At the end of this first observation, the witness left home with his son around 9:10 PM and arrived at his brother's house around 9:15 PM. His brother was waiting for him with a neighbor. As he got out of his car, the main witness saw the UFO again. The four of them saw another UFO above a local hill. The brother and the neighbor returned home. The main witness and his son then saw five new luminous phenomena above the hills. The witness tried to film them, but his camcorder refused to work. The observation ceased at 9:25 PM. The witness reported his sighting to the police the following day. On October 9th, around 6:00 AM, he saw two more UFOs in the sky, which he filmed. These videos were recorded using a Sony DSR PD150 camcorder. The witness provided two videos of the sightings: the first, lasting 1 minute and 51 seconds, is a summary of the October 7th sighting and was published on YouTube on October 10th. The second, lasting 12 minutes and 9 seconds, shows all the footage the witness recorded on the evening of October 7th and the morning of October 9th. Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency (see the investigation report), this case appears to be a definite case of mistaken identity involving several astronomical objects: Arcturus, Vega, Capella, Aldebaran, Sirius, Jupiter, and Regulus. The quality of the videos taken by the witness allows for the precise location of the various UFOs relative to terrestrial landmarks, and the zoomed-in footage reveals several fainter stars nearby. With this information, verification using Stellarium allows for the certain identification of each UFO. This case is classified as Class A, a definite case of mistaken identity involving the following astronomical objects: Arcturus, Vega, Capella, Aldebaran, Sirius, Jupiter, and Regulus.

summary: Observation of the silent presence in the sky of luminous phenomena with alternating colours and then movement: probable observation of LED balloons.
description: On October 3, 2015, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness closing his shutters observed three ogival-shaped objects above his neighbor's trees. The alternating colors of red, blue, and green were different for each object. Initially motionless for several minutes, they then moved southward. The witness filmed his observation. His son and wife drove to the coast to continue the observation with binoculars. No noise was heard during the 10 to 15 minutes of observation. Only one witness statement was collected. According to the attached investigation report, an aeronautical phenomenon is possible but unlikely given the alternating blue, green, and red colors of the UFO, which do not correspond to any type of aeronautical navigation lights. The observation of a Thai lantern is also improbable due to the three alternating colors observed. The observation of three distinct UAPs, as described by the witness, cannot be confirmed by video analysis, as the distinction between three UAPs is not evident. This video shows that the UAP did indeed move away, and corresponds to the witness's description, which describes a phase where the UAP appears to move very little and then slowly southward. The data concerning its apparent size and brightness are not confirmed by the video. Indeed, the streetlights visible in the video, as well as in images taken from the video, allow for an assessment of the brightness by comparison. However, the video was not taken at the beginning of the observation, so it is possible that the brightness observed at the beginning was greater. This decrease in brightness would also confirm the UAP's southward movement. Following the analysis of this data and the visit to the witness, the most likely hypothesis is an LED balloon or a group of three LED balloons. Indeed, the alternating three colors at regular intervals, the slow movement carried by the wind, and the absence of sound are consistent with this type of object. Furthermore, the observation was made on a Saturday evening between 10:00 PM and 11:00 PM, by the sea. This increases the probability that a festive event took place that evening. Comparison with images taken from the witness's video and some photographic examples of LED balloons also supports this hypothesis (see the investigation report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: LED balloons.

summary: Numerous observations of the rapid passage across the sky of a very bright phenomenon: observations of a fireball of natural origin.
description: GEIPAN was informed on October 1st by the OVNI66 website of several observations made on September 30th around 11:50 PM. Witnesses reported simultaneous sightings of very bright, luminous balls rapidly crossing a part of the sky, which appeared to be a bolide, a type of meteor (see explanation of the phenomenon in the article a bolide?). "The meteor that crossed the sky over Gers yesterday, Wednesday, September 30, 2015, at 10:53 PM was visible from Les-Vans (07), Campome (66), Canet (66), l'Yssandon (19), Saint-Victor-en-Marche, Brissac (34), Chemille-Melay in Maine-et-Loire (49), Toulouse (31) and as far as Lyon (69)." (source OVNI66). GEIPAN received a formal report of an observation at 10:53 PM in Bonnes (86), near Poitiers. Numerous witnesses reported their sightings to the newspaper "La Dépêche du Midi" in Toulouse. A GEIPAN member also observed it out of the corner of their eye. At 10:53 PM, GEIPAN's "Allsky" automatic camera also recorded the phenomenon, as did the cameras at the Pic du Midi Observatory and Rochechouart (87), between Angoulême and Limoges (see camera images). The three-dimensional model produced from the camera images allows for a precise characterization of the trajectory of the luminous phenomenon, at a very high altitude of approximately 60 km. This phenomenon was produced by the reentry into the atmosphere of a meteoroid, fragments of which may have reached the ground. (See the Google Earth model: 2015-30-09 2254.kmz) The short duration of the phenomenon implies an initial velocity greater than 8 km/s, pointing towards a natural origin: a small mineral object probably originating from the asteroid belt. Space debris would have produced a longer phenomenon. GEIPAN verified on the website http://www.calsky.com that no recorded space debris had fallen that day within sight of France. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as perfectly identified: observation of a bolide of natural origin.

summary: Brief observation of the straight passage of a triangular shape delimited by red circles at each end; instantaneous disappearance into the deep sky: lack of information.
description: On September 28, 2015, at 5:26 AM, an outdoor witness observed a silent, red triangular shape (with rounded red extremities, the object itself being less bright than its extremities) passing silently across the sky for 5 seconds. The UFO moved parallel to the horizon in a straight line and disappeared instantly into the deep sky. Only one witness report was recorded. The witness observed a red triangle bordered by three bright red lights; it is possible that the triangular shape was a visual illusion, and that only the three lights were real. Satellite pass tracking on Calsky indicated two satellites visible on the northeast horizon where the witness observed: USA 16/NOSS 1-7A, and Lacrosse 5 Rocket. There was indeed a third satellite on the same trajectory: NOSS 6 (D), but it passed 10 minutes later. Therefore, we cannot directly correlate the witness's observation with these three satellites, unless the Calsky model is inaccurate. The red color would be surprising, but at low altitude, it would be conceivable due to the thickness of the atmosphere traversed. We could also consider Thai lanterns moving south, pushed by the light northerly wind (see Météociel), but the day and time (Monday morning) seem unlikely to support this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this somewhat unusual phenomenon as category C due to a lack of information to confirm or refute these hypotheses.

summary: Observation of about twenty lights passing in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 26, 2015, at 11:59 PM, a witness observed about twenty lights in the sky, resembling streetlights but moving. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. Their movement was observed from northeast to southeast, which is perfectly consistent with the northeast wind recorded in Creil (see the Météociel report). The witnesses did suspect Thai lanterns, but couldn't understand how one of them could move faster. It is noted that this supposed lantern is the last one, and therefore licked after the others, which has not yet reached the same altitude. It is possible that the wind speed at altitude is slightly different from the wind speed near the ground; a perspective effect must also be considered: at the same speed, a nearby object appears faster than its more distant counterpart (see diagram). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of a formation of 5 white dots in the sky: probable observation of balloons.
description: On September 26, 2015, at 3:00 PM, a witness observed five white dots in a clear blue sky for approximately five minutes. The dots moved slowly and silently towards each other. The formation continued to fly, then entered a cloud and disappeared from the witness's view. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of white dots flying together in a blue sky, in the same direction as the wind, strongly suggests balloons, likely licked at a party. The objects appeared to originate from Remoncourt, to the northeast of the observer. The wind recorded in Nancy was indeed a northeast wind (see the Météociel report). The date and time (Saturday, 3 p.m.) could correspond to a wedding (there was indeed a wedding in Remoncourt on September 26). GEIPAN did not pursue the investigation to verify this hypothesis. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of balloons.

summary: Successive observations in September of the passage of aircraft preceded by luminous phenomena: probable observations of aircraft in military operations.
description: The witness heard the sounds of airplane engines and observed several luminous orbs moving very quickly in multiple directions. Two airplanes were flying near these orbs. The witness had observed a similar phenomenon the previous week (September 14, 2015) and believes this new observation is a logical continuation. The witness gave two very similar accounts on September 14 and 23, 2015, from the same location and at the same time (around 10:30 PM). Each time, the witness clearly observed an environment of military air operations, describing the aircraft with their sounds and contrails. Furthermore, the witness indicates that this made him "think of the very recent exercises (early September) of Rafale fighter jets along the coast (Roscoff/St-Pol-de-Leon border) flying at low altitude (exercises?) "for hours they flew over our heads at low altitude!" and he specifies for September 14th that "For me, it's almost certain that on Monday, September 14th, it was military aircraft." In this environment of air operations, here is what surprised the witness on September 14th: - "Two very loud and distinct noises (like a "missile" or a huge firework without a detonation) made me look out the window." - a UFO that appeared different from the aircraft moving in the sky because it was in the form of a spherical ball and which at one point released a curtain of light towards the ground. And what surprised the witness on September 23rd: - "several (4 or 5) "Bright balls" (much brighter than the few star-like lights that appeared) moving very quickly in different directions (could be mistaken for a "ballet") appearing and disappearing alternately at high speed. - "Two planes (identifiable by the white trails they formed) near these bright balls (I only saw 2, there may have been more, given the noise). The phenomenon lasted about 1 to 2 minutes, the "bright balls" disappeared quickly, only the planes remained visible and audible." The UFO zone, as reported by the witness in relation to its location (SW or SE depending on whether it was the 14th or 23rd), and also as drawn on the map by the witness, corresponds to a low-altitude military flight zone (see RTBA map of 2015). The witness therefore attended two air exercises. In such a context, what seemed strange to the witness is not necessarily so. These exercises can, for example, involve tests of infrared flare launches, which can generate strange flashes for those who might have difficulty associating them with the context of maneuvers and exercises (see the article: Illuminating munitions and military flares as UFO generators). No other witness contacted GEIPAN to report any unusual aspects of these events, which nevertheless attracted attention in the sky, at least by their noise (as in the case of this testimony). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the cases of September 14th and 23rd as Category B: aircraft.

summary: Two close observations of the movement of an orange or grey object in the sky; trajectory with obtuse angles: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, September 20, 2015, around 8:00-8:15 PM, a witness on their terrace observed a clear sky with a "vertical fall" of an object at high speed, which disappeared into the landscape. The witness initially thought it might be a supersonic aircraft. A few seconds later, the witness again saw an object, rapidly ascending towards the zenith. Part of the object appeared to detach and descend horizontally. The witness believes it was the same object seen in both observations. No noise was heard during these orange or gray phenomena. Based on the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - Lack of precise angular data. - Lack of azimuthal data for the appearance and disappearance of UFOs during each phase of the observation. - Incomplete information regarding the presence of contrails. - Observation durations for each phase are unknown. - Lack of detail regarding the nature and magnitude of the movements reported by the witness as being at an "obtuse angle." And although the only plausible hypothesis considered is that of confusion with contrails observed at sunset, we can conclude that the lack of information prevents us from definitively confirming this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as an observation of a phenomenon that cannot be identified in its current state, as the lack of information prevents us from establishing a firm opinion.

summary: Observation after the fact on a photograph without direct visual of bright points in the blue sky: confusion with the reflection in a window of light fixtures located behind the witness photographer.
description: On September 20, 2015, at 4:52 PM, while visiting the Ballon Keep (72) during Heritage Day, a witness took several photos of the site, including one of the landscape through a windowpane, without noticing anything unusual. However, upon returning home and viewing these photos, he observed three very distinct points of light against the blue sky in the one showing the landscape, which he described as follows: "I noticed three points of light in the blue sky in one of them. I then enlarged the photo and, to my great surprise, I saw three groups of six points of light, each forming a hexagon in the photo." No other witness statements were collected. The series of photos analyzed (see investigation notes) shows reflections, in a window, of one of the groups of LED lights present and illuminated in the room where the witness was located when he took the photographs. An on-site investigation confirmed the existence of these lights and made it possible to reproduce in photographs the effect observed by the witness (see GEIPAN photos). Consequently, the case is classified as A e, confusion with the reflection in a window of lights located behind the witness taking the photographs.

summary: Observation of the silent and simultaneous passage of three grey light spots on a straight trajectory: probable observation of the passage of birds illuminated by a light area from the ground.
description: On September 19, 2015, a witness observing the stars, particularly the constellation Ursa Minor (the Little Dipper), was surprised to see three fixed gray lights moving in a straight line, forming an isosceles triangle in the sky. No trails, halos, or noises were observed during the simultaneous passage of the three lights. They gradually faded out over the course of a second. The observation lasted a total of eight seconds. Immediately after this observation, the witness watched an aircraft cross the path of the unidentified flying object. No other witness statements were collected. The witness could not provide the exact time of the observation but did give a clue (a French rugby try against Italy): the investigator was able to determine the time of the observation to be 10:31 PM (see the investigation report). Aeronautical (airplane flyover) and aerospace (satellite or rocket launch) hypotheses were therefore investigated. Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency, this case could be mistaken for a flock of birds illuminated by a ground-based light source. The non-point-like appearance of the light spots composing the UFO, as well as its rapid angular velocity, are compatible with this hypothesis. Furthermore, there are two sources that could potentially illuminate birds from below in the direction indicated by the witness. This case is Class B, a possible misidentification of a flock of birds illuminated by a nocturnal light source.

summary: Successive observations in September 2015 of the passage of aircraft preceded by luminous phenomena: probable observations of aircraft in military operations.
description: The witness gave two very similar testimonies on September 14th and 23rd, 2015, from the same location and at the same time (around 10:30 PM). Each time, the witness clearly observed an environment of military air operations, describing the aircraft with their noises and contrails. Furthermore, the witness indicates that this made him "think of the very recent exercises (early September) of Rafale fighter jets flying at low altitude along the coast (Roscoff/St-Pol-de-Leon border) (exercises?) "for hours they flew over our heads at low altitude!" and the witness specifies for September 14th that "For me, it's almost certain that on Monday, September 14th, it was military aircraft." In this environment of air operations, here is what surprised the witness on September 14th: - "Two very loud and distinct noises (like a "missile" or a huge firework without a detonation) made me look out the window." - a UFO that appeared different from the aircraft moving in the sky because the UFO was in the form of a spherical ball which at one point released a curtain of light towards the ground. And what surprised the witness on September 23rd: - "Several (4 or 5) luminous spheres (much brighter than the few star-like lights that appeared) moving very quickly in different directions (resembling a ballet), appearing and disappearing alternately at high speed. - Two aircraft (identifiable by the white trails they formed) were near these luminous spheres (I only saw 2, there may have been more, given the noise). The phenomenon lasted approximately 1 to 2 minutes; the luminous spheres disappeared quickly, leaving only the aircraft visible and audible." The area of the UAPs, as reported by the witness in relation to their location (SW or SE depending on whether it was the 14th or 23rd), and also as marked on the map by the witness, corresponds to a low-altitude military flight zone (see RTBA map of 2015). The witness therefore attended two aerial exercises. In such a context, what seemed strange to the witness is not necessarily so. These exercises can, for example, involve tests of infrared flare launches, which can generate strange flashes for those who might have difficulty associating them with the context of military maneuvers and exercises (see the article Illuminating munitions and military flares as UFO generators). No other witness contacted GEIPAN to report any strangeness about these events, which nevertheless attracted attention in the sky, at least by their noise (as in the case of this testimony). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the cases of September 14 and 23, 2015, as category B: aircraft.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 8 orange objects in the night sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 13, 2015, between 1:15 and 1:30 a.m., a witness observed from their balcony the silent passage of eight bright orange objects (appearing successively) from southeast to northwest in the clear sky. The objects disappeared one after another. The witness took photographs. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a local festival or a private party. The witness took several photos: they turned out to be out of focus (a common issue with night photos under these conditions) and show only a blurry orange circle. However, they confirm the reality of the phenomenon, and the color is entirely consistent with that of Thai lanterns. The movement is observed from Southeast to Northwest, which is consistent with the easterly wind, shifting to Southeast during the night, as recorded at Toulouse Blagnac (Météociel report). The very regular movement of objects in the sky is quite normal for an object carried by a light wind; if the objects fly over industrial areas with strong ventilation or large heat sources, the trajectory is, of course, irregular. As the lanterns are often licked one after the other, after the same delay corresponding to the time it takes to light the lantern, the result is a very organized line of flying lights. Due to their inherently low luminosity, Thai lanterns are often interpreted as being farther away than they actually are, and therefore moving faster.
