GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 5 bright yellow-orange points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 13, 2015, at 8:30 p.m., two people on a balcony were intrigued by the silent movement of five bright yellow-orange points of light in the sky, following an upward trajectory. Three of them formed a triangle. Only one witness statement was recorded. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (attached document), namely: - the orange or yellow-orange color, identical to that of lanterns; - the number corresponding to a "classic" lecher group of lanterns; - the simultaneous movement of the lanterns, carried by the wind and creating a Gestalt psychology illusion; - the movement in the direction of the prevailing wind; - the behavior identical to that of objects subjected to no or light wind: low speed; - the short observation period (1 to 2 minutes), consistent with the lifespan of the lanterns; - the date: a Sunday evening, consistent with those times when lantern releases are organized for celebrations. - The disappearance caused by the extinguishing of lanterns that had reached the end of their lifespan. - The absence of noise. - The presence nearby of open-air facilities suitable for launching lanterns, located in the direction of observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Appearance and disappearance three times of a spherical, pale yellow luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, September 13, 2015, between 9:05 PM and 9:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by the appearance and disappearance, on three separate occasions, of a pale yellow, spherical luminous phenomenon in the clear sky. The phenomenon moved erratically, and no unusual noise was heard. The witness recorded a 1-minute, 34-second video. Although accompanied by another person during the observation, only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the information gathered in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - the yellow and reddish-yellow color, identical to that of lanterns; - the brightness, comparable to that of a very bright star; - the shape, described as spherical; - the behavior, identical to that of objects subjected to no or light wind: movement in the direction of the prevailing wind and an upward movement caused by warm air; - the duration of the observation, consistent with the lifespan of lanterns. - The date: a Sunday evening, consistent with the times when lanterns are typically released for celebrations. - The number of lanterns is consistent with the number of lanterns released in succession. - The disappearance of the lanterns was caused by them going out. - The absence of noise. - The presence of nearby facilities suitable for lantern release, located in the direction the witnesses observed. GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable sighting of Thai lanterns. The witness, informed of this hypothesis, refuted it: having already released them, he knows what they look like. But it's important to understand that the appearance of a Thai lantern seen from a distance is nothing like the view one has when releasing them. GEIPAN did not launch a local investigation to find the possible perpetrators of this lantern release. This type of investigation is only conducted for large-scale lantern licking events held during major holidays, which are relatively easy to locate. Smaller lantern licking events may occur at minor private gatherings (birthdays, or trials), which are very difficult to detect in urban areas.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of two luminous orange balls in the sky: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 13, 2015, at approximately 12:25 a.m., a witness at his home observed two glowing red-orange orbs silently passing in the clear sky. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from Southeast to Southwest, which is consistent with the Southeast to North wind recorded in Brive-Souillac (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation in Brive-Souillac). The very precise testimony and especially photo 477 confirm this hypothesis: the "madeleine" shape, the characteristic color, and the more yellow center leave no doubt. The other photos show the phenomenon from a distance and are more difficult to interpret. The witness, an amateur astronomer, was surprised by this unusual object, of a nature quite different from the celestial bodies he knows well. Due to the rather low intrinsic luminosity of the lanterns These lanterns are often estimated to be farther away, and therefore larger, than they actually are. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" – an observation of thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of a white phenomenon in the sky and a humming noise: lack of information.
description: On September 11, 2015, around 3:00 AM, two people in their car were intrigued by a white luminous phenomenon in the sky. The witnesses stopped, and the object changed direction, emitting a whirring sound. The witness took three photos. Only one witness statement was collected. The case contains elements of strangeness. The luminous sphere, seemingly stable in the sky, eventually moved and departed with a whirring sound. There is no radar recording. One hypothesis could be a helicopter maneuvering (undetected by radar due to its low altitude), although this remains surprising at 3:00 AM in open countryside and without the knowledge of the local police. Furthermore, the case contains inconsistencies in the witness statement, the first being that the witness did not respond to repeated requests for an on-site investigation. Previously, he had also failed to respond to requests for clarification regarding the UFO's position in the sky, nor to the request for a statement from the spouse of the witness who was also in the vehicle. An on-site investigation would have allowed for further investigation and perhaps resolved the remaining questions. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: no response from the witness.

summary: Observation of a 3-second movement in the night sky of a black rectangular shape with an orange band in the middle: mistaken for a paraglider.
description: On September 9, 2015, at 9:30 PM, a witness observed, for three seconds, above the Belledonne mountain range, the movement of a pale yellow rectangular shape marked in the middle by a black band. No sound was heard as this shape moved along a straight downward trajectory. No change of course was observed. Only one witness report was collected. The UFO sighting site is located only 3 km from an extremely active free flight (paragliding) area. The described appearance is consistent with a paraglider that may have been conducting a night flight (aeronautical night begins 30 minutes after local sunset). Night flight (paragliding, hang gliding) is regulated. The aircraft must display two lights (one green and one red). Furthermore, a night flight must be declared to the prefecture and can only take place three days before or after a full moon. This was not the case here. This night flight was illegal, which explains the lack of regulation lighting. The 7th Alpine Chasseurs Regiment (located in Varces) indicates that there were no military exercises that night. Given the available information, we can conclude that this observation likely concerns an unauthorized night flight of a civilian paraglider (see the attached investigation report). This testimony is of average consistency (some discrepancies between the questionnaire data and those collected on site, a single testimony) but sufficient, given its unusual nature, to classify the case as B: probable misidentification of a paraglider.

summary: Successive observations in the same night of the passages of 3 silver lights and a flashing red light; engine noise: probable observation of an aircraft.
description: On Sunday, September 6, 2015, around 11:30 PM, a witness heard the unusual noise of an aircraft that had been flying over their neighborhood at night for several months. At midnight, the noise started again, but the witness turned off the radio and lights and opened the window of their fourth-floor apartment. They then observed three steady silver lights and one flashing red light. The object's trajectory was straight. It passed over the building opposite and then disappeared, hidden by the urban landscape. The sighting was repeated at 12:11 AM and 12:35 AM. No other reports were collected. This sighting did not represent anything particularly strange: the witness themselves indicated that the noise did not surprise them, saying, "I recognize the noise of this aircraft that has been flying over our neighborhood irregularly at night for several months; I don't think it's necessary to get up from my chair." The unusual element this evening lies in the fact that the witness finally looked at the object that was the source of the not-so-strange noise and did not recognize it as an airplane or helicopter, specifying that he could only distinguish the lights and not the shape of the unidentified flying object (UFO). The object passed several times over the building opposite, and there is every reason to believe it was a helicopter, given that helicopters use varying nighttime lighting depending on their type or mission. Furthermore, a noisy and particularly strange object passing and repassing over a Parisian neighborhood around midnight during the summer months would likely have generated other reports. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable sighting of an aircraft.

summary: Observation of two brief flashes spaced a few seconds apart in the clear sky: mistaking for a satellite reflection phenomenon, involving the Globalstar 56 satellite.
description: On September 7, 2015, at approximately 9:43 PM, a witness observed two brief flashes, spaced a few seconds apart, in the clear sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. While of moderate strangeness, this case appeared to be a case of mistaken identity involving satellite reflections. Further investigation (see the investigation report) allowed for the identification of the satellite most likely responsible for this misinterpretation, as its trajectory and timing perfectly matched the witness's description. This case is classified as Class A, a case of mistaken identity involving satellite reflections, and involves the Globalstar 56 satellite.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 8 to 9 yellow-orange lights in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 6, 2015, at 12:15 a.m., a witness was driving between Airvault (79) and Viennay (79) when he observed the silent movement of 8 to 9 lights in the clear sky. They initially formed two distinct shapes: the first four in a square, the last 3 or 4 irregularly aligned. The witness then stopped in a parking lot and focused particularly on the last light, which was directly above him. He saw a perfect circle, ranging in color from orange to yellow, and took a picture with his cell phone. The observation lasted 8 to 9 minutes in total. No other reports were collected. The observation strongly suggests a formation of Thai lanterns, whether in terms of its general appearance, the dominant orange color, the time (a weekend night), or the closer, more detailed observation of one of them passing vertically ("light appearing as a perfect circle with orange or yellow light circulating inside"). The estimated speed (90 km/h) cannot be accurate given the presumed wind speed. However, speed estimation is always difficult and subjective, and it is not consistent here with other elements of the testimony which indicate a much lower speed. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this observation as B: high probability of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the particular evolutions of a point of light in the sky: probable mistaking for a satellite coinciding with the observation of a meteor.
description: On September 6, 2015, at approximately 10:45 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light moving across the sky from south to north from their garden. Initially, they mistook it for a satellite. The UFO stopped for a few seconds, resumed its trajectory, and then made a half-loop in the opposite direction. After another stop, the UFO disappeared at high speed. Only one witness account was recorded. While of moderate strangeness, this case lacked sufficient evidence (a single witness, no photograph, and missing details). It appears to be a possible case of mistaken identity, involving the observation of an artificial satellite passing directly overhead, immediately followed by a meteor, likely belonging to the Kappa Cygnids meteor shower. However, the witness's lack of detail prevents formal confirmation of this hypothesis (see the investigation report). The unusual and immediate sequence of a satellite pass and a meteor could have been interpreted by the witness as the movement of a single object. Furthermore, the stops and rotations of the UFO described by the witness could be a misinterpretation of the observation, caused by a particularly uncomfortable viewing position, as it was vertical. This case is Class B, probable misidentification of a satellite coinciding with the observation of a meteor.

summary: Brief observation of the passage of a dark triangular shape and rapid departure: probable mistaking for an airplane.
description: On September 6, 2015, at approximately 10:40 AM, a driver was startled by a shadow that seemed to obscure the sun. While driving and leaning forward, the driver glimpsed, through the windshield, a slightly curved triangular shape with a lighter circle at each end. The entire object was matte black. Alerted, the front passenger opened the window but saw nothing. The driver continued on her way. A little further on, the two witnesses saw the phenomenon move away in the direction of Breteville (50). No noise was heard. No light was seen. Only one witness statement was collected. The most likely explanation is that it was an airplane (see the investigation report). Indeed, on Sunday, September 6, 2015, an event occurred 13 kilometers to the west of the location. The purpose was to honor the pilots of the Great War, and two French Air Force Rafale fighter jets flew over the bay of Étretat around 10:30 AM. It is quite possible that one of these aircraft flew directly over the exact location of the sighting and was the source of the observation. The witness's description of the aircraft suggests a Rafale, with some differences that could result from the difficult viewing conditions (the main sighting was brief, as it was made by a driver just before a roundabout). The absence of noise was what most surprised the two witnesses, along with the fact that apparently no one else had observed this phenomenon. It was a Sunday morning, and there were walkers and other vehicles around. However, it is possible under certain conditions not to hear the sound of an aircraft (see the excellent study by Gaelle Fedoce on this subject), and GEIPAN also knows from experience that visual surprise can mask or inhibit auditory perception. The fact that there were no other eyewitness accounts strongly supports the aircraft hypothesis. Other people may have observed the same thing as the two witnesses under better conditions and recognized an aircraft; in that case, there was no need to provide testimony. Lacking radar data for this observation and the exact trajectories of these two Rafales, we cannot definitively confirm the hypothesis that a Rafale could have flown over the witnesses' car. The second hypothesis, that a civilian or military drone was in the area, is less likely (due to the rapid angular movement). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable mistaking for an aircraft.

summary: Observations of silent evolutions of lights in the night sky on the same night: probable observations of a luminous animation.
description: On the night of September 4-5, 2015, two witnesses observed silent, glowing lights in the night sky above Roquebrune-sur-Argens. Witness T1 made their observation at 11:40 PM on the 4th, and Witness T2 at 12:15 AM. No other reports were collected. The observation of milky luminous circles moving in low clouds over a weekend night for several tens of minutes strongly suggests a light show produced by a nightclub or other public entertainment. The tourist area where the observation took place is, of course, very conducive to this type of event. The two witnesses observed a similar phenomenon 45 minutes apart, probably originating from the same source, but possibly oriented in different directions: these laser projectors are clearly visible from more than 10 km away. One of the witnesses took a series of photos of the phenomenon, which are entirely consistent with this explanation. GEIPAN has not conducted research to find the precise source of this animation and classifies this case as B: probable observation of a light animation.

summary: Observation of the step-like movement of a bright point at very high altitude in the sky: lack of information.
description: This report, filed in February 2016, concerns an observation made in the second half of September 2015 (the date is arbitrary). The witness was on a boat at the dock when they observed a point of light moving through their open skylight. The light stopped suddenly and then moved off very quickly, thus ascending in stages. Only one report was collected. The description may seem strange, but it has already been reported to GEIPAN and could be explained by one or more converging phenomena (satellites entering and leaving their line of sight, the effect of visual autokinetic, etc.). Without a precise date (the witness does not know the day of the month), further investigation is impossible. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of the gradual increase and decrease of a bright point in the night sky: observation of an iridium flare.
description: On Saturday, August 29, 2015, at 9:26 PM, a witness on his terrace was looking at the stars and an airplane when he was surprised to see a luminous phenomenon in the northwest that increased in intensity and then decreased until it disappeared. Only one witness statement was recorded. The characteristics of the UAP (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) were noted by the witness: - Immortal point of light - Observation duration of 10 seconds - Brightness similar to that of a star. These data are typical of an Iridium flare or flash. Furthermore, the data concerning the time and direction of the observation (the exact time recorded was 9:26 PM and the observation direction was towards the northwest) are consistent with those concerning the Iridium flare of the object Iridium 54, which had a maximum magnitude of -6.6 (see the investigation report). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of an Iridium flare.

summary: Observation of silent passages of several orange or white luminous points in the sky between 9:45 p.m. and 11 p.m.; various directions of movement: probable Thai lanterns.
description: On August 29, 2015, between 9:45 p.m. and 11:00 p.m., a family observed a succession of orange and white lights moving across the sky. Some gradually faded away, while others disappeared from sight in various directions. No noise was heard during the observations. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of orange and white lights in the sky on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The successive disappearance of these lights supports this hypothesis, as it resulted from the lanterns burning out. The very brief witness statement does not allow for a correlation between the observation and the wind. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of 4 round yellow-orange objects with a bright red center in the sky: probable observation of balloons.
description: On Saturday, August 29, 2015, around 2:00 PM, a witness watching television noticed four distinct, round, yellow-orange objects with red centers moving across the sky, seemingly forming a single phenomenon. The objects moved slowly and silently, passing over the building before disappearing from view. The witness managed to take a photograph. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness likely saw objects carried by the wind. The slow movement as they approached and flew over the building (heading northeast) is consistent with a light northeasterly wind (see the weather report). Furthermore, the photographs and description suggest a rather round shape, like balloons. The red or orange glow could be from Thai lanterns, which can vary in color and shape, but it could also be from helium-filled LED balloons. In conclusion, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a red ball in the sky and intriguing photograph: misinterpretation of a photograph by the witness.
description: On August 29, 2015, at 11:02 PM, a couple observed a red ball silently passing across the night sky for five minutes. The photograph taken intrigued witnesses (see image2.jpg). Only one witness account was collected. The witness initially saw a UFO in the sky. The description (particularly the color, the occurrence on a weekend night, and the strong wind direction "towards Switzerland") strongly suggests a Thai lantern. The witness wanted to photograph the UFO. However, the motivation for this testimony stemmed from what they believed they could discern figures inside the UFO in the photograph (it is clearly visible that there are figures inside, excerpt from the questionnaire). Analysis of the photograph (see Reconstruction PAN 2 publication.pdf) indicates, in addition to an obvious spherical structure, that the photo was not taken facing the sky, but rather towards a square. The origin of this discrepancy in perspective remains unknown. By comparison with the daytime photograph of the square, and despite the blurriness, we can identify: - the lights of two lampposts, one of which prompted the witness to report a UFO - the playground equipment in the square illuminated by these lampposts - and perhaps even the railing of the balcony where the photograph was taken. A geometric reconstruction shows that from the probable location of the photograph (based on the exact point on the balcony), the respective alignment of the lamppost lights and the playground equipment can be established. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: error in the witness's interpretation of a photograph.

summary: Observation of the silent evolution of two orange lights in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, August 28, 2015, between 9:00 and 9:15 PM, four people in a garden observed two orange lights in the sky. One light appeared stationary due west, and the second moved from the northwest. The lights disappeared one after the other in a southwest direction. No sound was heard during the one-minute observation. The witness had time to take four photographs. Only one statement was recorded at the police station. The series of photos analyzed (see the investigation report) shows, with a high degree of probability, two Thai lanterns, moving with the wind. The observation took place on a Friday evening, a day of the week conducive to weekend festivities (weddings, various celebrations) during which such lanterns may be released. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the event as category B: probable Thai lanterns.

summary: Nighttime observations in the Parisian sky of a red glow: probable observations of a luminous spot originating from a powerful red laser.
description: On the night of August 23-24, 2015, witnesses were intrigued by the presence of an intense red glow in the Parisian sky. They independently reported their observations. The first witness began their observation at 11:25 PM on August 23, 2015: they observed a very bright red glow in the Parisian sky towards the southeast. This light appeared to be constant (with a change in intensity) and moved slightly across the sky before returning to its initial position. Intrigued, the witness took photographs with their smartphone and observed the phenomenon until 1:00 AM before going to bed (see the investigation report). A second witness, at 12:58 AM on August 24, 2015, observed a fiery red ball located to the northwest above the Parisian buildings for 10 minutes. This witness had time to take three photographs with a mobile phone. He went back inside to wake his wife; the object had disappeared by the time he returned to the window (see the investigation report). The testimonies are consistent, with sufficient and usable data provided by the witnesses. Several photographs of the UFO were taken and used for analysis, leading to fruitful cross-referencing. In conclusion, the physical and dynamic characteristics of the UFO observed and photographed by the witnesses are similar to those of a powerful red laser used by a private individual in Paris, from a rooftop, and whose luminous spot produced by its impact on the low cloud/haze layer resembles the UFO. The ambient lighting conditions surrounding the witnesses during their observation and photography prevented the laser beam from being visible, both to the naked eye and to the camera sensor, except after one of the photographs was enhanced. The strangeness of this case is ultimately quite low and is mainly due to the intensity of the UFO's light and its persistence for over an hour and a half. The two eyewitness accounts are the subject of independent analysis thanks to the photographs and consistent testimonies (see the investigation reports). This case is classified as a Be-type event, a probable observation of a bright spot on cloud or hazy ground, caused by a powerful red laser projected from the top of a building in the 11th arrondissement of Paris.

summary: Observation of the movement in the night sky of a luminous phenomenon moving at a constant speed: mistaken for the passage of a satellite.
description: On August 23, 2015, at 10:25 PM, two witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon moving in the sky at a constant speed. However, the UFO changed direction slightly several times (North, then NW, then finally North again), which intrigued the observers. Only one questionnaire was completed. Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency (numerous coherent and precise details lending credibility to the case), this case turned out to be a classic case of mistaken identity involving a satellite. Further investigation identified two satellites that are very likely the source of this misinterpretation: IGS 5 H2A rocket, whose brightness matches that of the UFO and whose trajectory is very close, and Iridium 16, an out-of-control satellite whose trajectory and apparent speed match those of the UFO. GEIPAN classifies this case as A, mistaken identity involving a satellite, although some doubt remains about the exact identity of the satellite.

summary: Observation of three luminous white shapes forming a triangle in silent movement: possible mistaking for white birds illuminated by urban lighting.
description: On August 21, 2015, at 11:13 PM, a witness by the sea was drawn to a movement in the sky: three luminous white star-shaped objects formed an isosceles triangle that moved silently in a straight line. Looking away from the UFO to call another person, the witness never saw the phenomenon again. The observation lasted approximately 7 seconds. Only one witness account was recorded. While of moderate strangeness, this case is sufficiently plausible and could be mistaken for a flock of birds illuminated by a local light source (see the investigation notes). The proximity to the sea and the presence of a lighted marker reported by the witness are consistent with this hypothesis, which nevertheless remains fragile due to the lack of possible verification or other witnesses. The case also lacks precision due to the very short duration of the observation. This case is class B, possible confusion with white birds illuminated by urban lighting.

summary: Observation of a luminous bluish conical shape surrounded by a halo: cloud of gas resulting from the passivation of the cryogenic upper stage (ESC-A) of the Ariane VA225 launcher.
description: On August 21, 2015, at 2:00 AM on Réunion Island, a witness photographed an intriguing phenomenon in the sky. The witness reported seeing a luminous, bluish cone-shaped object surrounded by a halo. Only one witness account was recorded. This observation of a large, translucent luminous object moving slowly across the sky is quite exceptional, and the quality of the photographs taken by the witness allows for its precise characterization. Due to its resemblance to other similar phenomena (see the article on a luminous halo in the sky over the Indian Ocean on September 29, 2013), the investigation quickly focused on the possibility of recent satellite launches. Indeed, after investigation, the object's position in the sky is consistent with the trajectory of the cryogenic upper stage of the Ariane VA225 launcher, launched from Kourou on August 20th at 8:16 PM UTC. This stage, cataloged as N40876, began its passivation (fuel tank emptying) at 9:12 PM; it passed directly over Indonesia at an altitude of over 8,000 km (see attached map). Around 9:30 PM UTC (the date the image was taken), the object was clearly visible from Réunion Island. As this is a geostationary satellite launch into a highly elliptical transfer orbit (approximately 300-36,000 km), the launcher is already at a very high altitude at this time, and therefore visible from a very wide area. The cloud's trajectory is close to that of the launcher, but perturbed by the gas ejection velocity, which is difficult to model. The gas cloud released by passivation may have persisted until its dissipation into space. The observed halo is the unused gas cloud ejected by the launcher after the propulsion phase; it is illuminated by the sun and becomes visible to ground observers at night. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" as a perfectly identified phenomenon: a gas cloud resulting from the passivation of the cryogenic upper stage (ESC-A) of the Ariane VA225 launcher.

summary: Observation of the constant speed movement of a white luminous blimp-shaped object: probable mistaking for an airplane.
description: On August 17, 2015, at 7:04 AM, a witness observed a very bright white object, resembling a blimp, moving at a constant speed at high altitude for one minute. It gradually disappeared in a southerly direction. The observation lasted one minute. The witness filmed the phenomenon with their cell phone and remains intrigued. The video (see the investigation report) clearly shows a passenger plane flying at cruising altitude, in a stable atmosphere conducive, on the one hand, to the absence of a condensation trail and, on the other hand, to the effects of atmospheric scattering leading to the apparent disappearance (and confusion with the surrounding blue sky) of areas in the plane's shadow or less well-lit by the sun than the fuselage. Here, the wings disappear, giving the blimp-like appearance. It was not possible (analysis too late) to access the flight records to confirm the aircraft's presence and identity. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable misidentification of an aircraft.

summary: Observation of the movement in the sky of three equidistant white lights forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: On August 16, 2015, between 12:40 and 12:45 a.m., a witness, accompanied by friends, observed three equidistant white lights in the sky forming a perfect triangle. The object moved slowly and silently before disappearing suddenly. His friends did not have time to see the phenomenon. No other witness accounts were collected. Between the lights, the witness distinguished a thin black triangle. This triangle could be the result of a perceptual illusion called a contour illusion or shape illusion (see Game Psychology). The movement was observed towards the West; If these are lights carried by the wind, their movement seems incompatible with the westerly wind recorded in Béziers. However, the observation was very brief, and a local breeze is always possible along the coast. This case presents a low level of consistency: the observation was very short, and witnesses present noticed nothing. If we accept the possibility of an optical illusion, this case is not very strange and could correspond to illuminated balloons (LED balloons or Thai lanterns), frequently launched during festivals (it was the evening of August 15th, in a tourist area). The wind reading does not allow us to confirm or refute this hypothesis. Given these uncertainties, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and cross-checking.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 7 red-orange luminous points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, August 15, 2015, at 10:30 PM, two people observed seven luminous points crossing the clear sky. Round and reddish-orange in color, the points moved silently, initially in a straight line, then appearing to ascend. Only one well-documented witness account was collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from north-northwest to south-southwest, which is consistent with the northerly wind recorded in Angers (see the weather report from Météociel in Angers on the day of the observation). The photos are entirely consistent with this type of object. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a bright spot with sudden extinction: mistaking for a satellite reflection phenomenon, involving the Metop A satellite.
description: On August 15, 2015, at 10:36 PM, a resident of Nîmes (30) was stargazing with his wife and daughter from his garden when he saw a very bright point of light shining in the southeast for about ten seconds before going out. The witness tried to identify the UFO on the GEIPAN website: he thought it might have been an Iridium flare. Of moderate strangeness, but with sufficient consistency, this case turned out to be a classic case of mistaken identity involving a satellite reflection phenomenon from the Metop A satellite. The time, trajectory, and position of this satellite are perfectly consistent with the witness's description (see the investigation report). This case is classified as Class A, mistaken identity involving a satellite reflection phenomenon from the Metop A satellite.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of a triangular shape in the sky; pendulum motion: observation of a child's balloon inflated with helium.
description: On August 14, 2015, around 5:00 PM, a witness spotted a triangular shape in the sky, moving slowly with a pendulum-like motion. Using binoculars, he distinguished a royal blue color as the object flew overhead. The object remained below the clouds and moved silently from the NNW to the SSE. Only one witness account was recorded. The weather report from Lanvéoc, a few kilometers away, indicated a steady NW wind with overcast skies. The aeronautical weather report from Brest was as follows: METAR LFRB 141500Z 31010KT 280V340 9999 SCT017 BKN030 16/12; broken cloud base at 1700 feet (500m), below a thick layer at 3000 feet (1000m). The observed object, flying from the NNW to the SSE, therefore has the characteristics of a wind-borne object. Its described shape might suggest a hot air balloon, but the time of flight is unusual for this type of flight (aeronauts prefer to fly early in the morning or at sunset to avoid thermals). Furthermore, the area is a no-fly zone due to numerous military sites. Finally, since the cloud ceiling is low and the object appears almost point-like to the naked eye, it must be relatively small (if the object has an apparent size on the order of one-tenth the size of the Moon and is flying at an altitude of 500 m, it measures less than 50 cm). A child's balloon, perhaps a shiny Mylar balloon seen nearby, is much more likely (very common models in various shapes). A festival was held in Roscanvel (northwest of the observation site) on the evening of August 14th. Fairground stalls may have been set up that day. Based on this information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" as a probable observation of a child's helium-filled balloon.

summary: Observation of the movement of a particularly bright point in the night sky: probable observation of the International Space Station.
description: On August 12, 2015, between 10:00 PM and 11:00 PM, a witness and his grandson, out for a walk, observed a particularly bright point in the sky. After a few minutes, it began to move, crossed the sky in a straight line, and disappeared, hidden by a forest. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of a very bright point moving in a straight line could have several origins: - Satellite: the initial impression of immobility may have been an illusion due to the fact that the witnesses were walking. Around 9:50 PM that same day, a very bright ISS was observed passing over a northeast-to-east trajectory, but slightly before the time window identified by the witness. Several satellites passed along this northeast-to-east trajectory during the time window: Cosmos 2082, Rocket, Cosmos 1833 Rocket, USA 29/DMSP 5D-2/F9, but they are likely not bright enough (magnitude 3 at best) to have given this impression. However, we cannot rule out the possibility that one or more of them was in a position that day that made them appear very bright (negative magnitude). - A head-on aircraft: this explanation is possible but unlikely. To have this appearance, an aircraft must be seen quite low on the horizon (less than 30 arcseconds). When it changes direction, its flashing lights are then visible. Verification is impossible (too late). - A helicopter: this hypothesis could also work, but the silence doesn't support this hypothesis, and flashing lights would have been difficult to see. In summary, due to the strong similarity of the phenomenon described with the appearance of the International Space Station, despite the slight deviation from the time slot defined by the witness, GEIPAN classifies this case "B": observation of the ISS.

summary: Observation of several very distant luminous phenomena at sunrise: lack of information.
description: This complex report describes a series of luminous phenomena in the sky, just before sunrise on August 12, 2015, at 6:38 AM. The witness specified during a telephone conversation that their window was facing precisely southwest (225°). The observed luminous circle appeared to be three times smaller than the Moon. The first observation could correspond to a flare (sunburst) from an Iridium satellite. The other observed phenomena could correspond to sunlight reflecting off aircraft; indeed, the proximity of sunrise is very conducive to this type of phenomenon. As the observation report is complex and imprecise regarding the directions of observation, and because the report arrived too late to allow for verification with air traffic control, GEIPAN cannot confirm this latter hypothesis. No other reports have been collected. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the silent passage in the sky of two black boomerang-shaped objects with the front of a triangle; sudden change of direction for the second: lack of information and cross-checks.
description: On August 11, 2015, at 1:15 PM, a family was intrigued by the silent passage of two black, boomerang-shaped objects with a triangular front across the sky. The objects quickly disappeared, hidden by trees. The first object's trajectory was straight, while the second abruptly changed direction. No other witnesses were reported. The weather that day, recorded in Nîmes-Garons, was unusual: a change in wind direction was observed, shifting from northerly in the morning to southerly in the afternoon. The observation occurred right in the middle of this inversion, making it impossible to determine the local wind at that precise moment (see the Météociel report). The boomerang shape and non-linear trajectory suggest a kite or a radio-controlled model airplane or drone (see a video of a craft with this shape: drones or light-up flying wings). The local environment (a residential area) seems very unsuitable for flying a kite, especially if the wind is unstable. The remaining hypothesis is a radio-controlled flying wing, which seems compatible with the observation, but which GEIPAN is investigating. GEIPAN lacks the means to verify without further testimony or photos/videos. It classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient corroboration.

summary: Observation of the movements of two low-altitude light spots in the night sky; maintenance of the same spacing in the movements: lack of information.
description: On August 11, 2015, at approximately 10:05 PM, a witness on his terrace was intrigued by two bright lights of different colors at low altitude that he saw in the clear sky. The lights moved silently in a straight line, then accelerated, zigzagged, resumed a straight trajectory, and then disappeared. The lights maintained the same spacing between them throughout their movement. The witness added to his account his GPS coordinates, the exact azimuth of observation, and an annotated photograph of his sighting. Only one report was received by GEIPAN. Given the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - Lack of data regarding the colors of the UFO. And although the most plausible hypothesis (confusion with a drone flying at night) could have been considered, we can say that the lack of information prevents us from definitively concluding in favor of this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as an observation of a phenomenon not identifiable in its current state, the lack of cross-checks and elements not allowing a solid opinion to be established.

summary: Very long observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky moving slowly: observation of the star Arcturus.
description: On Monday, August 10, 2015, between 1:00 and 2:00 AM, two people observed a colorful luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them. One of the witnesses took photographs. Only one witness account was recorded. The prolonged observation (approximately one hour) of a luminous point moving slowly across the sky suggested a celestial body. It was determined that the star Arcturus was at an azimuth of 283° and an elevation of 13°, exactly in the direction of observation indicated by the witness (intersection of N104° and A10° at an azimuth of 282°, estimated elevation of 15°), therefore quite close to the horizon. The witness observed the phenomenon on subsequent days, but sometimes with a different appearance and fewer colors. On the evening of the first observation, unsettled weather was noted, with variations in pressure and wind (see the report Météociel). Star twinkle is very strong at low elevations, especially if the atmosphere is disturbed (wind, heat), which was the case that evening: a slow, multicolored blinking can frequently be observed when looking at stars or planets at low elevations with binoculars. The witness did not mention any stars in their field of view, even though they should have seen Arcturus in that direction. The photos do not provide much information due to significant camera shake and low light levels. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the star Arcturus.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of about fifty small white discs in the night sky: probable observation of the passage of luminous balloons.
description: On Saturday, August 8, 2015, at 2:00 AM, a person at home observed the silent passage of about fifty small, milky-white (then tin-gray) discs across the sky. The phenomenon was observed first with the naked eye and then with binoculars for 8 to 10 minutes. During their slow, undulating movement along a straight trajectory, some discs gradually detached from the front and rear of the group. The entire formation slowly disappeared from the witness's field of vision. No other reports were collected. The observation of about fifty luminous discs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests festive illuminated objects carried by the wind: illuminated balloons or lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party, birthday, or other celebration. The white, then gray, color suggests illuminated balloons, lit by LEDs and inflated with helium, similar to these: light-up balloons. Unlike Thai lanterns, these illuminated balloons do not pose a fire risk. Their movement is observed from northeast to north, which is consistent with the light north-northeast wind recorded in Cannes Mandelieu. Because the light wind was almost directly in front of the witness, the flying objects appeared to move very slowly (see the report from METEOCIEL). GEIPAN has not received any other reports of this phenomenon. An investigation to find the perpetrators of the lecher is extremely difficult in an urban environment. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of luminous balloons.

summary: Very long observation of 4 fixed silver lights at low height, seen through foliage: probable observation of lights on a sports field.
description: On August 7, 2015, at 3:00 AM, a witness observed four fixed, bright, silvery lights through the foliage. The lights were adjacent, two by two, on the same horizontal line. The witness observed these lights until 4:30 AM and then decided to go to bed. No other witness statements were collected. Fixed lights seen through low-hanging trees (from the first floor) can have various origins, most likely at ground level. In this case, contact with the witness established that there is a stadium behind these trees. Therefore, it is possible that specific work was carried out that night, or that the usual lights were left on exceptionally all night. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the event as Class B: probable ground lighting.

summary: Sudden nighttime observation of a green beam of light in an apartment: probable observation of a green laser spot operated manually at a great distance.
description: On August 6, 2015, between 12:15 and 12:20 a.m., a witness watching television was startled by the sudden appearance of a very powerful green beam of light that entered his apartment. The phenomenon moved across the walls for a few seconds. The witness ruled out the possibility of a laser, as he was on the 4th floor with no neighbors overlooking his apartment. No other witness statements were collected. A very bright green spot that moved very quickly and randomly had all the characteristics of a handheld green laser pointer operated by a prankster. This type of very powerful laser has a range of several kilometers. At long distances, the movements of the light spot are, of course, extremely rapid: a movement of the operator's hand of just a few degrees results in a large movement of the beam over a kilometer. This type of laser is banned from sale in France, but unfortunately quite widespread. Users of these lasers are severely punished if they target aircraft in flight. GEIPAN lacks the resources to identify the operators of these devices. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a manually operated green laser beam at a great distance.

summary: Very brief observation of a grey triangle with lights at each corner: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On August 6, 2015, around 10 PM, a witness glanced briefly out of their skylight and saw a stationary gray triangle with orange-red lights at each corner. The UFO then moved very quickly westward in a straight line. No other eyewitness accounts were collected. This very brief observation describes a gray triangle with a light at each corner. This type of description often stems from a perceptual illusion called a contour illusion or Gestalt (see the article on the psychology of form). It is highly probable that what the witness saw was simply a collection of points of light. Similarly, the onset of the phenomenon at "phenomenal speed" may simply have coincided with the lights going out. The origins could be various: lanterns, airplanes, satellites. The observation period is too short, and the time frame too broad to allow for a reasonable investigation. The Météociel report indicates a light northerly wind recorded in Reims. Lacking precise information and cross-checking, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: One-second observation of the rapid movement of a translucent triangular shape in the sky: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On August 6, 2015, at 10:20 PM, a witness spotted a translucent triangular shape in the sky, which intrigued him. No noise, no flashing, no trail was observed. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness observed the phenomenon moving from southwest to northeast over a few tens of degrees in one second. An initial check of the astronautical context, using the Calsky website (see attached report), indicated a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) between 10:20 PM and 10:25 PM, from west to east, at low elevation, simultaneously with the observation but quite far from the direction of observation of the witness, who, lying down, was looking towards the zenith. The speed of the phenomenon, and its coincidence with the Perseid meteor shower observation period, suggests a hypothesis of three simultaneous shooting stars (perhaps originating from the same celestial body). This hypothesis, of course, does not explain the hollow triangular shape observed by the witness. This shape could be a perceptual illusion (see the link Illusion of shape or contour). However, this hypothesis cannot be confirmed. The witness, interviewed by telephone, specified that the brightness of the points of light did not resemble that of a shooting star. The very brief observation by a single witness does not allow for a detailed characterization of the phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Nighttime observations of the silent passage of orange balls sparkling in the clear sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 5, 2015, between 10:00 and 10:30 PM, two people in the same town observed several orange orbs silently passing across the clear sky. The intensity of these orbs gradually decreased until they disappeared. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a summer night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked off nearby after a private party. The movement was observed coming from the southeast. The Infoclimat report from Epinal (approximately 10 km away) indicates a light wind, highly variable throughout the evening (South wind at 9 pm, North wind at 10 pm Infoclimat report for the day of the observation). It is not possible to correlate this wind with the observed movement. The second witness reported identifying a flicker similar to a candle flame. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a very bright white point in the night sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On August 5, 2015, at 11:10 PM, a witness was intrigued by an intensely bright white point moving across the sky before disappearing. This eyewitness account of a very bright point crossing a portion of the sky is very precise, both in terms of the date and the position in the sky. The trajectory of the phenomenon corresponds perfectly to that of the International Space Station (ISS), which was very visible that evening. The witness only observed the end of the passage. (See Calsky's report, in text and graphic format against a sky background). One detail of the observation may seem contradictory to this explanation: the witness describes a few zigzags in the trajectory of the phenomenon. This is a perceptual illusion called autokinetic illusion or autokinesis (see the article on the perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky), which applies to both stationary and moving points of light. This illusion is common when observing the ISS, which is particularly bright (see observation case CLARET (04) 22.08.2012). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS)

summary: Observation of the silent passage in the night sky of 3 red-orange circles: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 4, 2015, at approximately 11:00/11:15 PM, several people on a terrace observed two large, luminous, reddish-orange circles moving in a straight line across the sky at the same speed and without noise. The objects passed over the roof of the house and were lost from sight. A third object then appeared, its brightness seeming to decrease. The witnesses searched the house, but the object had disappeared. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness's description (colors, shapes, group flight) strongly suggests a flight of Thai lanterns. The described movement has a strong north-south component (constant and strong 60th elevation and azimuth varying from northwest to southwest), which is consistent with the predominantly north-south wind direction recorded nearby in Blagnac (see the weather). The different appearance (at the end of its observation) of the third object can be explained by the extinction (including the slow extinction described) of the lantern, thus gradually changing it from a luminous round shape to a gray round shape. The latter is still distinguishable when the environment is not too dark, which is often the case in cities (a lantern flies at a height of 50 or 200 m not far from streetlights). The lantern's descent (which can be rapid once it reaches the minimum temperature for lift) This could have occurred immediately after the initial observation, when the lantern was obscured by the house. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the passage of a long trail in the sky: certain observation of the disintegration upon its entry into the atmosphere of a Soyuz rocket stage catalogued under the number "15035B/40745".
description: On July 27, 2015, at 8:00 PM (Tahiti time), a witness observed a long, incandescent trail with parts breaking off and moving east-west. The continuous observation lasted between 30 and 40 seconds. The phenomenon disappeared behind clouds. Only one witness account was recorded. Given the evidence gathered, namely: - The time of reentry was identical to the time of observation. - Existing data on the SATOBS website. - The physical and dynamic characteristics of the observation were identical in every respect to those of a space debris reentry, GEIPAN classified this case as a confirmed observation of the disintegration, upon atmospheric reentry, of a Soyuz rocket stage cataloged under number "15035B/40745", the day after its resupply from the ISS.

summary: Two successive observations of two flashes in the night sky: very likely a mistake with two satellite flashes.
description: On July 21, 2015, at 2:00 AM, a witness was observing the stars when he saw a flash intensifying and then diminishing. He observed the same effect two minutes later. Only one witness statement was collected. Due to its lack of specificity and consistency (single witness, no photograph), this case appears to be a very likely case of mistaken identity involving two satellite flashes (see the Investigation Notes document). The UFO exhibits all the typical characteristics of such a phenomenon: increasing and then decreasing brightness, slow flash, and a static position in the sky. Furthermore, several satellites, known to produce powerful flashes, passed in an area close to where the UFO was observed. However, the lack of precision in the witness statement makes it impossible to definitively identify the satellite or satellites responsible for the observation. This case is classified as Class B, a very likely case of mistaken identity involving two satellite flashes.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear and silent movement of a fire-colored flying object in the night sky: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Tuesday, July 21, 2015, at 11:00 PM, a witness observed a flying object moving quickly and silently in a straight line across the sky for 10 to 15 seconds. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - the orange color identical to that of a lantern - the rounded shape, like a lantern observed from a distance - the movement in the direction of the prevailing wind - the short observation duration (10 to 15 seconds) consistent with the lifespan of lanterns - the absence of noise, GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable sighting of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the passage in the sky of an object composed of several lights; sound of engine humming heard: probable sighting of a helicopter.
description: On July 20, 2015, two people at their home were intrigued by the slow movement of an object with several lights of different colors in the sky. A whirring engine sound was heard. The UFO was moving in a straight line from north to south. The observation lasted between four and seven minutes. Only one witness statement was sent to GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group). Based on the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - Observation of lights whose colors were identical to those of aircraft navigation lights. - Correct positioning of these lights relative to the direction of movement of the UFO and the position of the witnesses. - Observation of the beam of a searchlight similar to those used by Civil Security and Gendarmerie helicopters. - Perception of an engine noise identical to that of an aircraft. GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable helicopter sighting (category B). Given the low oddity of the sighting, GEIPAN did not conduct any investigations with the national gendarmerie or air traffic control.

summary: Observation of the silent and straight passage of a blazing red object in the night sky: observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 20, 2015, at approximately 10:57 PM, a family observed a bright red object moving silently in a straight line across the night sky before disappearing behind a building. Only one witness account was recorded. A video was taken on a cell phone but could not be sent. The witness's description of the object's movement is confusing regarding the end of its trajectory (although the witness did not appear to be familiar with the area). The object's trajectory appears to have originated in the northeast but ended in the southwest rather than the southeast. Indeed, the statement "heading towards the center of Nérac" indicates an endpoint southwest of the observation point, not southeast. Similarly, the descriptions of its movement "across the entire visible horizon from the balcony, from left to right" and "disappearance of the object behind the annex" located to the right confirm that the observation ended in the southwest. The weather situation in Agen-La-Garenne at 11 PM, located 20 km to the NEE, indicates a light northerly wind (6 km/h) and visibility of 45 km (see the website Météociel). The southwestward trajectory is consistent with a northerly wind direction measured 20 km from the east. These elements support the observation of a Thai lantern: significant brightness, red color, moving with the wind, straight and uniform trajectory, and no noise. This hypothesis is reinforced by the summer period and the location in a holiday village. Lanterns are frequently licked during this period as well as on New Year's Eve. The launching of a single lantern is frequently observed. Consequently, GEPAN classifies it as B: observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the OE movement of an orange luminous phenomenon in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On Sunday, July 19, 2015, at approximately 12:15 a.m., a witness observed a luminous, reddish-orange ball moving rapidly from west to east for 30 seconds before disappearing into the clouds. He later noted luminous irregularities in the photographs taken. Five other people observed the phenomenon, but only one well-documented questionnaire was collected. Given the objective elements defined in the investigation report (see attached document), namely: - Reddish-orange color identical to that of lanterns. - Short observation duration (approximately 30 seconds), consistent with the lifespan of lanterns. - Movement in the direction of the prevailing wind. - Day: a Saturday evening, a day suitable for lantern releases during celebrations. - Illusion of disappearance caused by the lantern going out or entering the cloud layer. - Absence of noise. GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear movement of a line of orange lights in the sky: very likely observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 19, 2015, around midnight, two people observed a line of several orange lights in the sky through binoculars. The objects twinkled, and the whole formation resembled a flock moving from west to east. A witness noticed a final light that quickly joined the others. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the information gathered in the investigation report (see attached), namely: - the orange color identical to that of lanterns; - the behavior identical to that of objects subjected to no or light wind (moderate speed); - the short observation period (approximately 1 minute), consistent with the lifespan of lanterns; - the date: a Sunday evening, consistent with the times when lanterns are released for celebrations; - the number of lights consistent with the number of lanterns released. - The illusion of acceleration and disappearance caused by the lanterns going out or entering the cloud layer. - The absence of noise. GEIPAN classifies this case as a B-level observation of Thai lanterns, a very probable occurrence.

summary: Intermittent observation of an orange luminous phenomenon in a stormy sky: lack of information.
description: On July 17, 2015, at 10:30 PM, five people were intrigued by the presence of a round, orange object near a storm cloud. The luminous phenomenon disappeared after 10 minutes. It returned and then vanished again. Fighter jets were seen at that time. Photos taken with cell phones were unusable. Only one witness statement was collected. The strangeness of this case is primarily due to the simultaneous observation of the UFO with two known phenomena (storm and fighter jets), which the witness unconsciously associated, even though nothing indicates a link between the three phenomena other than a temporal and spatial coincidence (see the investigation report). The witness statement is weak, with little usable data collected. Furthermore, the observation conditions were poor, at night. Although some clues suggest confusion with two Thai lanterns, this case should be classified as an observation of a phenomenon for which the absence of concrete and usable data does not allow us to conclude.

summary: Observation of the silent flight of a fireball and sudden disappearance: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Thursday, July 16, 2015, at 10:21 PM, a witness was surprised to see an object flying at low altitude that appeared to be on fire. It flew silently from west to east, then stopped and changed trajectory. It disappeared in a matter of seconds, vertically above the ground with a "surprising" acceleration. The witness had time to take a photo with their phone and discovered an orange "fireball" in the picture. No other witness statements were collected. Based on the objective evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - the orange color identical to that of lanterns; - the behavior identical to that of an object subjected to no or light wind (moderate speed); - movement in the direction of the prevailing wind; - the short observation time (1 minute) consistent with the lifespan of lanterns; - the illusion of disappearance caused by the lantern going out; - the absence of noise; - the time of year and location conducive to celebrations. GEIPAN classifies this case as B as a probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a luminous orange ball skimming the treetops: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Thursday, July 16th, around 11:00 PM, a witness in his garden spotted a bright light in the night sky. The witness described an orange fireball moving silently, skimming the tops of nearby trees. Its trajectory was linear, then it slowly disappeared over the horizon. His partner had previously taken a photograph, which was scanned and attached to the police report. Only one witness statement was recorded. The description includes typical characteristics of a Thai lantern (color, trajectory), and its movement is consistent with the wind direction measured a few kilometers from east to west (see the weather forecast on Infoclimat). The witness stated that it did not resemble any lantern he had previously seen. However, lanterns can vary in appearance depending on their color, altitude, and phase of flight. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage across the night sky of a triangular shape formed by three low-intensity orange circles at each end: lack of information.
description: On July 15, 2015, at 11:45 PM, a witness observing the stars saw a satellite pass overhead and was then surprised to see a triangular flying object formed by three faint orange circles at each end. The phenomenon was fleeting and disappeared very quickly to the northwest in the clear sky. The observation lasted 5 seconds. Only one witness account was collected. This account is of average quality: imprecise, coming from a single witness, and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly unusual, as the behavior and appearance of the UFO are ultimately quite commonplace. Considered as a whole, and pending further details from the witness regarding the UFO's angular measurements, its movement, and certain observation conditions, this case is provisionally classified as Category C: observation of a phenomenon not currently identifiable, the significant lack of information preventing a firm conclusion.

summary: Observation of three red lights moving silently in the sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On Wednesday, July 15, 2015, at 10:37 PM, a witness in a parking lot observed three very bright red lights forming a triangle and flying at low altitude. The object emerged from behind a forest, headed towards the witness's building, then made a 45° turn and disappeared from his field of vision. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the evidence gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - the red color identical to that of lanterns; - the number corresponding to a typical group of lanterns; - the simultaneous movement of the lanterns, carried by the wind and creating a Gestalt psychology illusion (movement in the direction of the prevailing wind); - the behavior identical to that of objects subjected to no or light wind: moderate speed; - the absence of noise; - the short observation period (10 to 15 seconds) consistent with the lifespan of the lanterns. - The presence nearby of facilities suitable for launching lanterns, located in the direction of observation and not visible from the witness's position. GEIPAN classifies this case as a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a small star blinking at a regular frequency, then moving in a straight line, blinking again then disappearing in the clear sky: probable mistaking for an out-of-control satellite rotating rapidly on its axis.
description: On July 12, 2015, between 3 and 4 a.m., a witness located on the banks of the Hérault River observed a small star that blinked at a regular frequency, then moved in a straight line, blinked again, and disappeared into the clear sky. No unusual noise was heard. Only one witness account was recorded. Due to its lack of specificity and consistency (single witness, lack of precision regarding the time), this case appears to be a likely case of mistaken identity involving an off-axis satellite, rotating rapidly on its axis (see the Investigation Notes document). The UFO indeed exhibits all the typical characteristics of such an object: brief and intense blinks, short observation period, slow movement, and the appearance of a star or satellite. Unfortunately, the lack of precision in the witness statement regarding the time prevents formal identification of the satellite, although the Iridium 73 satellite, known for its regular flashes, did pass directly through the area indicated by the witness at a very close time. This case is class B, likely a case of mistaken identity with a rapidly rotating, out-of-control satellite.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of more than a dozen orange balls in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: In the early hours of Sunday, July 12, 2015, at 12:45 a.m., several people at a gathering with friends were intrigued by the silent passage of more than a dozen orange orbs across the clear sky. Their trajectory was straight. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from SSE to East, which is consistent with the westerly wind recorded at Le Havre-Octeville (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of the passage of a luminous ball in the sky: observations of an atmospheric reentry.
description: On July 9, 2015, around 7:00 PM, two witnesses in the Seine-et-Marne department (77) observed the rapid passage of a luminous phenomenon across the sky. The phenomenon was described as a luminous ball with a trail. This observation, lasting a few seconds, of a luminous ball followed by a trail is typical of the bolide phenomenon. See the article A Bolide?. GEIPAN received another report of a simultaneous observation, and the specialized website IMO (International Meteor Organization) received 14. (See the website IMO). GEIPAN therefore classifies this case as A: confirmed observations of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid, which produced a bolide.

summary: Observation of the silent movements of a white sphere. Disappearance in the sky: lack of information and corroboration.
description: On July 9, 2015, at 5:30 PM, a witness in their garden spotted a white, spherical object hovering in mid-air. The sphere moved forward, backward, veered to the right, then to the left, before very quickly taking a straight, upward trajectory and disappearing into the sky. The observation lasted three minutes. No noise was heard. Only one witness report was filed. Upon reading this report, GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) considered the possibility of a child's balloon, initially held captive, subject to the whims of the wind or the will of its owner, and then licked intentionally or unintentionally. This rather unusual hypothesis could explain the observation, but cannot be confirmed without photos, videos, or further witness accounts. The Météociel weather report indicates a sustained northwesterly wind in Blagnac. Therefore, despite a reasonable assumption, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and cross-checking.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 15 to 20 orange light points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On July 6, 2015, at 10:45 PM, two people observed multiple bright lights (between 15 and 20) moving across the sky. These pinkish-orange lights were in a line and moved silently toward Aix-les-Bains in the clear sky. The observation lasted approximately 10 to 15 seconds. Only one witness account was recorded. The sighting of orange orbs crossing the sky in less than a minute on a summer night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from south to north, which is consistent with the southerly wind recorded in Chambéry-Aix-les-Bains. The Météociel weather report for the day of the observation indicates a light south wind of 2 to 9 km/h recorded in Chambéry. The witness's distance estimate cannot be accurate since they have never seen this type of object. Because Thai lanterns are inherently dim (large candle flame), they are always perceived as being farther away, and therefore larger and faster than they actually are. See the article "Size and Distance Estimation of an Unknown Phenomenon" on the GEIPAN website. The very regular movement of objects in the sky is perfectly normal for an object carried by a light wind; if the objects fly over industrial areas with strong ventilation or large heat sources, the trajectory is, of course, irregular. Since the lanterns are often released one after the other, after the same delay corresponding to the time it takes to light the lantern, the result is a very organized line of flying lights. The videos mentioned by the witness seem to correspond perfectly to the release of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observations of two types of luminous phenomena in the sky: observation of Venus and Jupiter for fixed UFOs and lack of information for the others.
description: witness reported several successive observations of luminous phenomena seen in the sky. He filmed the phenomena. Only one testimony was collected. This observation is quite complex, as it includes two types of phenomena: - a stationary phenomenon, clearly visible in the video due west (see astronomical chart): this is the planet Venus, very visible at the 30-second mark in the sky (Jupiter can be seen slightly to the right, at the same altitude. They set at 11:45 PM that day). - several other phenomena that are mobile, moving slowly and irregularly from west to south (see chart). They appear as yellow or yellow-orange lights: "It looks like a large airplane headlight coming from the horizon." The observed doubling could correspond to two airplanes whose trajectories converge and then diverge. The variation in the lights is due to the variation in the aircraft's heading: the landing light appears brighter the closer the observer is to the aircraft's flight path. This hypothesis seems quite plausible: aircraft approaching an airfield do indeed have this appearance: at long distances (>15 km), flashing lights are much less visible than landing lights. However, GEIPAN did not receive this report quickly enough to compare this observation with actual air traffic. This hypothesis cannot be definitively confirmed. This case involves the observation of Venus and Jupiter for the fixed lights, but is classified as Class C for the moving lights, which appear to be aircraft viewed head-on.

summary: Night observation of the movement of a bright point with blinking at low altitude in the sky: probable observation of an aircraft preparing to land.
description: On July 5, 2015, at 10:30 PM, a witness observed a yellow light approaching through his bay window. He went out onto his terrace and saw the object veer off, flashing rapidly, before disappearing at high speed. The witness filmed his observation: streetlights and the moving light can be seen in the distance. No other witness accounts have been collected. This powerful yellow light (see photo), which can be seen flashing (see video), moving slowly low on the horizon, suggests an airplane preparing for landing. The apparent disappearance of the phenomenon corresponds to the airplane changing course, so that it was no longer facing the witness. In this configuration, an airplane is visible from more than 20 km away. The witness is located 20 km from the busy Bele Mulhouse airport and 10 km from the Mulhouse-Habsheim recreational airfield. GEIPAN did not process this case quickly enough to determine which aircraft was involved in the sighting. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable sighting of an aircraft preparing to land. Southwest to West wind reported at Mulhouse: see Météociel.

summary: Long and repeated observations of two bright points in the night sky: observations of Venus and Jupiter.
description: The witness observes a bright point of light every evening (without specifying for how long) starting at 9:45 PM, soon followed by a second, less bright one. These points move slowly together and disappear, hidden by the landscape. The prolonged and repeated observation of bright points in the sky naturally suggests a common astronomical phenomenon: stars or planets. A check with a star chart does indeed indicate Venus and Jupiter exactly along the witness's line of sight. It is regrettable that the witness, despite having a high level of university education, did not independently consider an astronomical phenomenon; he was clearly too influenced by television programs on the subject of UFOs. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of Venus and Jupiter.

summary: Observation of the evolution of a luminous red-orange shape in the night sky: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 4, 2015, around 11:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by the movements of a bright, reddish-orange, round shape in the night sky. No noise was heard during the observation. The object suddenly disappeared. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation, at night, of an orange ball or light moving in the sky for a few minutes, followed by its sudden disappearance, can be explained by a Thai lantern. The change in trajectory during the observation period is consistent with the fluctuating wind direction recorded by nearby weather stations that day (see attached document). The probability of a Thai lantern is reinforced by the presence of a festival that evening in the village, as mentioned by the witness. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of light evolutions in the night sky: confirmed sighting of the 8 Alphajets of the Patrouille de France.
