description: On July 3, 2015, at 10:29 PM, several people were intrigued by the presence of a peculiar luminous phenomenon in the night sky. Only one witness reported observing two rows of round, white, parallel, and horizontal lights for three to four minutes, without any halos. These lights gradually formed a triangle, without any apparent noise, and began to curve before disappearing to the west. The repeated observation of lights in the sky, arranged in regular geometric shapes, suggested an aerobatic team performing a training exercise or demonstration. A check with the Patrouille de France, based in Salon-de-Provence, confirmed that the team had exceptionally flown at night in this region on July 1 and 3: on July 1 to rehearse the demonstration that took place on July 3 for the graduation ceremony of the new classes. The silence accompanying the sighting is perfectly normal because the noise of an aircraft seen head-on, from more than a few kilometers away, is very faint. The eight Alpha Jets of the Patrouille de France are equipped with powerful searchlights visible from over 10 km along their flight path. When the aircraft turn, the searchlight beam changes direction, and observers located on the initial flight path see it suddenly disappear. These aircraft, seen from the side, are only visible by their red or green position lights, which are not powerful enough to be seen at long distances. Seen head-on, the approach is not perceptible; the aircraft appear motionless. Only lateral movement is perceived, and this may be slight. GEIPAN also received reports of a sighting of the same patrol on July 1st, from Valensole, Lurs, and Sainte-Tulle, about ten kilometers away. During the first days of July, GEIPAN has received similar sighting reports in Provence every year since 2008, one in particular being reported in Villeneuve on July 5, 2013. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": confirmed sighting of the 8 Alphajets of the Patrouille de France. See a video of the Patrouille de France flying at night over Paris.

summary: Observation in the sky of a group of lights that separate and evolve independently but in pairs: observation of satellites.
description: On July 3, 2015, at approximately 1:10 AM, a witness observed four vertically aligned "stars," tilted to the right and evenly spaced, in the darkness of night. The group then separated, and the points moved differently in pairs. The lights eventually went out. A check of satellite passes on the Calsky website (see attached record) indicates that at that precise moment, two groups of two remarkable satellites passed: the pair of satellites USA 62/NOSS 2-1C and USA 62/NOSS 2-1B, and the ADEOS 2 H2A Rocket satellite and the Yaogan 1 LM Rocket "debris" (the brightest of the four), which appeared to be "traveling" together but were in fact at very different altitudes. The rare spectacle described by the witness perfectly matches the model generated by Calsky based on orbital parameters published by NORAD (USA). Due to the streetlights being switched off, the witness would have particularly noticed this rather exceptional coordinated pass; it was even noted that another pair of satellites was visible on a nearby trajectory a few minutes earlier: Cosmos 1689 Rocket and Landsat 5. This time of year is very favorable for observing a maximum number of satellites on axes close to South-North or North-South. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: satellite observation.

summary: loud, dull noise precedes the sighting of a dark mass with many lights: likely sighting of the Patrouille de France during a night exercise.
description: On July 3, 2015, around 10:00 PM, during a family gathering, a witness and his son went to the far end of the family garden. A deep, muffled noise was heard, and then the witness observed a moving mass above the trees of the neighboring house. Numerous lights (about a hundred), not flashing, were seen beneath the mass. The witness wanted to alert the others, but the loud noise prevented him from doing so. No one in the group saw the phenomenon, but everyone heard the muffled noise. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation of multiple multicolored lights beneath a dark mass is quite atypical. The engine noise noted by the witness suggests an aeronautical hypothesis. A map check (see attached map) indicates that the witness was in line with the runways of Salon-de-Provence, from where the Patrouille de France takes off, particularly active at this time of year, preparing for graduation displays and the Bastille Day celebrations. A check with the Patrouille de France indicates a takeoff at 9:49 PM for a flight of approximately one hour. (See the video Night Training of the Patrouille de France.) A southeast wind was recorded at that moment in Marignane on Météociel. The Patrouille de France therefore took off towards the southeast, into the wind, flying almost directly over our witness. It is therefore highly probable that this is the aircraft the witness observed, either just after takeoff, which is carried out in groups of four (as seen in the video), or after the formation takeoff. Focusing on all the navigation lights (at least four per aircraft, i.e., at least 32 points of light), the witness had the illusion of a single dark object carrying all the lights (a classic illusion known as a "shape illusion" or "outline illusion"). However, it should be noted that the times do not correspond exactly (the witness indicated 10:00 PM for a takeoff at 9:49 PM): was this a second pass after formation, or was the witness uncertain about the time reported? The witness reported seeing around one hundred lights, compared to 32 on the eight aircraft: this difference is significant. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of the Patrouille de France shortly after takeoff. The precise scenario of the observation could not be established due to the lack of minute-by-minute flight path data for the aircraft. Only a very strong coincidence between the events can be noted.

summary: Observation of the slow silent north-south movement of a luminous orange ball; disappearance behind the clouds: lack of information and cross-checks.
description: On Thursday, July 2, 2015, at 10:30 PM, several people observed the slow, silent movement of a luminous orange ball in a north-south direction, which disappeared behind the clouds. Only one eyewitness account was recorded. The observation of a fireball floating slowly in the sky along a seemingly random trajectory suggests a flaming object carried by the wind, such as a Thai lantern. The Infoclimat network indicated a light westerly wind at Mas-de-la-Barque, 5 km away. Météociel reports a weak, unstable wind recorded in Mende, at an altitude of 35 km. These factors, combined with the fact that the observation took place in the heart of a relatively narrow valley, make it impossible to determine the actual wind speed at low altitude. Winds at low altitude are very complex in mountainous areas. This Thai lantern hypothesis, which remains consistent with the observation, cannot be confirmed. GEIPAN considered a plasma-type phenomenon: however, there is no stormy context or seismic environment. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation of the passage of three consecutive bright points: observation of the Yaogan 20A, B and C satellite triplet
description: On July 1, 2015, between midnight and 12:15 a.m., a witness observed a bright point of light passing in the clear sky. Two seconds later, the witness observed two more bright points of light. The three points followed each other at the same speed and moved in exactly the same direction. No flashing or unusual noises were noted. The points disappeared due to the brightness of the Moon. The observation lasted between 15 and 20 seconds. No other reports were collected. Considered unusual and of moderate consistency (single witness, precise description), this case appears to be a case of mistaken identity involving a specific triplet of satellites: the Chinese military satellites Yaogan 20A, B, and C. The UFO exhibits all the typical characteristics of such a triplet: perfectly consistent brightness, trajectory, and timing. This case is classified as Class A, an observation of a triplet of Yaogan 20A, B, and C satellites.

summary: Multiple observations of the evolution of bright points in the night sky: certain observations of the 8 Alphajets of the Patrouille de France (PAF).
description: On July 1, 2015, starting at 10:30 PM, several people in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department observed luminous phenomena moving across the sky. Some witnesses described geometric shapes or a kind of vessel formed by points of light. The local press also reported the observations (see the last report). The observation of lights in the sky, arranged in regular geometric patterns, suggested an aerobatic team performing a training exercise or demonstration. A check with the Patrouille de France, based in Salon-de-Provence, confirmed that the team had exceptionally flown at night in this region on July 1 and 3: on July 1 to rehearse the demonstration that took place on July 3 for the graduation ceremony of the graduating classes. The silence that accompanied the observation is perfectly normal, as the noise of an aircraft seen head-on, more than a few kilometers away, is very faint. The eight Alpha Jets of the Patrouille de France are equipped with powerful searchlights visible from over 10 km along their flight path. When the aircraft turn, the searchlight beam changes direction, and observers located along the initial flight path see them suddenly disappear. Viewed from the side, these aircraft are only visible by their red or green position lights, which are insufficiently powerful to be seen at long distances. Viewed head-on, the approach is not perceptible; the aircraft appear motionless. Only lateral movement is perceived, and this may be slight. GEIPAN received reports of several sightings of the same patrol: from Valensole (04) and Sainte-Tulle (04) on July 1st, and from Villeneuve (04), 10 km away, on July 3rd. During the first days of July, GEIPAN has received similar sighting reports in Provence every year since 2008. In particular, one was reported in Villeneuve (04) on July 5, 2013. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": confirmed sightings of the 8 Alphajets of the Patrouille de France. The video from the witness in Sainte-Tulle will be posted on the website later following a temporary technical issue. See a video of the Patrouille de France flying at night over Paris.

summary: Long observation of two bright points moving very slowly one above the other: conjunction of Venus and Jupiter.
description: On June 30, 2015, between 11:30 PM and midnight, a witness observed two unusual lights in the sky, yellow-orange in color, positioned one above the other. He took several photographs. The observation of these slowly moving points of light immediately pointed to an astronomical origin. A check of the star chart indicated that that evening the planets Venus and Jupiter were visible at their closest point, just above the west-northwest horizon: this rare phenomenon of apparent proximity is called a conjunction. The attached star charts show the appearance of the phenomenon at 11:33 PM, and then at 11:55 PM when the planets were about to disappear below the horizon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," as perfectly explained: conjunction of Venus and Jupiter.

summary: Observation of the movement and disappearance of a point of light in the night sky: observation of the flash from the Iridium 52 satellite.
description: On June 25, 2015, at approximately 3:15 AM, a witness observed a bright point of light moving in a straight line for 10 to 15 seconds, which they identified as a satellite. They then saw another, larger, bright point of light, white and orange in color, moving at high speed, without blinking, and silently. This second point appeared to stop, then abruptly changed trajectory and disappeared. Data from the "Calsky" satellite pass simulator indicates that at that time, on that day, numerous satellites were visible on trajectories close to the north-south or south-south direction. The COSMOS 2428 satellite, visible on an apparent north-northwest to south trajectory between 3:00 AM and 3:12 AM, seems to be the one seen by the witness (though this is not certain, as other satellites could be the same), but it was another, much brighter, luminous phenomenon that caught their attention, on a south-north trajectory, which disappeared after 10 to 15 seconds. The Calsky report, and also that of Heavens-above, indicate that at 3:25 AM from Nantes, a flash from the Iridium 52 satellite was visible. The satellite orbits on a south-to-north trajectory. See information on Iridium satellite flashes. The witness then describes a right-angle turn, a sudden acceleration before disappearance: this type of description is common for satellites entering the Earth's shadow, or whose brightness suddenly ceases due to a change in orientation relative to the sun. The sudden decrease in brightness is subconsciously interpreted as a movement away. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: observation of the Iridium 52 satellite flash.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about ten colored light phenomena in the sky: probable observation of LED light balloons or Thae lanterns.
description: On June 24, 2015, at approximately 9:45 PM (the witness mistakenly indicated June 25 on the questionnaire), a person watching television was drawn outside by the movement of about ten bright, colored lights hovering above the hill and treetops. No noise was heard during the approximately fifteen-minute observation. Only one witness statement was recorded. The observation of flying lights crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests illuminated balloons (LED balloons or Thai lanterns), likely released nearby after a private party (Saint John's Day celebration?). The witness's account indicates a westward movement, but the drawing shows a movement from the NNE to the SSW (see the map reconstruction). The movement is observed generally from North to South, which is consistent with the Northwest to North wind recorded in Mulhouse-Bele (at 9 PM: light North wind of 7 to 11 km/h shifting to the West at 11 PM: Météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," probable observation of LED light balloons or Thae lanterns. The multiple colors and the long duration of the phenomenon point more towards LED balloons, as Thae lanterns most often have a dominant yellow-orange color due to the flame, which is the light source.

summary: Simultaneous observations of two luminous phenomena in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns, simultaneously with the observation of a bolide.
description: On June 20, 2015, around 11:00 PM, a motorist spotted three red-orange lights moving silently from north to south. At the same time, a bright green light was moving from east to west. This account describes two distinct phenomena: - Three red-orange lights moving slowly from north to south for several minutes. - A very bright green light moving very quickly westward. The witness naturally made the connection between the two phenomena, which turned out to be coincidental. Indeed, the first phenomenon had all the characteristics of Thai lanterns, frequently observed on Saturday evenings in the summer, released after weddings or other celebrations. Their southward movement is consistent with the northerly wind recorded at Lyon-St Exupéry Airport (see the weather report). The green phenomenon has all the characteristics of a fireball. It was observed simultaneously by several witnesses in the region: in the Ain, Saône-et-Loire, Nièvre, and Rhône departments. Unfortunately, the BOAM camera network did not record this fireball, probably due to cloud cover at the camera locations. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns, simultaneously with a fireball.

summary: Observation of the silent evolutions of an object with a changing shape in the clear sky: probable observation of a cluster of "Mylar" balloons.
description: On Tuesday, June 16, 2015, at approximately 9:25 a.m., two people on a beach were intrigued by the presence in the sky of a shape described as initially triangular, then round, composed of spheres, every other one luminous and flashing, and the other white or light gray and non-flashing. The UFO then formed a straight line of six distinct objects that finally disappeared at 10:10 a.m. as it gained altitude. No noise was heard during its movements in the sky. Only one witness statement was recorded. Based on the information gathered (see the investigation report), namely: - the appearance, color, brightness, and behavior of the UFO; - the favorable weather conditions: sunshine and a transitional, variable, and very light wind following a land breeze; - the favorable summer period. We can conclude that the UFO observed by the witnesses was certainly a cluster of Mylar balloons, tied together, with high reflective properties, and tossed about by the changing wind. This testimony is quite consistent: precise, but coming from a single witness and without a photograph. The observation is not particularly strange because the UFO is ultimately easily characterized, both in its appearance and its behavior. This case should be classified as a highly probable observation of a cluster of Mylar balloons.

summary: Observation and videos of a sphere in front of a star: observation of the planet Venus with a camcorder equipped with a strong zoom, with a focus shift causing an artifact in the image.
description: On June 15, 2015, a witness observed and filmed a bright star in the northwest sky around 11:15 PM but was intrigued by a sphere positioned in front of the star. No other witness statements were collected. This testimony is fairly consistent: although somewhat imprecise and coming from a single witness, it is accompanied by two usable videos. The only hypothesis considered is that of confusion with an optical defect in the out-of-focus image of Venus, captured with a high zoom (see the investigation report). Based on the evidence gathered, this case is classified as an A-level observation of Venus with a camcorder equipped with a high zoom, resulting in a focus misalignment causing an artifact in the image.

summary: Observation in different locations of silent evolutions in the sky of a large yellow-orange oval shape: probable observation of laser animation of a Sky Tracer or Sky Rose.
description: On June 14, 2015, between 3:28 and 3:45 AM, a witness observed a large, slightly elongated, yellow-orange oval object in the sky. The object silently moved and stopped repeatedly before disappearing. Joining a second person for carpooling, the two witnesses again observed the phenomenon and then saw it again in another town before it was lost from sight. The photos and video taken by the witness were unusable. Only one witness statement was collected. The phenomenon observed by the witnesses is entirely consistent with the hypothesis of confusion with a nightclub laser (sky tracker) used on a weekend night (see the investigation report). Such an establishment is located in the town of Jouy-sur-Morin, within the theoretical visibility range of such a sky tracker. Although the investigator was unable to demonstrate the use of such a laser from the nightclub on the evening of the observation, the explanatory hypothesis remains plausible given the other testimonial evidence. GEIPAN supports the hypothesis put forward by the witness himself. The objection he raised was the absence of beams rising from the ground. In fact, a laser beam may or may not be visible, depending on local weather conditions, with pollution also very likely playing a role, as well as the beam's intensity. The presence of fine particles suspended in the atmosphere is a crucial and essential factor in the formation of a light beam. These particles can be water droplets, microparticles of pollutants, etc. At the time of the observation, visibility was good (over 20 km) and no precipitation was observed. The conditions were therefore quite favorable for a laser beam not to be visible. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable laser animation of Sky Tracer or Sky Rose.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 7 to 8 orange spherical objects in the sky: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On Sunday, June 14, 2015, at approximately 5:10 a.m., a witness at his window was intrigued by the successive and silent passage of seven or eight luminous, spherical, orange objects across the sky. The observation lasted about ten minutes before they disappeared into the clouds. The witness managed to take photographs, but unfortunately, they were unreadable. The witness went to the police station. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. No explanation appeared in the local press in the following days. The observation of orange lights crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from southwest to northwest: if these were objects carried by the wind, it would have been a south or southeast wind. The Météociel weather report (see the weather document), taken at the exact location of the observation (Dijon airbase), indicates a highly variable and undetermined wind at 5:00 AM, light from the southeast at 4:00 AM to east at 6:00 AM. This weather report neither confirms nor denies that the observed objects were indeed wind-borne. Furthermore, GEIPAN requested a primary radar scan around Dijon at that time: the scan only indicates airliners at high altitude. The photos taken by the witness proved unusable, evidence of the faintness of the observed lights. Despite a testimony consistent with the presence of Thames lanterns, GEIPAN lacks sufficient evidence to confirm this hypothesis and classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observations at 23:20 then at 0:05 of the silent movement of an orange shape in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 13, 2015, at 11:20 PM, several people on a terrace observed an orange shape moving silently in a straight line in the sky. At 12:05 AM, two of the witnesses again saw the silent movement of an orange shape in the sky. Intrigued, they called the police, who dispatched a patrol. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked off nearby after a private party. The movement is observed first from Northwest to Southwest, then from East to West, which is consistent with the light North wind at 11 PM, shifting to Northeast around midnight, recorded at Orly (see the Météociel record for the day of observation at 11 PM and midnight; and that of Sunday, June 14th at 1 AM (Météociel). The GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the passage of a dark flying object with a fluorescent green halo and a lawnmower noise: lack of information.
description: On June 10, 2015, at approximately 12:20 AM, a person heard a low-pitched noise coming from outside. From their terrace, the witness observed a flying object for about three minutes, emitting a sound reminiscent of a lawnmower engine. The object was circular, dark in color, and surrounded by a fluorescent green halo. It came from the west and moved east in a straight line before disappearing into the low clouds on this stormy day. Only one witness account was collected. The description of a fluorescent green flying object making a lawnmower-like noise suggests a powered paraglider (paramotor) flying at night, its wing illuminated by a spotlight on the pilot's back (See an example at Night Flight with Headlamp). A paramotor club in Manosque was consulted to determine if this practice was common in the region. They replied that, to their knowledge, night paramotor flights are not practiced in the area. These flights are strictly regulated and tolerated only by special permit (see Free Flight Air Regulations) in clear weather and on nights close to a full moon—conditions not met that day (cloudy weather, last quarter moon). This hypothesis, which nevertheless corresponds quite well to the witness's description, cannot therefore be confirmed and is thus extremely unlikely, but not impossible. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the passage of about ten red-orange luminous points in the night sky; rapid extinction: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On June 8, 2015, at 2:30 a.m., a witness observed, through a skylight, approximately 10 red-orange lights moving silently in a straight line across the night sky. The lights gradually disappeared. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of red-orange lights crossing the sky in less than a minute on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The gradual appearance and disappearance of the lights is quite characteristic of these objects, which are launched in a chain and have a lifespan of only a few minutes (depending on the person who releases them). The movement is observed from East to South, which is consistent with the Northwest to North wind recorded in Neuilly-sur-Marne (see the Infoclimat report at Roissy, 20km away: a light Northwest wind is noted). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of three small silver-colored flying objects, moving from NW to SE, then suddenly moving vertically before disappearing: probable observation of balloons.
description: On June 6, 2015, at 5:30 PM, a witness observed three small, silvery flying objects moving from northwest to southeast, then suddenly rising vertically before disappearing. The local weather report indicated a light westerly wind at 4:00 PM, shifting to northwest at 5:00 PM, and then north at 6:00 PM. The objects' movement was consistent with the wind direction, suggesting they were simply small party balloons, silvered by the sun. The vertical departure and disappearance were likely caused by the balloons bursting at some altitude. GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of balloons.

summary: Observation of an object rotating in a circle in the sky then straight trajectory; disappearance hidden by vegetation: probable observation of a drone.
description: On Saturday, June 6, 2015, at 10:10 AM, a witness near an amusement park was intrigued by something circling in the sky. The UFO was making small circles, like a bird circling its prey or a drone. But the object suddenly changed course and headed northwest at a very steady speed and without noise. The object was then hidden by vegetation. Only one witness account was collected. This account reflects little of the strangeness perceived by the witness, as they had one or more possible explanations for their observation: a Northern Gannet, then a drone. Indeed, it could be either, although a drone (for recreational purposes) is a more compatible hypothesis for all phases of the observation. We were near an amusement park (Parc du Rademe) in broad daylight around 10:00 AM on a Saturday. There are likely many potential observers (the witness mentions other people present) of the phenomenon, both outside the park and, even more so, inside it. However, we have no other eyewitness accounts. The most probable scenario is that the witness saw something rather unremarkable, and that this unremarkable thing was a recreational drone (the witness's video shows nothing, but the audio indicates an exchange where one voice opposes the drone hypothesis, arguing that the drone pilot was not visible, an argument that is directly contested by another voice). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable drone sighting.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of red lights: lack of information.
description: On Friday, June 5, 2015, at approximately 11:15 PM, a witness and his wife observed, from their north-facing bathroom window, the slow and silent passage of red lights across the clear sky. The lights moved eastward. The witness reported his observation to the police. No other witness statements were collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a matter of minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked off nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from north to east, which may be consistent with the very weak and unstable wind observed in Salon-de-Provence at approximately 10 km (see the report METEOCIEL). Due to the lack of information regarding the local wind at the precise moment of observation, GEIPAN cannot confirm this hypothesis of Thai lanterns. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to the lack of a photograph and information on the local wind.

summary: Long observation of the presence of two dark shapes in the clear sky, one of which seems to be rotating around the other: observation of hot air balloons.
description: On June 5, 2015, at 9:10 PM, a witness observed two round, dark-colored objects in the clear sky from their fourth-floor balcony. The first UFO appeared relatively stable, while the second moved slowly in an arc, centered on the first object. The witness filmed the phenomenon for an extended period and then decided to drive closer, but lost sight of the objects (the witness's videos were later uploaded to the website due to a temporary technical issue). Only one witness account was collected. The shapes discernible in the videos strongly suggest two hot air balloons (or possibly gas balloons), whose gondola was not visually separated from the balloon due to the distance. The dual-body appearance (balloon + gondola) is confirmed by radiometric analysis (using the specialized software IPACO). The two partially reconstructed trajectories (from the video and the ground markers that appear there) are quite similar, except for a loss of angular altitude for one of the two shapes. These trajectories can, at times, give the illusion (to the witness's perception) that one shape is rotating around the other. These trajectories are reminiscent of objects carried by the wind, with a constant drift to the left of the witness. The decrease in altitude of both shapes is consistent with the need to land before nightfall (according to regulations). See the investigation report. It was not possible to finalize the exact identification of the aircraft at the origin; however, a large majority of the descriptive parameters from visual observation and the videos converge perfectly on this very simple and plausible explanation. The probability of a flight departing from Kehl (or even Offenburg) is high. Indeed, there are tourist flight companies operating in this area, located in the direction of the observation and at a distance consistent with the size of the hot air balloons seen in the video. The likelihood of an unnatural event is therefore very low, and even though there is only one witness, the evidence remains quite strong because the videos confirm their observation and allow for a very objective assessment of the observed phenomenon. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this observation as A: hot air balloon sighting.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of luminous spots in the night sky; filmed observation: observation of Thai lanterns.
description: During an outdoor party, about twenty people observed the slow movement of luminous white patches in the night sky. No noise was heard. A witness reported his observation, which he was able to film. The observation of luminous orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from North to South, which is consistent with the North wind recorded in Lyon Bron (see the link Météociel). The good quality video absolutely confirms this hypothesis: the luminous orbs can clearly be seen moving together, but without being connected; We have observed the extinction of some of them. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A" – observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of about ten luminous points in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On May 31, 2015, at 12:15 a.m., a witness observed a bright point moving from south to north across the sky. Very quickly, the witness saw more than a dozen white and red lights appear, moving silently. No other reports were collected. The observation of a series of red or white luminous shapes crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from South to North, which is consistent with the South to North wind recorded in Evreux (see the Météociel report for Evreux on the day of the observation). The triangular shape described by the witness could be the shape of the most illuminated part of the lantern: see the attached GEIPAN photo which shows the illuminated part as approximately triangular. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Low-altitude observation of lights followed by a dark V-shaped UFO that appears stationary: observation of a night-time tourist aircraft (pivot effect).
description: On May 31, 2015, at approximately 12:50-12:55 AM, two witnesses (T1, the driver, and T2, the passenger in his right-hand seat) working in a van were in the town of Silly-Le-Long (60) and entered the N2 highway heading northeast (towards Nanteuil-Le-Haudouin (60)). The night was clear, and the moon was behind them. While driving, they noticed white (steady) and red (flashing) lights at low altitude, which intrigued them. Familiar with the area and close to Roissy Airport, they were used to seeing aircraft, but what they saw appeared far too low and stationary, therefore abnormal. Slowing down, they noticed a massive, dark, V-shaped UFO on their left. Just after crossing the bridge known as the "Silly Bridge," only T1 was able to see the UFO. The observation while driving was made through the windshield, window, or rearview mirror; it lasted between one and four minutes before the UFO was obscured by the road's contours (downhill). Witnesses reported their observation in a police report and in a GEIPAN questionnaire. No other testimonies were collected. This case of observation was very interesting and represented a significant amount of work for GEIPAN: it ultimately constitutes a textbook case from several points of view, detailed below and in the attached investigation report. The witnesses observed white and red lights arranged horizontally in front of their vehicle. These appeared stationary. Upon reaching the level of the phenomenon, the witnesses observed a massive, very flattened V-shaped object. The element that makes the observation so strange (and motivates the witness's testimony) is the seemingly stationary levitation of a triangular-shaped object (not an airplane, as it was stationary, and not resembling a helicopter). The investigation reveals that a light aircraft was flying at low altitude (touch-and-go exercise) in the opposite direction to the movement of the witnesses' vehicle. Considerable investigative work, including on-site reconstruction with the witnesses and 3D simulations based on the aircraft's GPS navigation data and the witnesses' vehicle's trajectory, reveals a pivoting phenomenon. This means that the axis connecting the witnesses' position and that of the aircraft essentially pivoted on itself, potentially giving the witnesses who saw the aircraft the impression that it was fixed at the point of pivot. The pivoting effect of this aircraft is particularly evident and consistent with the visual observation of the UFO by witnesses when they passed closest to it. The pivot point is located at a bridge spanning the road, and it is also at this point that the stationary UFO was seen. The reconstructed position of the aircraft and the witnessed positions of the UFO are close angularly over a large part of the observation. The angular difference can reach 20 to 30 degrees, especially just after the bridge, but this remains consistent with an error in perception or memory, all the more so since a similar discrepancy appears between the two testimonies. This provides a key element in favor of the witnesses mistaking the aircraft for the real one. Furthermore, the witnesses did not distinguish the aircraft from the UAP, whereas the aircraft (if it was not the UAP) would only deviate by 20 or 30 degrees and emit its lights on a clear night from a distance of a few kilometers (or even much less at the pivot point). Similarly, the pilot of the aircraft (when questioned) did not notice any large object (as described by the witnesses) emitting lights (bright enough to be seen from several kilometers away by the witnesses) and located in the immediate vicinity of his landing path. These elements taken alone would allow this case to be classified as a case of mistaken identity with the identified aircraft. However, this case has been the subject of more in-depth analysis in relation to significant discrepancies between the witnessed observation and the appearance of the aircraft. Among the lights witnessed, some (color, flashing or not) cannot be explained by those of the aircraft. However, the most significant discrepancy regarding the lights comes from one of the witnesses (T1), and poor perception can be cited. In particular, T1 perceived (after passing under the bridge) slowly flashing white rectangles of light that should have been isolated flashes (flashcodes from the aircraft). The main discrepancy with the aircraft hypothesis lies in the angular sizes: the aircraft's angular size, at the witnessed observation point, is 0.7 arcseconds, while the reported size is between 14 and 27 arcseconds, depending on the witnesses and reconstruction methods. It is common to overestimate the angular sizes of a UFO, but the discrepancy here is very large. It should be noted, however, that these angular reconstructions of the UFO's size are obtained in absolute terms or without reliable ground reference. It is also noted that the most pronounced angular discrepancies (the white lights differ from the aircraft not only in their rectangular shape, but also in the angular distance between them) were observed by witness T1 alone, while he was behind the bridge and observing in less than ideal conditions, hardly conducive to accuracy (at night, looking backward while driving, and largely using the rearview mirror). Because of these discrepancies, the entire case was submitted to the GEIPAN panel of experts. The evidence supporting the misidentification of the aircraft prevailed, and the majority of experts validated the hypothesis of a significant perceptual illusion, an illusion considered explainable by night driving, observation in the rearview mirror, as well as fatigue or stress. These discrepancies are nonetheless significant and justify their inclusion in the GEIPAN database to inform current and future research on perception and memory issues (whether specific to UAPs or not). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: mistaken for an aircraft. A first 3D simulation video features several synchronized windows: - Main screen: simulation of the view from the witness's vehicle, the UAP (according to witness statements), and the aircraft (according to the GPS positions recorded in the aircraft). The aircraft's pivoting effect is evident, particularly when passing under the bridge. This pivot is indicated by a purple vertical arrow. - The visual appearance of the UAP is primarily based on witness T1's descriptions. The difference in position compared to the aircraft is noticeable, as is the angular size difference before and especially after the bridge (the two red markers don't point to anything specific but represent an angular difference of 20 degrees between their two positions). - Bottom right window: video taken inside the vehicle during a daytime reconstruction. - Bottom left window: zoom on the aircraft simulation. The other 3D simulation video shows the scene from the air. It does not, of course, include the witness's view of the UFO. This video allows us to appreciate the pivoting effect.

summary: Observation of the straight, silent and slow passage of a luminous orange object in the cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On May 30, 2015, at approximately 11:55 PM, a couple outside were intrigued by the slow, straight passage of a bright orange object across the cloudy sky. No unusual noise was heard. The object disappeared into the clouds. Only one witness account was recorded. GEIPAN analyzed several hypotheses for this observation: - Flare (reflection) on an Iridium satellite, visible at that precise moment (see Calsky report), but it was visible towards the southwest and moving in a northwest direction; moreover, the brightness would have been perceived as variable: this hypothesis is unlikely. - Flare on another, unlisted satellite: very improbable. - Fireball (meteorite re-entry into the atmosphere): the brightness, duration, and trajectory could fit, but the witness would probably have perceived variable brightness. No other observations were reported, nor were any camera recordings made (although the sky was cloudy!). - Thae lantern: the color, time, and date of the observation are consistent with this hypothesis, but the sustained northerly wind is a priori incompatible with the observed eastward movement (see Météociel). GEIPAN ultimately rejected none of these hypotheses due to a lack of verification or cross-checking. Additional information may eventually help determine the origin of the observed phenomenon.

summary: Sighting of a white object zigzagging between two planes: probable sighting of an object falling from a parachute drop plane.
description: On May 30, 2015, around 2 p.m., a witness observed parachute drop planes in the sky when he spotted an object between two of the planes, descending in a zigzag pattern with rapid, jerky movements. The object moved away at a phenomenal speed. GEIPAN contacted the "Abeille Parachutisme" club in Honfleur, which confirmed repeated rotations that day to drop parachutists; a club official stated that "During these rotations, objects sometimes escape from the drop planes, and these objects never follow a direct trajectory, but rather arabesques linked to air currents." Indeed, an object dropped from a plane in flight possesses the aircraft's own velocity. It is then subjected to: - gravity, which causes it to fall; - aerodynamic forces, which slow it down and make it spin; - the prevailing wind, which pushes it in its own direction; - and any local air currents, sometimes updrafts. The sum of these forces can explain the observed trajectory, which is quite chaotic due to the fact that the object in question is certainly very low density. The shape described by the witness (flat, rectangular) could be that of a piece of cardboard. GEIPAN classifies this case as B, a probable observation of an object falling from a parachute drop aircraft.

summary: Long observation of a bright colored point in the night sky: probable observation of the star Capella.
description: On May 26, 2015, from 9:45 PM to 10:00 PM, a witness observed a phenomenon he had seen a few weeks earlier and which intrigued him: a luminous point, "less bright than Venus," stationary, with changing colors (green, red, yellow), visible to the naked eye, appearing to make small circles around a fixed point. Only one witness account was collected. This account is not very precise: the time is likely incorrect, as the witness described and photographed the event at night, while the sun does not set until 10:07 PM. We will assume that the observation took place around 11:00 PM. The indicated direction of observation is rather imprecise: the witness's diagram best indicates the altitude above the horizon, which we will estimate to be on the order of 20ths of an arc. The weather report for Brest does indeed indicate a mostly clear sky and a northerly wind (see the report Météociel). The observation of a seemingly fixed point of light in the sky does indeed suggest a star (probably Capella, see attached star chart), but the witness reports a rotating red, green, and yellow light: it is this characteristic that seems strange, but which can be explained by the phenomenon of scintillation (see the article A Star?). Twinkle and the more or less rapid variations in color and appearance are often observed and are a source of misinterpretation; These variations are all the more noticeable when the star is low in the sky and the atmosphere is both clear and disturbed (high temperatures, wind), which was the case that day. The photograph, taken handheld with a camera equipped with a powerful zoom, shows a reddish arabesque typical of motion blur. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of the star Capella.

summary: Observation of a dark phenomenon with six lights in a circle in the sky: lack of information.
description: On May 25, 2015, at 7:58 PM, a witness observed a dark phenomenon in the sky, consisting of six lights arranged in a circle. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation report is particularly brief, the geographical details are imprecise, the account is very short, and there is no drawing or photograph. The circular shape described by the witness is not necessarily real; it could simply be the abstract outline of the six lights observed. These lights could be those of an airplane or a helicopter (a heliport is very close). GEIPAN did not process this case in time to obtain verification of air traffic at that moment. Due to a lack of detail in the witness statement and air traffic, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" for insufficient information and precision.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of two bright orange objects in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, May 23, 2015, between 11:00 PM and 11:15 PM, two people observed a very bright, orange object moving quickly and silently across the sky for approximately five minutes. A few minutes later, a second object with the same characteristics as the first was seen. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from west to east, which is consistent with the westerly wind recorded in Cognac (see the report on Météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of 5 to 6 balls of light seeming to delimit a shape; sudden extinction: lack of information.
description: In the early hours of Sunday, May 17, 2015, at 12:45 a.m., a witness closing a window was surprised to see five or six colored balls of light passing silently across the clear sky. These lights appeared to outline a dark object. The observation lasted only a very short time, and the lights suddenly went out. The witness described a "gray and metallic" object equipped with "six large colored balls of light." If we accept that the witness may have experienced the classic form illusion (see the article on Gestalt psychology), it is possible that only the luminous balls were real, but not the gray object. The observation of luminous orbs crossing the sky in a straight line on a weekend night suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The disappearance of the orbs could correspond to them going out or passing behind a building. As the observation was very brief, and the witness did not describe the direction of movement, it is impossible to verify if the movement was consistent with the wind. It would be surprising if it were a drone, which is very difficult to pilot safely at night in an urban environment; moreover, drones tend to have non-linear trajectories. GEIPAN has not received any other reports that could correspond to this same phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of precise information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of the silent passage in the night of a V-shaped formation of luminous points and detachment of one of these points: probable observation of birds (migrants in formation).
description: On May 17, 2015, at approximately 11:16 PM, a witness observing the night sky was intrigued by the appearance of a series of bright points of light (the witness counted up to eight) which gradually formed a large V shape. The entire formation flew silently at low altitude. One of the points detached from the formation, and the whole thing disappeared. No other witness statements were collected. The witness submitted their statement to GEIPAN on June 16, 2015, using the GEIPAN questionnaire. A meeting with the witness took place on December 15, 2015, for a cognitive interview and a reconstruction of the event. The strangeness of the case stems from the V-shaped formation of the lights and their sequence of appearance and disappearance. V-shaped formations are rarely seen in more than two scenarios: - a patrol of aircraft or drones flying in formation; - a group of migrating birds. Regarding the patrol of aircraft or drones, it is surprising to see them at night in an urban environment, and why would the lights of the devices have followed such a sequence? The hypothesis of a group of migrating birds, on the other hand, explains this sequence: - we are slightly outside of a migration period, but gulls and seagulls sometimes move at night when their roost is disturbed, for example, and they then fly at low altitude; their white bodies, even barely illuminated by urban lights, can give a luminous (and especially "white") impression. It could also be ducks that move at night and frequently form V-formations; - The formation's entry into a slightly brighter area could have produced this immediate appearance for each bird (from shade to sufficient light) and a gradual one for the V. The observed sequence of light would indicate that the V entered from the left, following a brighter area; - everything disappeared suddenly, which would indicate that the V exited the bright area upon encountering a shadow front (or a less bright one) fairly transverse to its movement, whereas the brighter front causing the appearance was more aligned with its movement; - a bird could very well have detached itself from the formation for a brief moment. This is more unusual but not contradictory, especially since we don't know how long this detachment lasted just before the disappearance. This hypothesis was explained with the help of an ornithological expert. However, it was not possible to understand how the neighborhood's lighting configuration could produce such a sharp and linear contrast at the birds' altitude. This would mean that a relatively slight change in lighting can cause a white bird to appear or disappear in a night sky, or that a particular event that evening (it was a Sunday) led to specific lighting patterns. The testimony is consistent. It is precise and was able to be reconstructed on site. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of birds (migratory flocks in formation). The explanation of a bird phenomenon is recent at GEIPAN; it is possible that some past unexplained (or poorly explained) observations, including less unusual ones (without this particular sequence of lights), could in fact be related to this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of multiple passages of white glows with a slight veil behind them in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On Friday, May 15, 2015, at approximately 10:00 PM, a driver and his passenger observed numerous flashes of white light with a slight veil behind them in the night sky. The observation lasted for 7 minutes over 8 kilometers on country roads. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was collected. This sighting (incorrectly considered a fireball by the witness) occurred approximately one hour after sunset, in the last light of twilight, just 10 km from the Camargue ponds and their thousands of large birds: it was the end of the "evening migration" when the last birds left the ponds and returned to their roosts inland. This hypothesis of birds was indeed considered by the witnesses, but dismissed because they thought of nocturnal birds, which is probably not the case, especially given the multiple sightings. However, GEIPAN has not collected any concrete elements to confirm this hypothesis, and the description made by the witnesses is very succinct (white glow with a slight veil at the rear), GEIPAN classifies this case "C" due to lack of cross-checking.

summary: Observation in the night sky of the evolution of 12 to 15 bright round objects: lack of information.
description: In August 2015, a witness reported an observation made during the night of May 9-10, 2015, at 3:40 AM. This person observed 12 to 15 bright objects in the sky. These objects were round and light in color. They were arranged in a semicircle. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted two minutes. Only one witness statement was collected. This statement provides insufficient information for a full investigation, even though the observation of numerous orbs on a weekend night (including, in this case, in a semicircle) suggests the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent passage of an orange sphere in the night sky: probable sighting of a Thai lantern.
description: On Saturday, May 9, 2015, around 10:30 PM, a witness observed the slow movement of an orange sphere across the night sky for 10 seconds. The sphere lost intensity as it moved away. No other witnesses reported seeing the sphere. The observation of an orange ball crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests a Thai lantern, probably licked nearby after a private party (perhaps licked from the leisure park: see map). The movement was observed from west to southwest, which is consistent with the light westerly wind recorded in Albi (see map and data from Météociel). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Very long observation of a very bright spherical shape on a downward trajectory in the sky: certain observation of the planet Venus, very low on the horizon.
description: On May 7, 2015, at 11:15 PM, a witness observed a particularly bright, spherical object in the sky, which intrigued them. The UFO was moving along a downward vertical trajectory. The observation lasted one hour and ended when the UFO was obscured by clouds or fog. Only one witness statement was recorded. The witness reported observing the UFO to the east-southeast, "towards the Basilica of St. Martin," which is contradictory. This basilica is located to the northwest of their position (see the investigation report). Given the objective evidence gathered, we can conclude that this case should be classified as Category A, as a confirmed observation of the planet Venus, located very low on the horizon.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of a bolide, result of the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid probably originating from the Eta-Aquariids swarm.
description: The witness observed, very early in the morning, a very bright object moving silently. Its trajectory resembled that of a shooting star. The observation of a "very bright thing" crossing the sky at high speed, appearing much lower than a shooting star, strongly suggests a fireball. The BOAM network (see attached document) reported at 2:27 UTC (4:27 civil time) a video recording of a seemingly similar phenomenon, captured by a camera located in Gretz-Armainvilliers in Seine-et-Marne, heading east-northeast at an elevation of approximately 50°. This time of year is quite favorable for observing this type of phenomenon (the Eta Aquarid meteor shower), and GEIPAN received other similar reports during the same period. GEIPAN classifies this case "A": observation of a bolide, result of the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid probably originating from the Eta-Aquariids swarm (coming from the direction of the constellation Aquarius).

summary: Observation of strong colored lights in the sky and silent movement: observation of an airplane.
description: On May 7, 2015, at approximately 9:45 PM, two people were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the sky. Powerful lights (white, red, and orange) appeared to be rotating around an object. No noise was heard during the movements. A check of air traffic in the direction of the witness's observation using the FlightRadar24 website indicated that a Ryanair flight, descending at an altitude of approximately 2,000 meters, was approaching from the north (southeast heading) and at 9:40 PM made a course change to 90° to the northeast, heading towards Strasbourg Airport (see the FlightRadar screenshots in the appendix). After this course change, it appeared to be "with its back to the observers," and therefore almost stationary, as its movement was difficult to perceive. The witness, however, only noticed this movement towards the end of the observation. This movement is entirely consistent with the witness statement: "It arrived from the NE at a fairly high speed and suddenly hovered." During this phase of flight, the aircraft's lights were multiple: very powerful landing lights, but directed forward; fixed green, red, and white position lights; and, most importantly, two types of flashing lights: red anti-collision lights and white strobe lights. These two types of lights flash approximately once per second but are not synchronized, sometimes giving the impression of a chain of flashing lights. The silence described by the witnesses is not surprising: the aircraft was 15 or 20 km away, the engines are at low power during this descent phase and therefore relatively quiet; moreover, the witness's surroundings do not appear to be very quiet: the television is on, and a noticeable background noise can be heard in the video. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the aircraft of Ryanair flight 5061.

summary: Observation of numerous traces in the sky: definite observation of contrails from airplanes.
description: On May 6, 2015, around 9:00 PM, a witness was intrigued by contrails in the sky. He took photographs. Only one witness account was reported. Given the evidence gathered—namely, the appearance of the phenomenon is consistent with that of many other examples of contrails created by airliners and illuminated by the setting sun in a suitable atmospheric layer, and the optical effect of perspective—we can conclude that the phenomena observed by the witness are very likely persistent contrails created by airliners (see the investigation report). This witness account is very consistent: precise and accompanied by numerous photos, but coming from a single witness. The observation is not very unusual because UFOs are immediately identifiable. This case is classified as a confirmed observation of aircraft contrails.

summary: Observation of a triangular shape passing in the sky, delimited by fixed or flashing colored lights: probable observation of an airplane passing by.
description: On May 4, 2015 (the witness confirms the date), around 4:00 AM, a witness, upon waking, was intrigued by the passage of a triangular shape across the sky, indicated by the presence of lights at its corners. The object passed at a right angle in front of his terrace, at the same altitude as a low-flying aircraft. The witness heard the sound of a low-flying plane. No other witness accounts were collected. This case report describes a phenomenon with many characteristics of an aircraft: fixed yellow-white lights, flashing red and white lights, apparent size, and noise. However, the witness, who could not discern a fuselage or wings, described it as triangular, which led him to find the craft strange. When an observer sees a cluster of lights, it is common to interpret this cluster as an object simply defined by those lights. This illusion, called a shape or outline illusion, occurs with independent lights (as with lanterns) and also with airplanes when the wings are poorly visible: the witness then reconstructs a black volume limited by the visible lights. If the witness did not see the wings or fuselage of the airplane, it may be because their angle of observation did not allow it (wings seen edge-on), or more likely because the airplane itself was very dark, as is the case, for example, with large military transport aircraft. The centerline of one of the runways at Le Bourget Airport does indeed pass through Épinay-sur-Seine (7.5 km). The Météociel report notes a southwest wind at Roissy: planes are therefore taking off westward towards Epinay (see the Météociel report). GEIPAN classifies this case as category B: probable aircraft sighting. Unfortunately, GEIPAN did not process this sighting quickly enough to verify with air traffic control whether there was indeed a flight at that time.

summary: Observation of the slow passage of a scintillating object in the Parisian sky in the morning: probable observation of a child's balloon.
description: On May 4, 2015, at 10:05 AM, a witness at home observed a shimmering object moving slowly across the sky. No other reports were received. This shimmering object, with its shifting reflections, moving slowly across the Paris sky in broad daylight, had all the characteristics of a fairground balloon (a Mylar-coated balloon) that had escaped its owner's control. These balloons come in a wide variety of shapes and colors (search "Mylar balloon" on Google Images); once licked, they spin, producing highly variable appearances and reflections, as seen in the witness's photos. The witness's account was not precise enough to determine the balloon's trajectory and its correlation with the local wind. GEIPAN classified this case as "B": probable observation of a child's balloon.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of three bright orange luminous balls: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On Sunday, May 3, 2015, at 1:30 a.m., a witness observed three very bright, vivid orange orbs silently passing across the night sky. The witness managed to grab a camera to film the sighting, but was disappointed with the video quality and did not provide it to GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Astronomical Phenomena). No other reports were collected. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night initially suggested the possibility of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from east to west, which seems inconsistent with the light southerly wind recorded in Caen (6 km away), as the terrain could not explain such a sharp change in direction at a distance of only 6 km. The late evening weather report for Caen indicates a sustained southeasterly wind with rain (see the report from Météociel). The rain has made the atmosphere very clear (see the horizontal visibility indicator at 55km), and has thus made the lanterns appear brighter. At the time of observation, there was a light southerly wind (see the report Météociel). The movement of Thai lanterns follows the local wind: it is very regular if the wind is steady and the terrain is flat, more turbulent if the area is subject to convection currents from various sources. The witness was disappointed by the video's quality: the brightness remains low, which proves that the objects were not as bright as they appeared; the witness, in complete darkness under an overcast sky, perceived the lights as very bright. The video makes the orbs appear whiter due to the effect of automatic white balance; the diamond shape corresponds to an out-of-focus (blurry) image. The diamond shape is actually the shape of the camera's diaphragm. Due to wind conditions incompatible with the observed movement, GEIPAN cannot confirm the hypothesis of Thai lanterns. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information (video, other witnesses) and corroboration.

summary: Quick observation of the silent and straight passage of a dark and triangular shape in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On Friday, April 24, 2015, between 10:30 and 11:00 PM, a father and his children were lying on the terrace gazing at the starry sky. Suddenly, the father's gaze was drawn to a moving shadow in the sky. The witness perceived "a dark, delta-wing-like shape moving at very high speed southward" on a straight trajectory. No unusual noise was heard during the 2-3 second observation. The witness lost track of it in the distance, obscured by light pollution. No other witness statements were collected. This very brief observation of a dark object could be consistent with the sighting of a nocturnal bird of prey (owl, eagle owl) flying over the observer. The witness lives on the edge of a forest, which makes this hypothesis plausible. However, GEIPAN has no evidence to support this hypothesis. The witness suspects a stealth aircraft: this type of aircraft is stealthy from radar but not particularly quiet, and most often flies at high altitude. Due to the lack of corroboration and the brevity of the testimony, GEIPAN classifies this case as category "C".

summary: Brief observation of the passage of an object illuminated by three white LEDs and a green light in its center; no noise: lack of information.
description: On April 22, 2015, at approximately 1:20/1:30 AM, two people very briefly observed an object (triangular or circular in shape) with three white LEDs and a green light in its center moving across the clear sky. No unusual noise was heard. No trail or halo was seen. The object moved along a downward curve. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation of a triangle formed by three points of light is atypical, but very brief: less than three seconds. GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study of Astronomical Phenomena) would have liked to conduct an on-site investigation, but because the witness was a minor, parental consent was required; GEIPAN was unable to obtain it. This very brief observation, especially since it occurred through a window, proved to provide relatively little reliable information. GEIPAN hypothesized that a drone had flown, or that a light from the bedroom, carried by one of the witness's guests, had reflected off the window. Without an on-site investigation, the validity of these hypotheses could not be verified. GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to a lack of reliable information and corroboration.

summary: Observation of a light of all colors in the sky: observation of the star Sirius.
description: On April 21, 2015, at 9:30 PM, a witness observed a "flashing" light of all colors in the sky for five minutes. The object disappeared after a few minutes, which the witness used to film the phenomenon. After confirming with the witness, it was determined that the object was located above Mont-Saxonnex (74), to the southwest. The witness observed the phenomenon again two days after the first sighting. This observation perfectly matches the observation of the star Sirius at sunset, with a strong twinkling phenomenon (interaction of light with atmospheric particles), common on this brightest star in the sky. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the star Sirius.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of two colored luminous phenomena in the night sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, April 18, 2015, at 11:45 PM, a witness on his property observed two luminous objects, one white and one red, moving across the night sky for two minutes. The two objects appeared to be flying one behind the other. No unusual noises were heard during the observation, which ended at 11:53 PM. The witness reported his observation to the gendarmerie in a letter. The investigation determined that no unusual weather phenomena occurred that evening, no fireworks displays were organized by local town halls in the area, and no military training flights took place. The initial inquiries did not yield any other eyewitness accounts. The observation of white and red lights crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from the Northwest (Bailleval) towards the West (see map), which is consistent with the Northeast wind speed of 20 to 30 km/h recorded at Creil (see the day's report Météociel). However, some elements of the observation report do not fit well with the hypothesis of objects carried by the NE wind: - the objects stop above the marsh: this fact implies that the wind weakens at this point, or changes direction: this remains possible given the particular topography of this especially damp valley. - one of the objects moves upwards towards Ars, due west: this description could correspond to the gradual extinction of the lantern; Witnesses often interpret this decrease in brightness as a sign of movement. - The second object moves out of the witness's field of vision at very high speed towards Bailleval (that is, northwards, therefore against the wind): this is completely contradictory to an object carried by the wind, unless we consider that it is also a perceptual illusion when the lantern goes out. - The return of the second object would then be a third lantern launched from the same location, towards Bailleval, shortly after the first two. In conclusion, after taking into account the possibility of perceptual illusions when the lights go out, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of 6 or 7 luminous red-orange balls in the night sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On April 18, 2015, around 11:30 p.m., a driver was alerted by his son in the back seat to the presence of a red light in the sky. Looking in the rearview mirror, he saw six or seven luminous red-orange orbs moving in formation and seemingly following the vehicle. The witness stopped his car and observed the phenomenon until it disappeared completely, except for one orb. He had time to take a few photos. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in just a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked off nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from the Northeast to the Northwest, which is consistent with the Northeast wind recorded in Le Mans on Météociel, indicating a sustained NE wind. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of two flashing white lights in the sky: probable sighting of two airplanes.
description: On April 14, 2015, at approximately 9:50 PM, a witness observed two flashing lights moving quite quickly towards the southwest for about a minute. In the final direction of observation (west), the civilian flight log "Flighradar" showed three aircraft at the time indicated by the witness, located approximately 80 km away. Two of these aircraft were very close but at different altitudes, which could give the impression of overlapping. At this distance, they appeared to the witness at an elevation of about 10 arcseconds (20 times the lunar diameter). At this distance, the contrails of the aircraft were still clearly visible (at sunset), but not necessarily the strobe lights. However, the witness described a movement from south to west, at an apparent speed faster than airliners at high altitude (10 to 12 km). It is more likely that the witness saw two military aircraft, at a distance of approximately 4 to 8 km. The area is a frequent maneuvering zone, and Tuesday is a fairly favorable day. The Météociel report for Nemes indicates very clear weather and a light south to southwest wind (see the weather). The silence perceived by the witness is not inconsistent with the presence of an aircraft more than 4 km away; the perceived noise depends on the type of aircraft, engine speed, relative wind, and the ambient noise level of the witness. The video taken by the witness at the end of the observation clearly shows two sources of flashing lights, each flashing once per second, typical of strobe lights (see the observation video). The green or red position lights were not seen by the witness: firstly, they are not necessarily illuminated during military operations, and secondly, beyond a certain distance, these low-power lights are difficult to perceive next to the powerful strobes. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of two aircraft.

summary: Prolonged observation of two luminous colored phenomena in the sky: probable observation of celestial bodies.
description: On April 13, 2015, from 10:10 PM to 11:30 PM, a witness observed two colored luminous phenomena in the sky, first with the naked eye and then with binoculars. The observation, lasting over an hour, of luminous, multicolored objects in the sky, moving slowly in accordance with the Earth's rotation (1/15th of an hour), is typical of celestial observation. In this case, the directions indicated by the witness were not very precise but seemed to point to the stars Procyon and Capella, which are, however, less bright than Sirius, or especially than the planets Venus and Jupiter (see the sky charts created with the "Stellarium" software for Albi at 10:10 PM and 11:10 PM). The strange aspect of the observation lies in the description of changing colors and a shape resembling a sea urchin's shell. Today's Meteociel report indicates high temperatures for this time of year (27th): see the weather. These significant temperature variations induce turbulence in the atmosphere, causing strong twinkling, particularly visible with binoculars. It is these somewhat unusual atmospheric conditions that gave this appearance to the observed celestial bodies. This type of twinkling also occurs with strong winds, especially warm ones. It should also be noted that the witness observed with hiking binoculars (10x25) at a high magnification of 10x, but with a small aperture of 25mm, poorly suited to astronomical observation (a lower magnification of 7 or 8 and a larger aperture of 50mm are preferred for this purpose). These binoculars can induce shape and color aberrations under these particular conditions; the high magnification makes a stable, handheld view very difficult. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: observation of celestial bodies. A more precise account, specifying the relative positions of the celestial bodies, would have allowed for more accurate identification of the objects in question.

summary: Observation of an intense white flash followed by three red balls in the starry sky: observation of the Chinese military satellite triplet Yaogan 16A, B and C.
description: On April 13, 2015, at 9:55 PM, a witness, who regularly observes the night sky and is familiar with the stars, first saw an intense and brief white flash, followed by three static red orbs forming a triangle. The phenomenon was silent. Its intensity, initially strong, diminished until the phenomenon disappeared. The observation lasted less than 10 seconds. Only one witness account was collected. Of moderate strangeness and consistency (single witness, precise description), this case turned out to be a case of mistaken identity involving a particular triplet of satellites: the Chinese military satellites Yaogan 16A, B, and C (see the investigation report). The UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) exhibited all the typical characteristics of such a triplet: perfectly consistent brightness, trajectory, and timing. This case is classified as Class A, a case of mistaken identity involving the Yaogan 16A, B, and C satellite triplet.

summary: Brief observation of the silent passage of a very bright object in the clear sky: probable observation of a mylar balloon.
description: On Monday, April 13, 2015, at approximately 10:45 AM, a person sitting with friends on a café terrace observed a very bright object silently passing across the clear sky. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness described a bright, metallic-looking object in the sunlight, rotating and crossing a portion of the sky in less than a minute. The image suggested a Mylar balloon (a metallic fairground balloon) had escaped its owner's grasp. Since the witness was unable to identify the object, they could not accurately estimate its distance or size. As is often the case, these elements were overestimated: a 50 cm object seen from 100 meters appears exactly the same to the observer as a 5 m long object of the same shape seen from 1000 meters. The witness looked towards the south-southwest (azimuth 220°) and observed a movement from their left to their right: the object could have been flying from the southeast to the northwest, but also from east to west. The distance would not be perceptible in such a short observation. The Météociel report for Orleans indicates a variable wind from NE to East (see the Météociel report). Although not exactly along the SE to NW axis perceived by the witness, an East or even NE wind can push a balloon from the observer's left to right. The end of the observation (spiral descent) could correspond to the balloon deflating due to overpressure caused by the altitude. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a Mylar balloon.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a dark object in the shape of a flattened lens at low altitude: probable observation of a small aircraft flying within visual range at low altitude, seen against the light.
description: On April 12, 2015, between 1:30 p.m. and 2:15 p.m., a witness on a terrace was observing aircraft high in the sky when he saw a dark, flattened lens-shaped object moving very quickly at low altitude in a straight line. The object disappeared from the witness's view, hidden by the landscape. Only one witness statement was recorded. A radar air traffic control report was requested. The resulting flight paths were overlaid on the Google Earth map (with an accuracy of approximately 500m): a fairly significant amount of air traffic of small aircraft flying under Visual Flight Rules (VFR) is indeed visible, including a particular trajectory that seems quite suitable for observation (see the radar map document and in particular the red trace that passes from East to West of Plaisir from 12:10:48 UTC (2:10 PM local time) to 12:12:18 PM). This aircraft climbs slowly from East to West from 400m (Z12) to 500m (Z16), and flies at around 160 km/h (89 to 75 knots).
