The passage in front of the witness lasted less than a minute, compared to the 30 seconds of observation indicated by the witness. This aircraft, probably small, appeared to the witness to be further away, and therefore faster, than it actually was. As the The witness is looking south, close to the zenith; the aircraft, backlit by the sun, appears black. Due to the low angle of attack, the wings, seen edge-on, may be invisible. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of a small aircraft in visual flight, at low altitude, seen against the sun. Due to the uncertainty surrounding the time of observation, this case is not classified as A.

summary: Successive observations of three luminous phenomena in the sky: very probable observations of reflections of the sun on an airplane and on satellites.
description: On April 11, 2015, at 9:41 PM, a witness observed a series of three intriguing luminous phenomena from his kitchen window. A large white flash occurred at 8:41 PM to the east, at an elevation of approximately 45°. Several high-altitude aircraft were observed in the direction of observation at that time (see the Flightradar24 report). The sun had set about twenty minutes earlier, but the aircraft, at an altitude of 13,000 meters, were still in sunlight: a temporary reflection of the sun on the underside of the aircraft's wings or fuselage could have caused this temporary flashing effect. The aircraft itself, being too far away, was invisible to the naked eye. - An orange flash, lower in the sky, moving for 2 seconds: the description corresponds well to a flash from an Iridium satellite, seen at low elevation (reddening in the atmosphere): the Calsky record (attached) indicates two Iridium flashes in this direction at very close intervals: one at 8:46 PM, with a magnitude of -2.5, the other at 8:55 PM, probably too low to be visible in a mountainous area. - A third, very short flash of half a second, the origin of which could be the reflection of the sun on one of the many satellites visible at that time. This observation is classified as "B": very probable observation of reflections of the sun on an aircraft and on satellites.

summary: Observations by many people of a bolide, resulting from the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: The phenomenon observed on Thursday, April 9, 2015, around 7:10 a.m., was simultaneously witnessed by numerous people spread across southwestern France (Foix, Montauban, Saint-Orens, etc.) and western France (La Chapelle-sur-Erdre, Plozevet), from Ariège to Finistère. Witnesses in the Spanish Pyrenees also reported sightings (see the summary table of testimonies collected on this phenomenon). This phenomenon is called a BOLIDE, an old term meaning "ball-shaped," a term more often used to describe a very fast vehicle, in reference to the speed of the observed phenomenon (see the general explanation of the phenomenon on bolide). Due to the intensity of the light, most witnesses, seeing this type of phenomenon for the first time, thought it was something very close, a few kilometers away, or even less; In reality, this luminous phenomenon occurs between 80 and 20 km altitude, which is why witnesses hundreds of kilometers away can see it simultaneously (See the report on a similar recent event: A large fireball observed over Catalonia, Spain). In the case of the fireball of Thursday, April 9, 2015, given the trajectories described by witnesses, it probably occurred over the Atlantic Ocean, about a hundred kilometers from the coast (a rough approximation). The fragments of the meteoroid, ranging in size from a few millimeters to centimeters, most likely fell back into the Atlantic Ocean. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: Observation of a fireball, the result of a meteoroid's atmospheric reentry. See other accounts on the following websites: Ciel des hommes, Actucity, France bleu, La Depeche with archive image. And a video on Dailymotion.

summary: Observation of the passage and evolution of a white flying object with V-shaped wings in the clear sky: probable observation of a radio-controlled model aircraft.
description: On April 8, 2015, at approximately 7:15 PM, a witness sitting on a sofa under a skylight observed a bright white flying object with no visible logo. The object, with V-shaped wings, made a curve, then climbed vertically very rapidly, appearing as a white line against the clear sky. It then disappeared from the witness's view. The observation lasted one minute, allowing the witness to sketch the object. The witness's description, the described shape, and the behavior suggest a radio-controlled model aircraft, of the flying wing type (see a model of this type, with the shape described by the witness, in the video radio-controlled flying wing model aircraft with astonishing flight performance). The witness lives less than 150 meters from a sports area, quite suitable for model aircraft flying, therefore within range of a radio transmitter and in view; Wednesday late afternoon is a fairly favorable time. Without being able to verify this information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a radio-controlled model aircraft.

summary: Prolonged observation of bright points in the sky moving rapidly: observation of a series of passes by military aircraft training for night flight.
description: On April 7, 2015, at 10:30 PM, a witness spotted several bright lights in the sky that appeared to be moving very quickly. The phenomena remained visible for over an hour, at which point the witness ceased observation. She provided her video to the newspaper Sud-Ouest. A northwesterly wind of 20 to 30 km/h was recorded in Cognac: weather. GEIPAN (the French group that investigates and protects against aviation-related incidents) contacted military air traffic control, which provided a series of radar traces of aerial activity corresponding to circuits around the Cognac-Chateaubernard military base (see the map showing the aircraft trajectories). Air Base 709 (Cognac-Chateaubernard) confirmed significant night flight training traffic that evening (the same evening as the observation, the witness had inquired with the same base about any traffic that evening and received a negative response: the person they spoke to may not have been qualified to answer public questions about military activities). GEIPAN classifies this case as Category "A," as it is clearly identified by a series of passes of military aircraft conducting night flight training.

summary: Observation of an intense and fixed light in the sky: observation of the planet Venus.
description: On April 5, 2015, between 9:30 p.m. and 11:00 p.m., a motorist spotted an intense, fixed, elongated light in the sky. He stopped several times along the way to observe the luminous phenomenon in the clear sky. This prolonged observation of a very bright point in the sky, which seemed to follow the observer but remained positioned in the west at the same elevation, is typical of observing a celestial body. The planet Venus was particularly bright at that time, and exactly in the direction indicated by the witness. The witness, contacted by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Astronomical Research), verified a few days later that Venus was indeed present in that direction in the sky. The elongated shape, described by the witness in his first observation, was not observed again during the verification of Venus a few days later. To explain this shape, one could consider visual fatigue on the part of the witness or a particular atmospheric effect that might have distorted the point image of the planet. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the planet Venus.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent flight of an unknown aircraft at very low altitude: certain observation of a military aircraft.
description: On April 3, 2015, at 4:15 PM, a driver and her two passengers were intrigued by the slow, silent, and low-altitude flight of an aircraft they did not recognize. GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) consulted military air traffic control regarding this observation; it turned out that, indeed, that day at 4:00 PM, a military aircraft was flying at a very low altitude (2,100 feet, or approximately 700 meters) over Lapeyrouse, on a north-northwest heading. Despite discrepancies between the witnesses' statements and the information provided by air traffic control regarding the time of the event (15 minutes) and the estimated altitude, the exceptional presence of this aircraft perfectly explains the witnesses' observation. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A," indicating a confirmed sighting of a military aircraft.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon: observation of the passage of a bolide caused by the entry into the atmosphere of a natural meteoroid which fragments.
description: On March 15, 2015, at approximately 8:45 PM, numerous people observed a bright colored object passing across the sky. GEIPAN (the French Aerospace Lab) received several reports, including one from a pilot. This phenomenon, observed by hundreds of people in northeastern France and especially in Germany and Switzerland, is clearly a fireball. A fireball is a phenomenon occurring when a large object (weighing over 100 grams and measuring from a few centimeters to 1 meter in diameter) enters the atmosphere. This produces a large trail of light capable of illuminating the landscape for several seconds. This fireball was also recorded by several cameras (see, among others, BOAM), which allows for a precise characterization of its trajectory and, consequently, its natural origin: it is a meteoroid, a small rocky body that crossed Earth's orbit. The size of this object at the entrance is very difficult to determine, between 100g and 10kg. This fireball was unusual in that it was observable for almost 10 seconds due to its relatively low trajectory. The fireball's trajectory went from Northeast to Southeast, approximately directly over Stuttgart as far as Zurich. GEIPAN received five eyewitness accounts from ground crew and two from pilots in flight (see table and maps). It should be noted that one of the pilots, flying north, said that the phenomenon "fell" the aircraft, even though it was more than 200 km away. This illusion of proximity is a constant in all fireball sightings; it does not spare pilots. Moreover, at high altitudes, atmospheric haze is nonexistent, making it even more impossible to estimate the distance of a powerful, unknown luminous phenomenon. An excellent analysis of all observations of this event, compiled by the American Meteor Association, is available at: U-Sphere. GEIPAN classifies this case as 'A': a phenomenon perfectly identified as a bolide, caused by the fall of a natural meteor.

summary: Observation of two luminous phenomena in the sky and filmed by the witness: observation of planes descending.
description: On March 12, 2015, at 7:45 PM, a witness observed two lights. Initially stationary, the first light moved in a direction and disappeared behind buildings, soon followed by a second light which followed the exact same trajectory. The witness observed from Courbevoie, 85 degrees to the right of the Total tower in La Défense (see map), indicating a northwest direction. A check of civil air traffic (see Flightradar report) shows that at that precise moment, flights AFR1159 and AF1281, descending towards Roissy, were in the witnesses' line of sight. These flights then turned slightly north. The video taken by the witness is entirely consistent with this explanation. It should be noted that an aircraft seen preparing to land, therefore viewed head-on, can be seen from more than 20 km away thanks to its landing lights, which make the flashing lights and position lights (green and red) almost invisible to the naked eye. When the aircraft's axis is no longer aligned with the observer's direction, these powerful lights, which have a relatively narrow beam, are no longer visible to the observer. See the article airplane?. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of aircraft in descent.

summary: Observation of a group of red lights moving in the sky: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On March 7, 2015, at 12:05 a.m., a witness, while driving, observed a group of nine red lights in the sky above a nearby hill. The lights appeared to be moving silently and rapidly in formation. The witness stopped to take pictures, and then, once home, continued observing with his family until the phenomenon disappeared. The hypothesis of Thai lanterns is entirely consistent with the observation: these objects are inherently very faint (equivalent to a small garden torch) and therefore often appear farther away than they actually are, and thus larger and faster than they really are; the wind, although light, was far from calm. It is common to feel nothing on the ground. Parties on Friday evenings are certainly less frequent than those on Saturdays, but nonetheless common (often professional or community events, for example, and it's also carnival season). The photo from witness Ne1164 is entirely consistent with a photo of Thai lanterns. The southeast wind, at 9 to 28 km/h, is consistent with the observed movement from Guermentes towards Chelles. See the weather report at Roissy. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon in the night sky: certain observation of the star Capella combined with an illusion of movement and a physiological effect of micro-nystagmus.
description: On March 7, 2015, at approximately 1:35 a.m., a driver and his passenger were intrigued by a luminous object moving in the sky. The phenomenon was first noticed while driving on the D37 road. The driver then pulled over onto the hard shoulder, and the observation lasted 3 to 4 minutes. The passenger took a photograph with a camera. No other witness statements were collected. The driver stated at the beginning of the questionnaire that he observed the unidentified flying object (UFO) on his left while driving on a straight stretch of road, and that the UFO began to move (to the right) when he turned (to the left). This well-known phenomenon is a perceptual illusion created by the movement of witnesses observing a stationary, distant object without reference points, particularly at night. The object, in fact, does not move at all but appears to move in response to the vehicle's movements. This is confirmed when the witnesses decide to pull over to the side of the road for a better look. The UFO then "comes to a stop," since the witnesses are no longer moving. Considering the information gathered in the investigation report (attached document), namely: - the shape, color, brightness, and apparent size; - the identical azimuth and altitude; - the confirmed illusion of movement; - the confirmed effect of micro-nystagmus; - the probable disappearance behind clouds, we can conclude that the case involves the confirmed observation of the star Capella, combined with an illusion of movement and a physiological effect of micro-nystagmus. The star disappears, probably obscured by a bank of clouds. This case should be classified as A, as an observation of the star Capella. One might be surprised by the significant discrepancy between the witnesses' account and the trivial explanation given. The key to this misunderstanding lies in the incorrect estimation of the phenomenon's distance: as it appeared to witnesses above the water tower, it was immediately interpreted as an object quite close to the ground; its apparent movement across the horizon was then perceived as an actual movement. Finally, the variations in light intensity, probably due to the invisible cloud cover, were interpreted as movements moving away or towards each other.

summary: Quick observation of the slow and silent movement of 4 pale white lights in the night sky: probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On Saturday, March 7, 2015, at 9:33 PM, a witness observed four pale white lights very quickly in the sky. The phenomenon moved slowly and silently along a straight path before disappearing into a cloud. No other witnesses reported seeing them. The observation of luminous orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a weekend night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. The movement was observed from west to north, which is consistent with the southerly wind recorded in Quimper (see the report from Météociel). The observation was very brief, and the available information imprecise; this case is not very consistent. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of a black, ovoid-shaped object, reflecting the sun's brightness and appearing to move slowly; rapid disappearance: probable observation of a tethered solar balloon.
description: On March 6, 2015, the witness was driving on the D112, near Lavalette (31), on his way to work. Around 8:30 a.m., while driving near Grousset, his attention was drawn to a black, ovoid-shaped object in front of him in a completely clear sky. The object reflected the sunlight and appeared to be moving slowly. The witness described it as appearing to be located approximately above the road and having a small white trail extending horizontally from its base. A slight orange coloration was also present on one edge of the UFO. After observing it for about two minutes, the witness reached for his cell phone, which was on the passenger seat, and was momentarily distracted. When he returned to look at the UFO, it had disappeared. The sighting was made through the car's windshield. After the UFO disappeared, the witness slowed down and tried to find it by looking all around the sky, without success. Only one witness statement was collected. The UFO had the appearance and movement of a solar-powered tethered balloon launched from a field to the witness's right (see the investigation report). The strangeness of the case is essentially caused by the UFO's disappearance while the witness was looking for his phone to take a picture. Had the balloon not disappeared, the witness would have recognized it (and would not have given a statement) and might have looked for and seen its operator on the ground, whereas he probably did not see the operator because he was busy searching for the UFO in the sky while driving. The strangeness was not apparent to drivers following or passing by, who either did not see the balloon or saw it descend and/or land (the witness indicated the presence of other drivers who noticed nothing). The witness's testimony is consistent, with sufficient and usable data provided by the witness. Furthermore, a photograph taken by the witness, reconstructing the scene, was used in the case analysis. This allowed for verification of the UFO's appearance as consistent with that of a balloon, the possibility of operating a balloon from the field, and the possibility of a witness not seeing the balloon operator, especially when the witness is startled by the disappearance and is looking at the sky rather than the ground. The main issue here is explaining the possibility of the balloon's rapid descent over a period of one to a few seconds, bearing in mind that only the descent time to the treetops, which then obscure it, is considered, and that the balloon was not necessarily visible very high above the trees initially. This descent could be explained by the balloon breaking up or being brought down to the ground by a spinnaker effect (due to the wind). Because of the strong resemblance to a balloon and the explanation for its rapid descent, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a tethered solar balloon.

summary: Observation in the sky of a trail with a particular zig-zag shape: observation of an airplane contrail.
description: On March 5, 2015, at 7:13 a.m., a witness at Longueville station was intrigued by the shape of an airplane contrail. As the witness correctly observed, this contrail was rather unusual. GEIPAN submitted the photograph to Météo-France experts: "This is indeed a contrail which, after its formation, was distorted by the turbulence prevailing at the location where it was created. Very turbulent areas can indeed exist in clear skies (this is called "clear-air turbulence"). These areas are dreaded by pilots because they are difficult to predict, are not visible on radar, and are the site of violent phenomena that force crews to change flight levels to ensure passenger comfort. Such a photograph with such pronounced sinuosities is, however, a first for us. This rare case is classified as "A" observation of a contrail from the Airbus A319 of flight AF7614 Marseille-Lille (see Flight Radar map at 7:13 a.m. local time), severely disrupted by atmospheric turbulence. Attachments: Flightradar report, Météociel report at ground, in Melun.

summary: Successive observations of phenomena in the sky: certain observation of an airplane, then probable observation of a reflection on a satellite.
description: On March 5, 2015, two witnesses traveling in a car successively observed several unexplained phenomena in the sky. Only one witness's testimony was recorded. This witness observed three successive phenomena: 1- An elongated object, a black and matte mass, composed of several white lights at different altitudes. A fin was visible. A check of civil air traffic showed an aircraft at low altitude, approaching Lille-Lesquin airport, in the direction of the witness's observation: flight EZY693F, whose yellow-orange tail was clearly noted by the witness (see Flightradar report). This phenomenon was therefore perfectly identified and classified as "A": aircraft sighting. 2- The witness then saw a yellow light quite high in the sky, in a direction close to that of the Moon. An astronautical verification (see Calsky report) indicates that this is the time of year conducive to sunlight reflecting off geostationary satellites, precisely in this direction; however, it is difficult to confirm this hypothesis. This phenomenon is probably identified as a satellite reflection and is classified as "B". 3- His last observation concerns a cigar-shaped object, similar to the first, but without a fin. A check of civil air traffic records shows no low-altitude aircraft in the observed direction. Given the similarity to the first phenomenon, which was an aircraft, the aircraft hypothesis is favored: the fact that it does not appear on civil air traffic records suggests that it may be a military aircraft, and therefore less illuminated than a civilian aircraft. Given the low oddity of the case, GEIPAN did not conduct any searches on military air traffic records.

summary: Observation of two small, thin lines around a luminous disk: observation of a lunar halo (paraselena).
description: On March 4, 2015, at approximately 8:15 PM, a witness observed a large, bright, off-white circle in the sky, roughly the size and brightness of the moon. The object was located above the trees, surrounded by two thin, luminous lines. The object moved slowly, then took on an elongated shape, followed by two red lights and a white light, before disappearing from the witness's view. Only one witness statement was recorded. GEIPAN contacted the witness to clarify certain points: the witness was observing in a northeast direction and had indeed noticed the moon to their right. They also pointed out two small, thin lines around the luminous disk. This description corresponds to the atmospheric optical phenomenon known as a paraselene, located at 22nd and/or 46th arcseconds from the moon, at a similar elevation. This phenomenon is an image of the moon produced by reflection off the ice crystals of high-altitude cold clouds (cirrus). See the Wikipedia article on paraselenes. Today's weather report is available on Météociel. GEIPAN classifies this case as A: lunar halo.

summary: Brief observation of the passage of a sphere and a luminous triangular object: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On March 3, 2015, at 9:30 a.m., a witness observed through a skylight the passage of a translucent sphere and a luminous white triangular object across the sky. Both objects disappeared northward in a straight line. No unusual noise was heard. The observation lasted less than 10 seconds within a limited field of vision. No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. This very brief account, observed through a narrow window, does not allow for an assessment of the phenomenon's trajectory. The translucent sphere could be a balloon carried by the south wind (see the report from Météociel in Melun). The triangle emitting flashes suggests an airplane. The Flightradar website indicates a possible candidate (see attached) within the witness's line of sight, but this airplane flies high and could not have appeared as a triangle; moreover, it flies towards the southeast, while the witness sees the objects moving north. A drone equipped with flashing LEDs could be considered, but verification is impossible without further evidence. The brevity of the observation and the narrow field of view do not allow for a firm opinion on this case of moderate strangeness and weak consistency. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to lack of cross-checking.

summary: Observation of the passage of three long, flat, very luminous shapes at sunset: lack of information on the date of the day.
description: In early March 2015, between 5:00 and 5:30 PM, a witness observed three long, flat, very bright objects passing across the sky from their kitchen window. Two other people also observed the phenomenon. Only one witness statement was recorded. This observation of three brightly lit objects suggests the possibility of airplanes reflecting the setting sun (at low altitude, in grazing light, the wings of airplanes are almost invisible). As the date of this observation is unknown, it is not possible to carry out the necessary verifications. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of date information.

summary: Observation of a red-orange oval mass in the clear sky: probable observation of a cloud at sunset.
description: On February 25, 2015, at 6:10 PM, a witness was driving when they spotted a colored phenomenon high in the sky, heading northwest. An airplane was passing nearby. The sky was very clear. A bright yellow or red oval, observed for five minutes against the light at sunset, suggested a small cloud mass backlit by the setting sun. It could have been water vapor from an airplane contrail, or a cloud. Airplane contrails are described as spindle-shaped or V-shaped. In this case, the presence of a cloud is more likely. Its disappearance within one or two minutes is not very surprising. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of a small cloud at sunset.

summary: Observation of the silent movement in the night sky and emitting 27 orange glows: probable Thai lanterns.
description: On February 22, 2015, at 3:03 a.m., a witness noticed an orange glow moving across the clear sky through a window. The witness eventually counted 27 identical glows coming from the NNE and disappearing eastward "with lightning speed." No noise was heard during the 34-minute observation. No photographs were taken. No other witness statements were collected. One hypothesis was considered (see the investigation notes): observation of the movement of Thai lanterns. The consistent appearance (color, brightness, duration), the number, the day and time, and the identical trajectory of all the objects support this hypothesis. However, the perpetrators of the lecher were not identified. The phase of the phenomena' rapid disappearance eastward corresponds to the extinction phase. As is often the case in these situations, the witness likely interpreted the lantern's rapid dimming as a sign of its rapid movement. Based on the evidence gathered during the investigation, GEIPAN classifies this case as category B: probable observation of Thai lanterns, licked after a private party.

summary: Observation from two different locations in the Haut-Rhin (68) of the movement of several bright points in the sky: very likely observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On February 22, 2015, between 6:45 PM and 6:55 PM, several people in Habsheim (68) and Eschentzwiller (68) observed the movement of luminous points in the sky. The witnesses' accounts and the photos provided clearly suggest the presence of Thae lanterns, which was the only hypothesis considered. The context is rather favorable to lanterns for the following reasons: - the Mulhouse Carnival took place on February 20, 21, and 22; - the Bele Carnival began on February 23 at 4:00 AM with the Morgenstreich (a lantern parade – not flying lanterns!); - throughout Alsace, Germany, and neighboring Switzerland, it is Carnival season (celebrations in most villages, spread over more than a month). - It was still the Chinese New Year period (February 19th). - It was a Sunday, which also leaves open the possibility of another community or private celebration. The location of the witnesses (attached file with various images) suggests that the phenomenon was quite close and therefore at a relatively low altitude. The movement was slow and the wind very light. The gradual and random disappearance of the lights corresponds rather well to lanterns (or variations thereof). The flight in a non-geometric formation also fits. The white color for one of the witnesses and even more so the orange for the other are also consistent, as is the absence of noise (one got out of the car, the other opened the window). Both photos are typical of lantern sightings (with "motion blur" due to low light, hence the slow shutter speed). Aspects unfavorable to the hypothesis: The wind was very light and from the southeast, which is therefore not directly compatible with the statement of the witness from Habsheim (68) who claims to have seen them passing from right to left (i.e., towards nearby Germany). The second witness describes them as being rather stationary, which is not incompatible in itself but not entirely consistent with the presumed wind, which, it should be noted, was very light (3 to 5 km/h) and therefore unstable and subject to local variations. We cannot therefore assert that the objects were indeed flying with the wind, but their very slow movement is not inconsistent with this hypothesis. - No mention found (so far) in the press or on the web. - Only two testimonies regarding a significantly higher potential range (nearby towns + villages + highway). In view of the descriptive and behavioral characteristics as well as the very festive context of the region on that day, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: very probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of orange luminous phenomena across the night sky: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, February 21, 2015, at 11:30 PM, a driver and his passenger were intrigued by several orange luminous phenomena moving silently across the sky over Lille. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party. It is worth noting that this was the first Saturday after the Chinese New Year (February 19), a popular occasion for licking sky lanterns. Because the witness was traveling by car and observed the multiple objects intermittently, their precise trajectory could not be reconstructed and compared with the wind direction (a light easterly wind). See the report Météociel. GEIPAN has not received any other reports of this type of phenomenon in Lille for this evening. Due to the impossibility of verification, and despite the strong resemblance to Thai lanterns, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to lack of information. The witness refutes this hypothesis of Thai lanterns that was presented to him.

summary: Observation in the sky of a fixed white object in the shape of an X: lack of information.
description: On Thursday, February 19, 2015, at approximately 2:30-3:00 PM, a driver observed an object resembling a passenger plane, but larger and seemingly flying much lower. The object was uniformly white and appeared stationary. It suddenly disappeared. This brief observation of a luminous white X-shaped object could have several origins: - an airplane, as the witness believes, but in a highly improbable position, and the object's disappearance remains difficult to explain. There is indeed an air corridor in the direction indicated by the witness, but airplanes typically fly at such a high altitude that the witness would not have seen it as large. GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) processed this observation too late to verify the presence of an airplane in the witness's field of vision. - a small, temporary cloud, made very bright by the sun. - a reflection of a white or reflective object inside the car, temporarily illuminated by the sun depending on the car's orientation. This last hypothesis would explain the immobility and subsequent disappearance of the phenomenon. Unable to validate either of these hypotheses, and lacking corroborating evidence or further investigations, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient information. This case is somewhat unusual because it involves a remote phenomenon whose behavior resembles known phenomena; however, it is not very consistent because it is based on a single, brief, and photographic account.

summary: Observation of the EO passage of a very bright white phenomenon with a red mark in front; sudden extinction in the clear sky: observation of a meteoroid reentry.
description: On February 17th, around 8 PM, a witness in their garden observed the east-west passage of a very bright, white, tube-shaped phenomenon with a red mark at its front. It suddenly disappeared in the clear sky. The observation lasted between 5 and 6 seconds. No other reports were collected. The bright, elongated appearance, as well as the linear and rapid trajectory across the sky, are characteristic of a fireball. The BOAM station in May-sur-Orne recorded a fireball at the same time, with a trajectory seen from the station located in an azimuth quadrant (150° to 160°) where the observation site was situated, and a direction clearly indicating an east-to-west perception. The high-elevation passage (45 to 60 arcseconds) observed on both sides is consistent with a fireball at an altitude of 50 to 100 km traveling from east to west, with the axis connecting the two points separated by 130 km. The witness was at the eastern limit of the station's visibility and was therefore able to begin seeing the fireball earlier and with a greater excursion across the sky (3/4 of the sky according to the witness). The witness most likely saw a meteoroid reentry. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: fireball observation.

summary: Observation of the passage of a bright white point in the sky: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).
description: On February 11, 2015, at approximately 6:40 PM, a witness and their son observed a bright point in the sky moving at a speed greater than that of a commercial airliner. The point then passed over the roof of the building and finally disappeared, fading away. This observation report is typical of a "large" satellite sighting. The Calsky record confirms the passage of the International Space Station (ISS) at precisely that time, according to the diagram provided by the witness (although there is an error in the initial azimuth of the observation, due to a mistake in the form). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: [BOLIDE] (NAT) FRANCE (FR) 10.02.2015. Numerous observations of the passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of a bolide, caused by the entry into the atmosphere of a small body of astronomical origin.
description: On February 10, 2015, numerous witnesses throughout southern France, from the Pyrénées-Atlantiques to the Hérault, observed a very bright luminous sphere crossing a portion of the sky. This phenomenon was also observed in Spain, from the Basque Country to Catalonia. The CNES automatic camera in Toulouse recorded the event at 7:22 PM. GEIPAN received three formal reports (see summary table), while La Dépêche du Midi and the website Ciel des Hommes received more than 80 reports. A 3D reconstruction of the trajectory is underway thanks to other cameras (Pic du Midi, Spain) that recorded the phenomenon. This luminous phenomenon, called a bolide, is produced by the entry into the atmosphere of a large meteoroid (a "rock" weighing over 100g, i.e., a few centimeters to 1 meter in diameter). This phenomenon occurs between 100 and 40 km in altitude due to the heating and ionization of the upper layers of the atmosphere. The color can vary (green, white, yellow) depending on the angle of incidence of the meteoroid; debris may reach the ground, which is then called a meteorite. The high altitude of the phenomenon explains why it has been observed within a radius of over 200 km. Its intense brightness often leads people to mistakenly believe it is a very close phenomenon. It often creates strong illusions of proximity, whereas the phenomenon actually occurs at high altitude (beginning around 100 km and ending around 20 km). The observation time of the phenomenon varied considerably (from 7:15 PM to 7:40 PM), a common occurrence for this type of event, as observed by numerous witnesses. The trajectory and speed of the phenomenon are characteristic of the reentry of a natural meteoroid. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of a bolide, caused by the reentry into the atmosphere of a small body of astronomical origin.

summary: Observation in the sky of a hatched trail with a downward spiral trajectory: probable observation of condensation trails from a military aircraft in maneuver.
description: On February 10, 2015, at 6:00 PM, a motorist observed a white, hatched chemtrail in the sky with a downward spiral trajectory and another object to the right of the trail. GEIPAN (the French Interministerial Group for the Study of Nuclear and Paranormal Activity) requested information from military air traffic control regarding air traffic in the area at that time. It appears that a military aircraft was flying in that area between 6:00 PM and 6:05 PM. However, it was not possible to verify whether the spiral contrails described by the witness corresponded exactly to the military aircraft's trajectory. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of contrails from a military aircraft in maneuver.

summary: Observation of the silent presence of 5 orange balls in the sky. Rapid disappearance on an upward trajectory: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Tuesday, February 10, 2015, at 9:05 PM, a witness observed five orange orbs that appeared to move silently towards him for 5 to 7 minutes, with a lighter halo surrounding them. The orbs then disappeared one after another. The observation of these orange orbs in the sky within a few minutes strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The slight movement was observed coming from the Northeast, with a possible approach, which is consistent with the 15-20 km/h NE wind recorded in Limoges (see the Meteociel report for the day of the observation). It should be noted, however, that lantern releases usually take place on weekends; also note that this particular day falls during school holidays and is conducive to carnival celebrations. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Prolonged observation of a bright colored point in the sky: observation of the star Sirius.
description: On February 9, 2015, between 8 PM and 11 PM, a witness observed a "strange" star, which he described as stationary, red, green, and blue. The prolonged observation (one hour) of a fixed object in the sky, resembling a star, suggests a distant astronomical phenomenon. The witness indicated the directions of Clayrac (azimuth ~165°) or Prayssas (azimuth: 142°). The star Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is visible at an azimuth of 143° and an elevation of 21° on the attached star chart. The appearance described by the witness – changes in color green/red/blue, vertical or horizontal oscillations – is entirely consistent with the artifacts produced by the scintillation caused by the atmosphere (see: a star?) and by a visual perception illusion called the autokinetic illusion (see: the perception of the movement of a point of light in the sky). GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of the star Sirius.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a flickering red glow: probable observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On February 8, 2015, between midnight and 12:20 a.m., a witness glimpsed a bright red glow through their window for barely 10 seconds, moving silently horizontally from right to left. The object suddenly changed direction and then disappeared very quickly. The observation of a red light less than 30 meters away, crossing the witness's field of vision at a constant altitude in less than a minute, on a weekend night, strongly suggests a Thai lantern, carried by the wind, probably licked nearby after a private party. The witness described the movement as "from southwest to southeast." In fact, after checking with the witness, they were looking west-southwest (see photo): the movement from their right to their left was more like north-northwest to south-southeast, which is consistent with the northerly wind recorded at Roissy Airport. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B" probable observation of a Thai lantern, or possibly a luminous balloon. Weather report for the day of the observation: Meteociel in Roissy.

summary: Multiple observations of different phenomena in the sky; presence of a red-orange ball, silent movement of a large black craft; very rapid departure from a very bright point: the witness's vision was very likely disturbed.
description: On February 2, 2015, at 1:00 AM, a witness in his yard observed a reddish-orange sphere in the sky for three minutes. The witness thought he saw an airplane. At 1:40 AM, the witness observed a very large, black object flying very low over the rooftops of neighboring buildings. The object, with all its lights off, was very large. The witness described the front of the object as having a rounded triangular shape with rectangular windows. As the object slowly moved toward the witness, he noticed a large reddish-orange sphere resembling a navigation light beneath its base. The object, moving very slowly, then hovered, emitted a thick fog, and disappeared from the witness's sight, moving backward. No sound was heard. At approximately 1:55 AM, the witness observed a very bright, large white star for one or two minutes. It suddenly moved off at very high speed and disappeared from sight. The witness believes it is the craft seen previously. Only one witness statement was collected, along with a photograph of the observation site. Since this sighting, the witness has observed UFOs in the skies over Perpignan, both day and night. These sky sightings present unusual characteristics, especially since the witness sees the phenomenon repeating itself. Consequently, GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group) requested a local investigator to interview the witness. On the evening of September 30th, despite the very overcast weather during the visit, the witness told the investigator that he saw luminous phenomena in the sky, which the investigator could not see at all. In 25 minutes, the witness described the passage of 31 UFOs as white dots that passed by, hid, and stopped. The witness stated that other people to whom he had tried to show the phenomena also did not see them. The witness reports having synthetic lenses implanted shortly after his February sighting (he was wearing glasses at the time but was almost blind). Since his operation, he has been seeing "armadas," "myriads" of UFOs every night over Perpignan. This case of observation is clearly the consequence of ophthalmic problems, even after his operation, both for the February sighting, before the operation, and for the recurring sightings afterward. The witness seems excessively focused on UFOs, to the point of ruling out the possibility that his sightings are the result of a vision problem. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: witness's vision very likely impaired.

summary: Prolonged observation of a fixed blue light above the clouds: lack of information.
description: On February 1, 2015, at 1:30 a.m., two witnesses observed a fixed blue light above the clouds, facing south, for a very long time. Only one witness statement was recorded. Observing a fixed light for over an hour suggests an astronomical phenomenon. The moon was particularly visible that evening, almost full. The blue color described by the witness suggests moonlight. The weather was unstable with numerous cloud passages, which could randomly create gaps or dense patches. The hypothesis that the moon produced this luminous phenomenon is quite likely, but it is very difficult to confirm this hypothesis without a photograph or other witness statement. Despite the possibility of this hypothesis, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observations of the passage near a house of an oval, grey phenomenon with multicolored lights: probable observation of the passage of a drone illuminated by LEDs.
description: On January 31, 2015, at approximately 5:45 PM, two children in separate rooms of their house observed the same unknown phenomenon through their windows: a gray, oval object with colored lights moving at low altitude near the house. Each child reported their observation to their mother a few seconds apart. A questionnaire was completed for both witnesses by their father. Each child then separately recorded their observation with a drawing. No other witness statements were collected. An investigation was conducted on-site (see the investigation notes document). At present, the observation appears to correspond to a drone seen edge-on (oval and flat shape), equipped with multicolored LEDs, with a likely misjudgment by the witnesses regarding the distance and size of the object. The witness statements are very brief but considered reliable and relatively independent because, although brother and sister, the witnesses were in separate rooms when they observed the object. The observation is rather unusual. Following the testimony of the drone pilot (named H1) interviewed during the neighborhood inquiry on April 25, 2015, it is proposed to classify case B as a highly probable observation of a drone illuminated by LEDs, with witnesses misjudging the distance and dimensions of the object. If the owner had been able to confirm the flight of his drone on January 31, 2015, this case would have been classified as A.

summary: Observation for 2 seconds by a motorist of an intense bluish light covering his entire environment: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On January 30, 2015, around 7:00 PM, a driver traveling on the Bordeaux ring road near the town of Carbon-Blanc (33) was suddenly frightened by a very intense bluish light that "covered his entire field of vision" (see the witness's drawing). No unusual noise was heard. Thinking it might be the light from a flashing blue light, the driver looked in his rearview mirror for a vehicle but saw nothing. No information was given over the radio. The driver continued driving, dazed. No other witness statements were collected about this phenomenon. The sudden and intense flash of light in the sky for two seconds could have two possible causes: a particularly violent lightning strike or a fireball (meteorite impact). Lightning strike records indicate that day there were strikes close to the observation area, but only from 1 p.m. to 2 p.m. (see records Météociel 1 and Météociel 2). Over Bordeaux-Merignac, overcast skies and a light westerly wind of 4 to 15 km/h, not exactly consistent with the witness's account (rain and strong wind), are indicated by the Météociel report. The witness's account would seem to support the first hypothesis, but it is not confirmed by the weather records; however, it remains possible. No fireballs were recorded by automatic cameras that day, but cloud cover was almost total over France at that time. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information to validate either hypothesis.

summary: Observation of an orange ball in the sky then disappearance: certain observation of the planet Venus at sunset.
description: On January 26, 2015, at 6:55 PM, a witness observed an orange sphere in the sky, much brighter than Venus and twice its size. When the witness, intrigued, tried to take a picture 10 minutes later, the phenomenon had disappeared. The witness observed a celestial body below the Moon, which he took to be Venus (see his very clear diagram on page 9 of his questionnaire), and in line with it, another large, much brighter and redder point, which seemed strange to him. The star chart shows us that the celestial body located slightly below the Moon is not Venus but Mars (magnitude 1.36, that is to say, slightly brighter than the stars of Ursa Major). Lower down, on the same axis, we find Venus, magnitude 3.34 that day, that is to say, about four times brighter; as Venus was setting, it appeared redder, like all celestial bodies in this position: 15 minutes later, Venus, having set, would have become invisible. GEIPAN classifies this very well documented case in category A: certain observation of the planet Venus at its setting.

summary: Long observation of white lights in the sky: observation of Venus and Mercury at their setting.
description: On January 14, 2015, at 6:25 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky, consisting of several white lights, without any trails or halos. No sound accompanied the phenomenon. Only one witness report was recorded. This observation, lasting several minutes, of two luminous points low on the horizon suggested celestial bodies nearing their setting point: the star chart shows that in the west-southwest direction, that is, the direction of the Dune du Pilat, south of Arcachon, the planets Venus and Mercury, rarely so close and so bright, were clearly visible 8 arcseconds above the horizon (see the star chart in Stellarium). The photograph shows a view taken approximately 45 arcseconds south of the axis of the Allée du Plaeot, which is oriented west. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of Venus and Mercury at their setting point. Since the direction of observation indicated by the witness is not very precise, this hypothesis is not supported.

summary: Long observation in the morning sky of a luminous white and oblong object: observation of an airplane and its condensation trail.
description: On May 13, 2015, at 8:40 a.m., a motorist on the Paris ring road was intrigued by the presence of an oblong, luminous, white object in the sky. Through the windshield, he took three photographs. The UFO appeared stationary and then barely moved. The witness lost sight of it upon exiting the ring road. Only one witness statement was collected. The strangeness of this case is minimal: it is primarily due to the perception of the UFO's immobility. The witness statement is fairly consistent, with sufficient usable data provided by the witness. Several photographs of the UFO were taken and were used for analysis (see the investigation report). The UFO's appearance and its slow, even motionless, movement, as noted by the witness, are typical of airliners and their contrails observed at altitude when they are already illuminated by the rising or setting sun, not yet visible from the ground. The three photographs were taken by the witness at 08:42:37, 08:42:48, and 08:42:54, precisely at sunrise. Depending on local weather conditions at the aircraft's altitude, a contrail may or may not form. If present, it may not be immediately apparent to the witness due to a combination of distance and perspective. The witness may then perceive the contrail as a single object, the aircraft itself potentially not being visible. This contrail can dissipate rapidly behind the aircraft in some areas and take longer in others along the same trajectory, which explains the observation period of over 10 minutes (not the duration of the aircraft itself, but that of a more persistent section of the contrail). This case is to be classified as Ae as an observation of an aircraft and its condensation trail.

summary: Short-range observation of the silent movement of an anthracite grey oval mass with lights: case class D1: unexplained phenomenon of medium strangeness.
description: On Monday, January 12, 2015, at 7:00 a.m., a witness was intrigued by a diffuse light he saw through a glass door of his home. Stepping out onto his terrace, he found himself a few meters from a UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) silently approaching him. A non-blinding white light was positioned at the front of the UFO. The UFO was moving slowly between closely spaced mobile homes. The witness went around his home and found himself facing the right side of the UFO, on which a yellow and red "logo" was visible. The witness "lost track of time" as the UFO continued its trajectory toward the north-northeast, banked, then gained speed and altitude before disappearing above the trees. The witness then noted the oval shape of the UFO. No other witness statements were collected. The observation is strange because it is a phenomenon with a rather unusual appearance at a very early hour of the night and in a very isolated location (see the investigation report). Its characteristics in terms of speed, size, and shape are not particularly extraordinary; from this perspective, it could be an inflatable advertising balloon. However, its trajectory, which was quite fortunate as it narrowly avoided obstacles, is astonishing. It would have had to escape its owner, and above all, what would it be doing so far from any advertising context? It is not possible to validate such a hypothesis. The consistency of the testimony is good, although it comes from only one witness. This single testimony and the absence of photographs place the level of consistency at just the minimum required to validate the strange and unexplained nature of the observation. The case has been submitted to the GEIPAN panel of experts. GEIPAN classifies this case as D1: unexplained phenomenon of medium strangeness.

summary: Observation of two bright points at low altitude: probable observation of low-altitude aircraft.
description: On January 10, 2015, at 6:08 PM, a motorist was intrigued by two very bright points of light quite low in the sky. He took a photo. No other reports were collected. This sighting of two bright points separated by a dark mass suggests an aircraft at medium or low altitude: the Flight Radar record (e 17:01 UTC) indicates that the Nantes-Lyon flight was flying over Communay at an altitude of less than 2,500 meters (see screenshot). The changes in direction observed by the witness could also be due to the sighting of another aircraft, given the relatively heavy air traffic in that area, even at medium and low altitudes. For example, an hour later, three HOP! aircraft were observed flying in succession, a few minutes apart, on a northwest-to-southeast trajectory at less than 2,500 meters in the same location. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a probable sighting of aircraft at low altitude.

summary: Observation of 5 bright points in the cloudy sky with 3 points perfectly aligned and the other two completing the set to form a diamond: certain observation of the constellation of Orion between clouds.
description: On January 8, 2015, at approximately 7:35 PM, a witness, sitting in his vehicle, observed five bright points in the sky for one minute through a break in the clouds: three points perfectly aligned, the other two completing the set to form a diamond shape. The witness himself discovered the explanation for his observation a few days later, upon seeing the same phenomenon in the same direction under a clear sky: the three aligned bright points were the "belt" of the constellation Orion (see astronomical chart). It was the sight of these stars isolated amidst the clouds, without their stellar context, that temporarily gave them their unusual appearance. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": confirmed observation of the constellation Orion between clouds.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a bright white-blue-green point, followed by a trail: observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On January 5, 2015, at 7:41 PM, a witness observed a unique phenomenon: a very bright white, blue, and green light with a trail. As the witness suspected, this observation of a bright white-blue-green point of light, followed by a trail, rapidly traversing a portion of the sky in a few seconds, had all the characteristics of a bolide, that is, the phenomenon produced in the upper atmosphere by the impact of a meteorite. The REFORME network confirmed this hypothesis (see attached document). GEIPAN classified this case as "A": observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Observations of three fixed orange-yellow light points that went out successively: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 4, 2015, at 7:20 PM, a witness and his wife observed three fixed points of light from their car for five minutes. The three points then went out successively. The observation of orange-yellow orbs in the sky for a few minutes, going out one after the other, on a weekend night, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby during the New Year's celebrations. The orbs appeared motionless, which is consistent with the very light south wind (2 to 4 km/h) recorded by the weather service in Saint-Brieuc (22). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thames lanterns. GEIPAN has not received any other reports related to this observation to date.

summary: Observation from an airplane of a luminous phenomenon on the ground moving at the same speed as the airplane: very likely observation of reflections of the Moon on bodies of water and flooded areas.
description: On January 4, 2015, at 7:45 PM, a witness, a passenger on a scheduled flight, observed a luminous phenomenon moving along the ground at the same speed as the aircraft. Other passengers, when asked, also observed the phenomenon. At the time of the observation, the aircraft was just before the outskirts of Paris. The witness specified over the phone that the phenomenon was located to the left of the aircraft, at an angle estimated between 50° and 70° relative to the aircraft's vertical. Relative to the aircraft, the phenomenon was sometimes positioned in front of and sometimes behind it, occasionally forcing the witness to turn their head backward. It was noted that the Moon, 99.6% full, was located due east at 90.8° with an elevation of 23.26°: it was within the witness's field of vision. However, the witness did not mention it, probably because their gaze was focused on the ground. Since the phenomenon seems to follow the aircraft, the hypothesis of an optical phenomenon involving a celestial body is immediately favored. The reflection (called specular) of the Moon on the lakes and flooded areas is very likely the origin of the phenomenon, highlighting the wet or flooded areas against the black ground. The filaments described by the witness are probably flooded paths or small canals. Weather reports indicate rain in the northern half of France on February 2nd and 3rd. It is noted that the angle of 50° to 70° indicated by the witness is consistent with this hypothesis: ideally, it should be the complement of 23°, that is, 67°. The forward/rear variation of the phenomenon stems from the change in the aircraft's heading: the phenomenon always appears due east. If the aircraft is flying due south, the witness sees it exactly to the left of the aircraft; if the aircraft is flying southeast, the phenomenon appears to the front left of the aircraft. GEIPAN does not have the necessary information to precisely correlate the aircraft's route with the apparent position of the phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": highly probable observation of moon reflections on bodies of water and flooded areas.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of about ten luminous balls in the sky: lack of information.
description: On January 2, 2015, at 1:30 a.m., a witness was stargazing from his window. He suddenly saw a disorganized group of about ten luminous orbs silently flying over the city. The observation lasted 15 seconds before the objects were hidden by the rooftops and the horizon. Only one witness account was recorded. The witness, contacted by telephone, finally indicated that his window faced southwest. The astronomical chart confirmed that Orion was indeed in the southwest (and not in the west as the witness indicated), and the Moon in the west-southwest; the cardinal directions therefore needed adjusting: the witness saw the objects move towards the south-southeast. The weather report from Météociel in Troyes indicates a light southeasterly wind measured at ground level, which is seemingly incompatible with the objects moving south-southeast, assuming they were carried by the wind. The observation of yellow balls crossing the sky in one minute, on a holiday weekend night, strongly suggests Thai lanterns, probably licked nearby after a private party; the witness's description perfectly matches these objects, which are very frequently launched on all sorts of occasions, but the behavior of these objects and their direction of movement do not correspond well with the wind recorded in Troyes. A weather assessment by Météo-France indicated that the wind at altitude was from the southwest, meaning perpendicular to the wind at ground level: this could explain the turbulent movements, but not the south-southeastward movement. The hypothesis of Thai lanterns released for the holidays cannot be confirmed. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of corroborating evidence: photos, videos, or other eyewitness accounts.

summary: Observation of the silent movement in the sky of about twenty luminous balls: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On January 1, 2015, at 4:25 a.m., witnesses observed about twenty colored, luminous orbs moving silently across the sky. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes on a festive night strongly suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party, as is often the case on New Year's Eve. The movement was observed from north to south, consistent with the northerly wind recorded by Météociel Orange. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," indicating a very probable observation of Thai lanterns. The videos taken by the witness leave no doubt about this hypothesis. The first reported sighting could also correspond to a festive object carried by the wind, but of a less common type than classic Thae lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent evolutions of 5 luminous spheres of bright red and orange color in the night sky: lack of information.
description: On January 1, 2015, around 1:00 AM, several members of the same family were intrigued by the movements of five luminous spheres in the clear sky. One was bright red, the others bright orange. No sound was heard during their movement. The objects changed position, rising and falling before disappearing one after another in the direction of the east. Only one witness account was recorded. The observation of orange orbs crossing the sky in a few minutes, on a night of a major celebration, strongly suggests the presence of Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The movement is observed from southwest to east, which does not correspond well with the light southerly wind recorded in Auch, 30 km away (see the Météociel report for the day of the observation in Auch). The phenomenon also exhibits rather atypical behavior, with a highly variable altitude, perhaps related to the extreme cold of that night (-4°C). Due to uncertainty regarding the local wind and the absence of photos or other witnesses, GEIPAN classifies this case as C, due to a lack of meteorological information and corroboration.
